| ---- | -------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | Kbd is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element | Role                                                            | Accessible name from              | States announced |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a `<kbd>`, which has no ARIA role and is read as its text | Its text, the caller's `children` | none             |

A screen reader reads the key's text in the sentence around it, as written: "Esc", "plus", "minus", "up arrow" for "Esc", "+", "−", "↑". Kbd adds no `aria-label` and no owned word for the key: the caller's text is already the key's name, and a `<kbd>` without a role can't carry `aria-label` reliably.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the box only says "this is a key"; the key itself is the text inside it, which a screen reader reads in place, and `children` is required.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the key is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: no owned strings, so no `*Label` props.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders as a string, an element and a list alike, on one line inside the box; `Kbd.test.tsx` checks all three, each inside the one `<kbd>` with `pn-Kbd` first.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the key has no motion.
- [ ] Native semantics first: the native `<kbd>`, with no ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: never focused; it has no tab stop.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Kbd is never pressed. A pressable key hint is the caller's button with the Kbd inside it, which meets the minimum itself.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the key has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: the key's name is the caller's `children`, and Kbd announces nothing else.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root is the native `<kbd>`, rendered through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'kbd'`, with `pn-Kbd` first in its `className` and the caller's after. It sets no role and no ARIA attribute, and no data attribute, since it has no `variant`, `color` or `size` prop.
- **CR-2.** The key is never interactive: no hover, focus, pressed or selected look, no tab stop, no role. A key hint the rider can press is a Perron button with the Kbd inside it.
- **CR-3.** The key sits on the line of the text around it and never breaks it: `display: inline-block`, `vertical-align: baseline`, so its text shares the sentence's baseline; `white-space: nowrap`, so it never wraps or truncates; `text-align: center`, so its text centres in its box. `margin-block: calc(-1 * border.width.025)`, so the border paints outside the line's layout and only the key's 1lh of `typography.data-sm` at `font.line-height.tight` counts toward the line. In `typography.body` and `typography.caption` text it is shorter than the line, by enough that the keys of two wrapped lines stand apart, so the lines around it keep their spacing and two keys never touch.
- **CR-4.** The CSS reads only the component layer's [token families](README.md#token-families), with no `opacity`, no `text-transform` and no `[data-theme]` selector: the key shows its text as the caller wrote it, "Esc" and not "ESC", in both themes through the semantic tokens.
- **CR-5.** One Kbd holds one key: a combination is written as one Kbd per key with the "+" between them in the caller's text, with no `keys` prop, no separator and no nested `<kbd>`. Mylder's keys are single, "+", "−", the arrows and Esc, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) lists them; a separator Kbd drew itself would be an owned string with nothing to say in four languages; and the caller writing `<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>` reads to a screen reader as the sentence says it.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw. Kbd has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `SingleCharacter` and `InHelpText` are the same variant with other text, and prove CR-3. Each `play` test reads the DOM and the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

| Story             | Shows                                                                                                                                                                | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`         | The key "Esc"; the contract story renders it as the subject, and its args pass every rule alone                                                                      | The root is a `<kbd>` with `pn-Kbd`, no role, no ARIA attribute and no `data-*`; its accessible text is "Esc"; it has no `tabindex`, and nothing in it takes focus                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SingleCharacter` | The key "+"                                                                                                                                                          | The root is at least as wide as it is tall, and its text is "+"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `InHelpText`      | A Text in `variant='caption'` reading "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels.", with "+", "−" and "Esc" each a Kbd, in a column narrow enough to wrap it | The paragraph's accessible text is the whole sentence, in order; each Kbd's height is no more than the paragraph's computed line height; a Kbd on a wrapped line stands apart from a Kbd on the line above by more than both their borders; the paragraph is no taller than a copy of it in the same column with each Kbd swapped for an inline-block stand-in of the same text and width, so both wrap at the same words; each Kbd's text stays on one line; no Kbd overflows the column |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                         | Don't                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Name keys in help text, one Kbd per key, as content design writes it: "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels." | Write a key as a quoted word, "press 'Esc'", where a Kbd says it is a key                                                                        |
| Write the key as the keyboard prints it or the platform names it, in its own case: "Esc", "Enter", "−", "↑"                | Write it in capitals ("ESC"), as an emoji, or as an icon; the key's text is what a screen reader hears                                           |
| Name the left and right arrows in words, or all four as "arrows", as content design writes it: "arrows pan"                | Put "←" or "→" in a Kbd; the font Perron ships has no glyph for them, so they fall back to the system's monospace and look unlike the other keys |
| Give a combination one Kbd per key, with "+" between them in the text: `<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>`                    | Put a whole combination or a sentence in one Kbd; the box is sized for one key                                                                   |
| Mark the control a key works with `aria-keyshortcuts`, and keep the action reachable by pressing the control too           | Make the Kbd the only way to learn or do the action, or add `onClick` or `tabIndex` to it                                                        |
| Show key hints where people have a keyboard, such as the help on a desktop screen                                          | Show keys on a phone's screen, which has no keyboard to press them on                                                                            |

title: Stat
markdown:
# Stat

A key figure with the words that say what it counts, such as "412" under "Reporting live", set large so it reads at a glance in a report, a panel or on the kiosk.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md) and the tokens. Stat has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`, and the extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Stat`. Family: none, since it is static content that sits on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden, which says an unknown figure in words (CR-4).

The drawing will have a `root` board holding two layers, `label` and `value`, and no variant property, so its one variant is `Default` ([CR-1](#component-rules) and [Props](#props)). There is no `State` property: Stat is not interactive and has only its rest state.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                     | Base UI part                          | Class           | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` stacking the label over the figure in a column                                                                                                                         | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-Stat`       | none            |
| `label`             | A `div` holding the caller's `label`: what the figure counts, such as "Reporting live"                                                                                         | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-Stat-label` | `label`         |
| `value`             | A `div` holding the caller's `children`: the figure, such as "412" or "4 min". With no figure it holds "—", hidden from screen readers, and the words "Unknown" for them alone | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-Stat-value` | `value`         |

No part has a Base UI component, because none has behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. Each part renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, so the root takes `render` and each inner part takes one through its `slotProps` key, as EmptyState's parts do.

The label sits above the figure, first in the DOM and on screen, so a screen reader hears "Reporting live, 412" in the order the eye reads it: reading the name before the number tells the ear what the number is before it hears it, the visual order matches the reading order the contract asks for, and it is how a key-figure tile reads in most systems (Chakra's `Stat.Label` over `Stat.ValueText`).

The root and both parts are plain `div`s, with no `dl`, `dt` and `dd` and no `role="group"`: a single name and figure is not a list of terms (FactList is the component for those), a `dt` or `dd` outside a `dl` is invalid, and a group role adds "group" to every figure read. A caller showing several Stats as a list makes each an `li` through `render`.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: `baseUiParts` stays empty in `packages/perron/components.json`. Each part renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render` and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part          | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                              | Passed through                                                        |
| --------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` for root  | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, `ref`, the class `pn-Stat`, `data-unknown` when the figure is unknown (CR-3), and the parts below as children                                                   | `render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props |
| `useRender` for label | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-Stat-label`, `label` as children                                                                                                                  | `slotProps.label`                                                     |
| `useRender` for value | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-Stat-value`, `data-unknown` when the figure is unknown (CR-3), `children` as children, or the "—" and its words when the figure is unknown (CR-4) | `slotProps.value`                                                     |

Base UI already does: swapping each part's element through `render` while keeping its class and props, joining `className` strings and `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`, and setting `ref` on the rendered element.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name              | Type                              | Default      | Base UI prop          | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`           | `ReactNode`                       |              | none                  | What the figure counts, in a few words: "Reporting live", "Average delay". Required                                                                                                       |
| `children`        | `ReactNode`                       |              | none                  | The figure, formatted as content design writes numbers: "412", "4 min", "≈ 30". Leave it out when no data says it, and Stat shows "—" and says "Unknown"                                  |
| `render`          | Base UI's `render`                |              | inherited             | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `unknownLabel`    | `string`                          | The locale's | none                  | Overrides "Unknown", heard in place of "—" when there is no figure                                                                                                                        |
| `className`       | `string`                          |              | none                  | Joined after `pn-Stat` on the root                                                                                                                                                        |
| `style`           | `CSSProperties`                   |              | none                  | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ref`             | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`             |              | none                  | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slotProps.label` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |              | `useRender` for label | Props for the `label` part                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slotProps.value` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |              | `useRender` for value | Props for the `value` part                                                                                                                                                                |

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, as the contract's Root section says; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `StatProps` does not declare it again.

The figure is the `children` and its name is a required `label` prop, not a `value` prop: the contract's `value` belongs to controls with `defaultValue` and `onChange`, as Delay's spec reasons, the figure is the content the caller writes, and `<Stat label="Reporting live">412</Stat>` reads as the screen shows it. `label` is a name the contract's Names from other libraries table leaves free, and it is a `ReactNode`, not an owned-string override, since it has no `Label` suffix after a key.

Stat ships with no `color`, `variant` or `size`, one look everywhere: a status colour on a figure would say "good" or "bad" by colour alone, which [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) rules out, and the live-share thresholds the status colours carry belong to a meter's mark, not to text; one size is `typography.stat`, the role made for key figures. Any of the three can join later as an optional prop without a break.

Stat leaves number formatting to the caller, taking the figure as already-written text rather than a number it formats with the locale: the figures Mylder shows mix units ("4 min"), estimates ("≈ 30") and percentages, which one `Intl.NumberFormat` call can't cover, and the caller already formats them in the screen's locale. A bare number still renders as given (CR-2).

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Stat has no interactive state, so every row is rest; the unknown figure is rest with `data-unknown` on the value.

| Part    | State                | Property               | Token                                                                  |
| ------- | -------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`  | rest                 | `gap`                  | `space.100`                                                            |
| `label` | rest                 | `font`                 | `typography.label-sm`                                                  |
| `label` | rest                 | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.label-sm`, its tracking                                    |
| `label` | rest                 | `color`                | `color.text.secondary`                                                 |
| `value` | rest                 | `font`                 | `typography.stat`                                                      |
| `value` | rest                 | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.stat`, its tracking                                        |
| `value` | rest                 | `color`                | `color.text.primary`                                                   |
| `value` | rest                 | `font-variant-numeric` | none: the keyword `tabular-nums`, so a changing figure keeps its width |
| `value` | rest                 | `white-space`          | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "4 min" never breaks from its unit      |
| `value` | rest, `data-unknown` | `color`                | `color.text.tertiary`                                                  |

The root is a flex column with `align-items: start` and the keyword `width: fit-content`, not a token, so it sizes to its content and a Stat made a link through `render` is no wider than its words (CR-10); every part and the root reset the margins their element may bring. `typography.label-sm`'s own use is "field and stat labels", and `typography.stat`'s is "key figures".

The root is a start-aligned flex column with `space.100` (4 px) between the label and the figure, and no fill, border, radius, padding or shadow of its own: Stat is content that takes the surface of the report, panel or kiosk bar it sits in, like EmptyState, and a box of its own would join no family. 4 px sets the small label close to the figure it names, as EmptyState spaces its title and sentence.

The figure uses tabular figures and never wraps, while the label wraps: tabular figures keep a figure that updates from shifting its width, and keep Stats side by side aligned, as the typography foundation asks for anything compared; a key figure is short, and a break inside "1 204" or between "4" and "min" would misread it, while a long Danish label must still fit 320 px.

[Typography](../foundations/typography.md#roles) steps `stat` down to `font.size.600` on phones, but the contract gives components no viewport query. Stat keeps `typography.stat` at every width, as Text does: the step-down is a token gap for the `design-tokens` skill, a phone modifier that redefines the composite on `:root`, so Stat, Text and the `perron-typography-stat` class step down together when it lands.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Stat has no keys of its own and is never focusable. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys.

| Key  | Does                              | From   |
| ---- | --------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | Stat is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element                            | Role                         | Accessible name from                                    | States announced |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`                             | None (generic `div`)         | Not named; its text is read in place, label then figure | None             |
| `label`                            | None (generic `div`)         | Its text, from `label`                                  | None             |
| `value`                            | None (generic `div`)         | Its text, from `children`                               | None             |
| The "—" in `value`, when unknown   | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"` | Not read                                                | None             |
| The words in `value`, when unknown | Text, in VisuallyHidden      | The owned string "Unknown", or `unknownLabel`           | None             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the label and the figure are read as shown, label first; "—" is `aria-hidden` and the ear hears "Unknown" in its place (CR-4). No colour carries meaning: the figure is `color.text.primary`, and tertiary only for the "—" the words speak for.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is not a landmark or region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `unknownLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `label` and `children` are `ReactNode`s; a string, a number, an element and a list each render, `0` is a figure and not unknown (CR-3), and `Stat.test.tsx` renders each shape. The `Default` story gives a string label and a string figure.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses. The "—" is `aria-hidden` because the words speak for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: plain `div`s, with no role and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` on the "—"; the caller's own element through `render`, such as an `li`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Stat takes no focus and opens nothing.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Stat is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Stat has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word Stat shows comes from the caller, through `label` and `children`, but for the one it announces when there is no figure.

| Key       | English   | Override       | Seen or heard where                                                             |
| --------- | --------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unknown` | "Unknown" | `unknownLabel` | `value`, heard in place of the `aria-hidden` "—" when there is no figure (CR-4) |

No key in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` says it: `delayUnknown`, "Delay unknown", names a delay, so `unknown` is new, with a JSDoc line like its neighbours.

The new key is `unknown`, English "Unknown", with Danish "Ukendt", Swedish "Okänd" and Norwegian Bokmål "Ukjent": after the label it reads "Reporting live, Unknown", says no more than the data knows, as content design asks, and matches the "unknown" in "Delay unknown" in each language.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Stat has one look: no `color`, `variant` or `size` prop and no `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size` attribute, as [Props](#props) sets out.
- **CR-2.** Stat doesn't format the figure: `children` renders as given, a number as React writes it, as [Props](#props) sets out.
- **CR-3.** The figure is unknown when `children` renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) or is a number that is not finite (`NaN`, `Infinity`). `0` and `'0'` are figures. When unknown, the root and the value part both carry the bare attribute `data-unknown`: the CSS reads the "—" colour from the value's, as `.pn-Stat-value[data-unknown]`, one class then an attribute, so a caller restyles it with a class of its own through `slotProps.value.className`, selected with `[data-unknown]` as Stat's is; the root's tells the caller the figure is unknown.
- **CR-4.** Stat shows an unknown figure itself, as "—" in `color.text.tertiary` with `aria-hidden="true"`, followed by the owned string "Unknown" in the VisuallyHidden shared part: content design writes "—" for unknown and the brand never shows a guess, while a screen reader skips or spells a bare "—", so the ear would get less than the eye; Delay does the same for an unknown delay. Tertiary is allowed because the "—" always sits under the stronger label.
- **CR-5.** The "—" is the character U+2014 in its own `span`, and the words are their own text run, so `expectOwnedStrings` reads them as a dictionary value.
- **CR-6.** Stat composes the VisuallyHidden shared part from `packages/perron/src/parts/VisuallyHidden/` and never draws its own hiding styles.
- **CR-7.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `render` swaps the element.
- **CR-8.** `label`, `children`, `unknownLabel`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so none reaches the DOM as an attribute.
- **CR-9.** Stat is not a live region and never moves focus. A screen that updates its figures announces changes of state in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) asks.
- **CR-10.** Stat sizes to its content, with no width of its own; the label wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) and the figure does not (see [Tokens](#tokens)).

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw. It has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `Unknown` is the same variant with no figure, and proves CR-3 and CR-4. The contract story renders `Default`.

| Story     | Shows                                                                                                             | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Default` | `label` "Reporting live" over the figure "412"; the contract story renders it, and its args pass every rule alone | The label comes before the figure in the accessible text; neither the root nor the value has `data-unknown`; the figure's computed `font-variant-numeric` is `tabular-nums`; nothing in it takes focus |
| `Unknown` | `label` "Reporting live" with no `children`: "—" under it                                                         | The root and the value carry `data-unknown`; "—" is `aria-hidden`; the accessible text is "Reporting live" then "Unknown"                                                                              |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                   | Don't                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Leave out `children` when no data gives the figure, so Stat shows "—" and says "Unknown"                             | Pass `0` or a guess when the figure is unknown: the brand never claims more than the data knows                                |
| Write the figure as content design does: "4 min" with a space, "≈ 30" for an estimate, "−1" with the true minus sign | Put the label's words inside the figure, such as "412 live": the figure stays short, and the label says what it counts         |
| Name the figure in a few words in `label`: "Reporting live", "Average delay"                                         | Leave `label` empty and rely on the layout to say what the number is: a figure without its name tells the ear nothing          |
| Say a status in words beside the figure, or show it with a Meter or a SeverityLabel                                  | Colour the figure through `className` to say it is good or bad: colour alone tells no screen reader and no colour-blind person |
| Use Delay for one vehicle's or departure's delay, and Text with `variant='stat'` for a figure inside a sentence      | Use Stat in a row of a list or table: it is set large for a key figure, and rows compare figures in a `data` role              |
| Announce a changed figure in the screen's own polite live region, when it changes state                              | Make a Stat a live region: a figure that updates every few seconds floods the screen reader                                    |

# Tag

A short word or two on a pill that marks a property of what it sits beside, such as "Night bus", "Replacement bus" or "Cancelled" on a departure or a vehicle, set in capitals in one of the intents' colours.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Tag`, not drawn yet: the design is deferred (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

Tag is a label with no behaviour: the registry gives it no `baseUiParts`, and the chips people press, FilterChip and HighlightChip, are components of their own on Base UI's Toggle. Its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop.

The drawing has a `root` board holding one text layer, `label`. Its variant properties are `variant` and `color`, in that order, with the values the [Props](#props) table gives, so its variants are `FilledNeutral`, `FilledSuccess`, `FilledWarning`, `FilledDanger`, `FilledInfo`, `DashedNeutral`, `DashedSuccess`, `DashedWarning`, `DashedDanger` and `DashedInfo`. There is no `State` property: Tag is not interactive and has only its rest state.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                | Base UI part                                  | Class    | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The pill: an inline box with a `radius.full` edge, filled with the intent's tinted surface or edged with a dashed line, holding the words                                                                 | none: a `<span>` rendered through `useRender` | `pn-Tag` | none            |
| `label`             | The words, from the caller's `children`, set in `typography.overline`'s capitals. The `label` layer is the root's own text, with no element, class or `slotProps` key of its own, as LineBadge's label is | none: the root's text                         | none     | none            |

## Base UI parts

Tag imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props with its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                                           | Passed through                                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`; `ref`; `props`: `mergeProps(rest, own)`, where `own` is `className: 'pn-Tag'`, `data-variant`, `data-color` | `render`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style` and every other `<span>` attribute |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class, the data attributes and the children; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and joining `className` and `style` and chaining event handlers through `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: Tag has no inner part. No owned strings, so no `*Label` props.

Tag takes `variant`, `'filled' | 'dashed'`, default `'filled'`. `filled` lays the intent's tinted surface under its text, for a property that holds, such as "Night bus"; `dashed` has no fill and a dashed `color.border.strong` edge, the "dashed tags" that token's description names, for something announced but not yet confirmed by live data, such as a planned replacement bus. The spellings are MUI Chip's `filled` and the token's own word for the edge; no family's spelling binds Tag, since it joins none.

`color` offers `'neutral' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info'`, default `'neutral'`, each with its `color.text.*` and `color.surface.*` tokens, and no `brand`: the brand yellow is kept for a screen's one main action, and a yellow pill beside it would read as a second one.

Tag comes in one size, with no `size` prop: `typography.overline` with `space.050` above and below and `space.200` at the sides, about 20 px tall with its hairline edge, so a tag fits beside a `size.badge` LineBadge in a row without making the row taller. A `size` can join later without a break.

Tag takes no `startIcon`: its words say everything it marks, and SeverityLabel is the label that comes with an icon. A `startIcon` can join later without a break.

`children` is required: a pill with no words says nothing, and its colour is never the only sign of what it marks.

| Name        | Type                                                        | Default     | Base UI prop        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `'filled' \| 'dashed'`                                      | `'filled'`  | none                | How sure the tag is: `filled` lays the intent's tinted surface under the words, for a property that holds; `dashed` has no fill and a dashed edge, for something announced but not yet confirmed by live data. Set on the root as `data-variant`.                                    |
| `color`     | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'neutral'` | none                | The intent: what the colour means. `neutral` for a plain property, such as "Night bus"; the status intents for good news, a warning, a problem or information, always in words that say it too, such as "Cancelled": colour is never the only sign. Set on the root as `data-color`. |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                 | (required)  | none                | The words: one or two, and on a `dashed` tag a word more that says it is not confirmed, such as "Replacement bus planned"; written in sentence case, which the tag sets in capitals. A string, an element such as `<time>`, or a list of both.                                       |
| `render`    | Base UI's `render`                                          |             | inherited           | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                                            |
| `className` | `string`                                                    |             | none                | Joined after `pn-Tag` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`                                             |             | none                | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ref`       | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>`                                      |             | `useRender`'s `ref` | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## Tokens

Tag is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row names the `data-variant` and `data-color` it applies to. It belongs to no family, so it takes the pill's `radius.full`, which that token's description gives to "chips, tags, counts", and the role `typography.overline`, whose description is "Section headings and tags, set in capitals".

| Part   | State                                       | Property          | Token                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `display`         | none: the keyword `inline-block`, so the tag sits on the line of the text around it                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `box-sizing`      | none: the keyword `border-box`, so the padding and the edge count inside `max-inline-size` (CR-6)                                                                                     |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `max-inline-size` | none: `100%`, so the tag never runs past its container (CR-6)                                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `padding-block`   | `space.050`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `padding-inline`  | `space.200`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `border-radius`   | `radius.full`                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `border-width`    | `border.width.025`                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `font`            | `typography.overline`                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `letter-spacing`  | `typography.overline-tracking`                                                                                                                                                        |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `text-transform`  | none: the keyword `uppercase`, as the `perron-typography-overline` class sets it                                                                                                      |
| `root` | rest, every variant                         | `overflow-wrap`   | none: the keyword `break-word`, so a tag alone in a narrow container breaks a word longer than the line within it, while in a flex row its narrowest width is its longest word (CR-6) |

| `root` | rest, `data-variant='filled'`               | `border-color`    | none: the keyword `transparent`, which Windows' contrast themes paint in the text colour, so the pill keeps its shape (CR-4)                                                          |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='filled'`, `neutral`    | `background`      | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='filled'`, `success`    | `background`      | `color.surface.success`                                                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='filled'`, `warning`    | `background`      | `color.surface.warning`                                                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='filled'`, `danger`     | `background`      | `color.surface.danger`                                                                                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='filled'`, `info`       | `background`      | `color.surface.info`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='dashed'`               | `background`      | none: the keyword `transparent`                                                                                                                                                       |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='dashed'`               | `border-style`    | none: the keyword `dashed`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `data-variant='dashed'`               | `border-color`    | `color.border.strong`, a line that decorates: the words, not the edge, say what the tag marks                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, every variant, `data-color='neutral'` | `color`           | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, every variant, `data-color='success'` | `color`           | `color.text.success`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, every variant, `data-color='warning'` | `color`           | `color.text.warning`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, every variant, `data-color='danger'`  | `color`           | `color.text.danger`                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest, every variant, `data-color='info'`    | `color`           | `color.text.info`                                                                                                                                                                     |

Every `color.text.*` intent token reaches 4.5:1 on `color.surface.default`, `raised` and `inset` in both themes, and each status one on its own tinted surface too ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-the-build-checks)), so the words read in both variants wherever the tag sits.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Tag is text: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys and must give it a target of `size.target-min`, which a tag is not.

| Key  | Does                             | From   |
| ---- | -------------------------------- | ------ |
| none | Tag is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element | Role                     | Accessible name from                                                        | States announced |
| ------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a generic `<span>` | Not named; its words are read in place, as part of the row or card it marks | none             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the caller's words say what the tag marks, in every `color` and `variant`; the colour and the dashed edge only repeat it, so a `dashed` tag's words say it is not confirmed, such as "Cancellation expected" (CR-5). The capitals are `text-transform` over sentence-case source text, so a screen reader reads the words as written, not letter by letter.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; Tag is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Tag owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` as a string, an element such as `<time>`, or a list of both, each inside the one root; every `variant` and `color` has its story.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; Tag does not animate.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<span>` with no role and no ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Tag takes no focus.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Tag is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Tag has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as `children`.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** Tag renders one `<span>` through `useRender`, with `defaultTagName: 'span'`, and its props merge as `mergeProps(rest, own)`, the caller's first, so `className` reads `pn-Tag` and then the caller's and Tag's own data attributes win. `variant` and `color` are taken out of `rest` before the merge, so neither reaches the DOM as an attribute.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant` and `data-color` with the prop's value, defaults included, and the CSS reads every colour from them, as [Tokens](#tokens) gives: `.pn-Tag[data-variant='filled'][data-color='danger']`.
- **CR-3.** The colour is set once, on the root, and the words take it; the `filled` fill and the `dashed` edge never change the text colour.
- **CR-4.** Both variants keep one geometry: each draws a `border.width.025` edge, `transparent` and solid on `filled`, `color.border.strong` and dashed on `dashed`, so a filled and a dashed tag with the same words share one width and height, and Windows' forced colours draw an edge round every tag when the fill is dropped. No `(forced-colors: active)` rule is needed.
- **CR-5.** A status `color` comes with words that say it, such as "Cancelled" or "Replacement bus", and a `dashed` tag's words say it is not confirmed where that matters, such as "Replacement bus planned". Tag can't hold this for the caller, so the JSDoc of `color` says it and the review holds the stories to it.
- **CR-6.** Tag never cuts its words off: it sits on one line wherever it fits, and it sets no `white-space: nowrap` and no `text-overflow`. Alone in a container narrower than it, at 320 px or at 200% zoom, it wraps inside itself, a word longer than the line breaking within it, and stays inside the container ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks), zoom and reflow). In a flex row, `overflow-wrap: break-word` keeps its words whole, so its narrowest width is its longest word: a row that holds a tag beside other content wraps, with `flex-wrap: wrap`, or lets its other content give way.
- **CR-7.** Tag is not interactive: no `tabIndex` and no handler of its own. The caller's handlers and attributes reach the root unchanged.
- **CR-8.** The source text is the caller's, in sentence case, as [Content design](../content-design.md) asks; the capitals come only from `text-transform`, so the DOM and the accessibility tree hold the sentence-case words.
- **CR-9.** Tag's own props are only those [Props](#props) gives: `children` is required in the type, `color` has no `brand`, and there is no `size`, `startIcon` or `slotProps`. Its one geometry is the [Tokens](#tokens) table's, so a tag sits beside a `size.badge` LineBadge without making the row taller.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named as the `variant` and `color` values in PascalCase. Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree and the DOM, not the pixels.

| Story           | Shows                                                                                                                                                   | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FilledNeutral` | `variant='filled'`, `color='neutral'`, the defaults: "Night bus", the meta's args                                                                       | `data-variant` is `filled` and `data-color` is `neutral`; the text in the DOM is "Night bus", in sentence case, and its computed `text-transform` is `uppercase`; the tag is not focusable; with the canvas narrowed to a few characters' width, the tag wraps onto more than one line and stays inside the canvas, then the canvas is restored (CR-6); in a 320 px flex row beside a departure's long text, the tag keeps "Night" whole on its line rather than break it (CR-6); `children` as a `<time>` element and as a list of a string and a `<time>` each render inside the one root |
| `FilledSuccess` | `variant='filled'`, `color='success'`: "Step-free"                                                                                                      | `data-variant` is `filled` and `data-color` is `success`; the text is "Step-free"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `FilledWarning` | `variant='filled'`, `color='warning'`: "Replacement bus"                                                                                                | `data-variant` is `filled` and `data-color` is `warning`; the text is "Replacement bus"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `FilledDanger`  | `variant='filled'`, `color='danger'`: "Cancelled"                                                                                                       | `data-variant` is `filled` and `data-color` is `danger`; the text is "Cancelled"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `FilledInfo`    | `variant='filled'`, `color='info'`: "Extra departure"                                                                                                   | `data-variant` is `filled` and `data-color` is `info`; the text is "Extra departure"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `DashedNeutral` | `variant='dashed'`, `color='neutral'`: "Night bus planned"                                                                                              | `data-variant` is `dashed` and `data-color` is `neutral`; the text is "Night bus planned"; the computed `border-style` is `dashed` and the computed border width is the `border.width.025` hairline `filled` draws too, so both variants share one box (CR-4)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `DashedSuccess` | `variant='dashed'`, `color='success'`: "Step-free expected"                                                                                             | `data-variant` is `dashed` and `data-color` is `success`; the text is "Step-free expected"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DashedWarning` | `variant='dashed'`, `color='warning'`: "Replacement bus planned"                                                                                        | `data-variant` is `dashed` and `data-color` is `warning`; the text is "Replacement bus planned"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `DashedDanger`  | `variant='dashed'`, `color='danger'`: "Cancellation expected". The subject story, alphabetically first with no `Default`: its args render the tag alone | `data-variant` is `dashed` and `data-color` is `danger`; the text is "Cancellation expected"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `DashedInfo`    | `variant='dashed'`, `color='info'`: "Extra departure planned"                                                                                           | `data-variant` is `dashed` and `data-color` is `info`; the text is "Extra departure planned"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                          | Don't                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mark a property of a departure, vehicle or line with one or two words: "Night bus", "Replacement bus".                                      | Put a sentence in a tag: say what is happening beside it, in plain sentences, as content design asks.                                          |
| Write the words in sentence case and let the tag set the capitals.                                                                          | Type the capitals: a screen reader may spell them out letter by letter.                                                                        |
| Say a status in the words: `color='danger'` on "Cancelled".                                                                                 | Let red or green be the only sign, which fails 1.4.1 and every rider who can't tell them apart.                                                |
| Use `dashed` for something announced but not yet confirmed by live data, and say so in the words where it matters: "Cancellation expected". | Use `dashed` as a quieter look for a property that holds: the dashed edge says "not confirmed", and the brand never claims more than it knows. |
| Name a kind of disruption with SeverityLabel, a line with LineBadge, and a number with Count.                                               | Spell out "Delays", a line's name or a count in a tag: each has its own component, with its own words, colours and figures.                    |
| Use FilterChip for a filter people turn on and off.                                                                                         | Make a tag a control through `render`: it is smaller than `size.target-min` and has no hover, pressed or selected state.                       |
| Let a row that holds a tag beside other content wrap, with `flex-wrap: wrap`, or let its other content give way.                            | Set a tag in a row that can't wrap: its narrowest width is its longest word, so a long word pushes it past the row's edge.                     |
