# EmptyState

Stands in for a list or panel that has nothing to show, and says in plain words what is empty, why, and what to try next.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md) and the tokens. EmptyState has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/EmptyState`. Family: none, since it is static content that sits on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment. Shared parts: none.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                             | Base UI part                          | Class                       | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` stacking the parts below in a centred column                                                   | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState`             | none            |
| `icon`              | A `div` holding the caller's `icon`, hidden from screen readers; rendered only when given              | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-icon`        | `icon`          |
| `title`             | A `p` holding the caller's `title`: what is empty                                                      | None: `useRender`, a `p` by default   | `pn-EmptyState-title`       | `title`         |
| `description`       | A `div` holding the caller's `children`: why, and what to try; rendered only when given                | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-description` | `description`   |
| `action`            | A `div` holding the caller's `action`, such as a button that clears a filter; rendered only when given | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-action`      | `action`        |

No part has a Base UI component, because none has behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. Each part renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, so each takes `render`, as the root does and as its `slotProps` key does for an inner part.

- Decided: the title renders as a `p` by default, with no heading level of its own; a caller that wants it in the page's outline makes it a heading through `slotProps.title.render`, such as `render: <h3 />`. EmptyState sits inside panels whose heading levels it cannot know, and a wrong level breaks the outline where a `p` leaves it whole.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: each part renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render`, and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part                | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                      | Passed through                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` for root        | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, `ref`, the class `pn-EmptyState`, and the parts below as children       | `render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props |
| `useRender` for icon        | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-icon`, `aria-hidden: true`, `icon` as children | `slotProps.icon`                                                      |
| `useRender` for title       | `p`     | `defaultTagName: 'p'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-title`, `title` as children                      | `slotProps.title`, its `render` making it a heading                   |
| `useRender` for description | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-description`, `children` as children           | `slotProps.description`                                               |
| `useRender` for action      | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-action`, `action` as children                  | `slotProps.action`                                                    |

Base UI already does: swapping each part's element through `render` while keeping its class and props, joining `className` strings and `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`, and setting `ref` on the rendered element.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                    | Type                              | Default | Base UI prop                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`                 | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | What is empty, in a few words: "No matches for Nørrebro st". Required. Replaces the HTML `title` attribute                                                                                                                                                               |
| `children`              | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | The sentence under the title: why it is empty and what to try. "Try a line number such as 5C."                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `icon`                  | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | An icon from Perron's set above the title, for the eye only: it is hidden from screen readers. It renders at 16 px, `icon.size.400`; for an icon drawn for another step, set `--perron-icon-size` to that step's `icon.size.*` on the icon part through `slotProps.icon` |
| `action`                | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | What the person can do about it, such as a button that clears the search, below the sentence                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `render`                | Base UI's `render`                |         | inherited                   | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                                |
| `className`             | `string`                          |         | none                        | Joined after `pn-EmptyState` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`                   |         | none                        | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ref`                   | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`             |         | none                        | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `slotProps.icon`        | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for icon        | Props for the `icon` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slotProps.title`       | `useRender.ComponentProps<'p'>`   |         | `useRender` for title       | Props for the `title` part. Its `render` makes the title a heading: `render: <h3 />`                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `slotProps.description` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for description | Props for the `description` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `slotProps.action`      | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for action      | Props for the `action` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, as the contract's Root section says; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `EmptyStateProps` does not declare it again. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop.

- Decided: `children` is the sentence under the title, the way MUI's `Alert` takes its message, rather than a separate `description` prop, so the common call reads `<EmptyState title="No departures in the next hour">Nothing leaves this stop in the next hour.</EmptyState>`. The part keeps the name `description` for its class and `slotProps` key.
- Decided: the names `title`, `icon` and `action` are taken from MUI (`CardHeader`'s `title`, `Alert`'s `icon` and `action`), and `title` is taken out of the root's props so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element; an EmptyState has no use for a hover tooltip.
- Decided: EmptyState ships with no `variant`, `size` or `color`, one look everywhere. The uses known now (an empty search, an empty list in a sheet, a data panel with nothing to show) share one calm look, and any of the three can join later as an optional prop without a break.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. EmptyState has no interactive state of its own, so every row is rest; the caller's action keeps its own states.

| Part          | State | Property             | Token                                 |
| ------------- | ----- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `root`        | rest  | `padding-block`      | `space.600`                           |
| `root`        | rest  | `padding-inline`     | `space.400`                           |
| `root`        | rest  | `gap`                | `space.100`                           |
| `icon`        | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.secondary`                |
| `icon`        | rest  | `margin-block-end`   | `space.200`                           |
| `icon`        | rest  | `--perron-icon-size` | `icon.size.400`                       |
| `title`       | rest  | `font`               | `typography.heading-sm`               |
| `title`       | rest  | `letter-spacing`     | `typography.heading-sm`, its tracking |
| `title`       | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.primary`                  |
| `description` | rest  | `font`               | `typography.body-sm`                  |
| `description` | rest  | `letter-spacing`     | `typography.body-sm`, its tracking    |
| `description` | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.secondary`                |
| `action`      | rest  | `gap`                | `space.200`                           |
| `action`      | rest  | `margin-block-start` | `space.300`                           |

The root is a flex column with `align-items: center` and `text-align: center`; the action is a flex row that wraps, centred. The spacing comes out as 12 px from icon to title (`space.100` and `space.200`), 4 px from title to sentence, and 16 px from sentence to action (`space.100` and `space.300`). Every part and the root reset the margins a `p` brings, and the icon part is a flex box so an inline SVG adds no baseline gap below it.

- Decided: the root has no fill, border, radius or shadow, so EmptyState takes the surface of the panel, sheet or popup it sits in. It is content, not a card, and a surface of its own would join no family and stack a box inside a box.
- Decided: the layout is a centred column, padded `space.600` on the block axis and `space.400` on the inline axis, with the gaps in the table above. Centred is how an empty list reads at a glance in a narrow sheet, 24 px matches the space between blocks of a pane, and 16 px inline keeps text clear of a 320 px screen's edges.
- Decided: the icon is a bare icon from Perron's set, in `color.text.secondary`, with no disc or tile behind it, and the icon part sets `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400`, the 16 px step the set's default icons are drawn for, as the contract sizes an icon on the element that holds it. An icon drawn for another step gets that step's `icon.size.*` through `slotProps.icon`, by `className` or `style`; a larger icon needs a new drawing, as the icon foundation's Sizes section says, never a scaled one. The brand keeps the interface calm, and a disc would need a size token no foundation gives it.
- Decided: the title is `typography.heading-sm` in `color.text.primary`, and the sentence `typography.body-sm` in `color.text.secondary`. The roles' own uses are "card titles" and "the line under a title", and both colours meet 4.5:1 on every surface.

## Keyboard and ARIA

EmptyState has no keys of its own and is never focusable. The caller's action is reached in reading order.

| Key         | Does                                                                   | From        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable element in the action, after the sentence | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back out of the action, to whatever came before the EmptyState   | The browser |

| Element       | Role                                                               | Accessible name from             | States announced |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`        | None (generic `div`)                                               | None                             | None             |
| `icon`        | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"`                                       | None                             | None             |
| `title`       | Paragraph, or a heading when `slotProps.title.render` makes it one | Its text, from `title`           | None             |
| `description` | None (generic `div`)                                               | None                             | None             |
| `action`      | None (generic `div`); the caller's controls carry their own roles  | The caller's controls' own names | Theirs           |

- Decided: the root carries no live-region role, leaving the caller to add `role="status"` when the EmptyState replaces results while the person types or filters. An empty state shown with the page on load needs no announcement, the accessibility rules ask for live regions on changes of state only, and a search field such as SearchField announces its own empty results.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the icon is `aria-hidden` and decorative, and the title, read as text, says what the icon shows.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is not a landmark or region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; EmptyState owns no string.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title`, `children`, `icon` and `action` each render a string, an element and an array; `description` and `action` are `div`s, so block content such as a list is valid inside them, and the title takes phrasing content as a `p` or a heading does.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `p` for the title, made a native `h2` to `h6` through `render` when it heads a section; the action holds the caller's own `button` or `a href`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the action follows the sentence in the DOM and on screen; EmptyState never moves focus when it appears, and nothing in it closes.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: EmptyState has no target of its own; the action's targets are the caller's components, which keep their own sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word EmptyState shows comes from the caller, through `title`, `children` and `action`, and the icon is hidden from screen readers.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The optional parts render only when given: no `icon` part without `icon`, no `description` part without `children`, no `action` part without `action`. A value that renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) counts as not given, so no empty wrapper takes up a gap.
- **CR-2.** The `icon` part always carries `aria-hidden="true"`, after the caller's `slotProps.icon` props, so those props cannot make the icon speak; the title says what it shows. A `render` element's own props are the caller's: `useRender` merges them last, as Base UI does, so a caller that swaps the icon's element leaves `aria-hidden` off it.
- **CR-3.** `title`, `icon`, `action`, `children`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element.
- **CR-4.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class, `aria-hidden` and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `render` swaps the element.
- **CR-5.** EmptyState never moves focus, sets no `tabindex` and adds no role to the root; the caller decides whether it is announced.
- **CR-6.** It sizes to its container, with no width or max-width of its own, and long words wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a long Danish stop name in the title fits a 320 px screen.
- **CR-7.** Colour sits on the parts that hold text, and the icon takes `currentColor` from its part, as the icon foundation asks.

## Stories

One per variant and state the Penpot design shows, named as Penpot names it. The design is deferred and has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `TitleOnly` is the same variant with the optional props left out, and proves CR-1.

| Story       | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                  | `play` test                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`   | Every part: the `search` icon, `title` "No matches for Nørrebro st", the sentence "Try a line number such as 5C." and an action, an `outline` `neutral` Button "Clear search", at rest | The icon part is `aria-hidden`; Tab reaches the "Clear search" button and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started                             |
| `TitleOnly` | `title` "No departures in the next hour", with no icon, sentence or action                                                                                                             | Only the root and the title render: no `pn-EmptyState-icon`, `pn-EmptyState-description` or `pn-EmptyState-action` element, and nothing in it takes focus |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                                                     | Don't                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Say what is empty, then what to try, in plain sentences: "No matches for Nørrebro st" over "Try a line number such as 5C."                                                             | Write "Oops! Nothing here!": content design has no exclamation marks, and the title should name what is missing                             |
| Say only what the data knows: "No departures in the next hour" when the timetable covers an hour                                                                                       | Write "No departures" when there may be some later: the brand never claims more certainty than the data has                                 |
| Use it for a list, a search or a panel with nothing in it                                                                                                                              | Use it for loading or for missing real-time data: loading says "Loading", and missing data uses the data-state words such as "No signal"    |
| Give one neutral action at most, such as clearing the search or the filters                                                                                                            | Add a `brand` action when the panel already has one: a screen has one brand action at most                                                  |
| Pick a decorative icon from Perron's set that matches the title, or none; it renders at 16 px, and one drawn for another step takes that step's `icon.size.*` through `slotProps.icon` | Let the icon carry meaning alone, or use an emoji: the icon is hidden from screen readers and Mylder uses no emoji                          |
| Make the title a heading through `slotProps.title.render` when the EmptyState stands in for a whole section                                                                            | Wrap the title in your own heading element inside `title`: the part is a `p` until `render` swaps it, and a heading inside a `p` is invalid |
| Add `role="status"` on the root when it replaces results as the person types or filters, so the change is announced                                                                    | Add a live region to an EmptyState shown on load: there is no change to announce, and it adds noise                                         |

markdown:
# SearchField

The field that finds a line or a stop: a labelled text input with the search icon, a clear button while it holds text, and a list of suggestions under it that narrows as the person types.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `Field` and `Autocomplete` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/SearchField`. Family: Fields, for the input group; Popups, for the list's popup; Rows, for its suggestions. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, for a hidden label; `CloseButton`, for the clear button.

SearchField is a text field whose value is the words typed, with suggestions under it: Base UI's Autocomplete, not its Combobox, which keeps a chosen item as its value. It composes the parts the registry entry lists, `Field.Root`, `Field.Label` and the ten `Autocomplete` parts from `Autocomplete.Root` to `Autocomplete.Empty`, and none of Autocomplete's others: no `Autocomplete.Trigger` or `Autocomplete.Icon`, since the list opens as the person types; no `Group`, `GroupLabel`, `Separator`, `Row` or `Collection`, since the suggestions are one flat list; no `Status`, `Backdrop` or `Arrow`. Groups can join later, as an optional prop, without a break.

The suggestions are data, `items`, and SearchField draws each row, so the caller never writes a row and there is no `SearchFieldItem` component: the contract's rule of a component per child applies to a child the caller writes many times.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                            | Base UI part              | Class                        | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `<div>`, a flex column that stacks the label over the input group and takes its container's width                                                                                   | `Field.Root`              | `pn-SearchField`             | none            |
| `label`             | The `<label>` that holds the caller's `label` and names the input; with `hiddenLabel`, a `VisuallyHidden` span the eye never sees                                                     | `Field.Label`             | `pn-SearchField-label`       | `label`         |
| `inputGroup`        | The field's box, `size.input` tall: a flex row on the Fields family's fill and edge that holds the icon, the input and the clear button, and the box the list is placed against       | `Autocomplete.InputGroup` | `pn-SearchField-inputGroup`  | `inputGroup`    |
| `icon`              | The `search` icon at the start of the box, an inline SVG hidden from screen readers                                                                                                   | none: an `<svg>`          | `pn-SearchField-icon`        | none            |
| `input`             | The native `<input>` the person types in, transparent inside the box, growing to fill it                                                                                              | `Autocomplete.Input`      | `pn-SearchField-input`       | `input`         |
| `clear`             | The `CloseButton` at the end of the box, named by the owned "Clear"; rendered only while the input holds text and the field is not disabled                                           | `Autocomplete.Clear`      | `pn-SearchField-clear`       | `clear`         |
| `portal`            | Not drawn: the `<div>` Base UI appends to `<body>` while the list is open                                                                                                             | `Autocomplete.Portal`     | `pn-SearchField-portal`      | `portal`        |
| `positioner`        | Not drawn: the box Base UI places under the input group, flipping above it when there is no room, and that carries the stacking and the gap                                           | `Autocomplete.Positioner` | `pn-SearchField-positioner`  | `positioner`    |
| `popup`             | The list's glass panel, as wide as the input group, that scrolls when the suggestions are taller than the room                                                                        | `Autocomplete.Popup`      | `pn-SearchField-popup`       | `popup`         |
| `empty`             | The message the popup shows when no suggestion matches, the owned "No matches", a polite live region that stays mounted and holds nothing while there are matches                     | `Autocomplete.Empty`      | `pn-SearchField-empty`       | `empty`         |
| `list`              | The `<div role="listbox">` that holds one row per matching item                                                                                                                       | `Autocomplete.List`       | `pn-SearchField-list`        | `list`          |
| `item`              | One suggestion: a row, a flex row of the item's `startIcon` and its text, highlighted under the pointer or the arrow keys                                                             | `Autocomplete.Item`       | `pn-SearchField-item`        | `item`          |
| `startIcon`         | A `<span>` before the text that holds the item's `startIcon`, such as a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) or a [LineBadge](line-badge.md); rendered only when the item gives one         | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-startIcon`   | none            |
| `text`              | A `<span>`, a flex column that holds the item's label and description                                                                                                                 | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-text`        | none            |
| `itemLabel`         | A `<span>` that holds the item's `label`, the words the input takes when the item is chosen                                                                                           | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-itemLabel`   | none            |
| `description`       | A `<span>` under the label that holds the item's `description`, such as "Metro, S-tog and bus"; rendered only when the item gives one                                                 | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-description` | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring round the input group while the input has `:focus-visible`, drawn on the group so it rings the whole box rather than the bare input inside it; not an element | `Autocomplete.InputGroup` | none                         | none            |

`Autocomplete.Root` groups the Autocomplete parts and holds the value and the open state; it renders no element, so it has no layer, class or `slotProps` key. The item's inner spans are named for the item fields they show, `itemLabel` rather than `label`, since `label` is the field's own part.

The clear button composes the `CloseButton` shared part, rendered through `Autocomplete.Clear`'s `render` as `<Autocomplete.Clear render={<CloseButton label={strings.clear} />} />`. It keeps the part's own `size.control` square and looks, SearchField's CSS sets only its place in the row, it is left out entirely while the field is disabled, and the build adds `Autocomplete.Clear` to the part's "Composed in" cell in the contract's Shared parts table. The contract's `shared-parts` check keeps the `close` icon inside `CloseButton`'s folder, so SearchField can't draw a cross of its own; a 34 px square sits inside the 38 px box with a pixel to spare above and below; and the part has no disabled look (Dialog CR-6), while a disabled field takes no clearing, so the button is not rendered rather than shown live.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/field` and `@base-ui/react/autocomplete`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part              | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                | Passed through                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field.Root`              | A `<div>`, with `data-disabled`, `data-filled`, `data-focused`, `data-dirty`, `data-touched` and `data-valid`                                                                                                                                                                             | `className` (`pn-SearchField`, then the caller's), `ref`, and the parts below as children                                                                                                  | `name`, `disabled`, `render`, `style` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                              |
| `Field.Label`             | A `<label>`, its id the input's `aria-labelledby`; with `hiddenLabel`, the `VisuallyHidden` span through `render`, with `nativeLabel={false}`                                                                                                                                             | `className` (`pn-SearchField-label`, then the caller's), an `id` from React's `useId` that the list's `aria-labelledby` reads, and `label` as children                                     | `slotProps.label`                                                                                                         |
| `Autocomplete.Root`       | No element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `items`, `filter`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `open` and `defaultOpen` from SearchField's props; `onValueChange`, turned into `onChange`; `onOpenChange`, turned into `onOpen` and `onClose` | none                                                                                                                      |
| `Autocomplete.InputGroup` | `<div role="group">`, with `data-popup-open`, `data-list-empty`, `data-disabled`, `data-filled` and `data-focused`                                                                                                                                                                        | `className` (`pn-SearchField-inputGroup`, then the caller's), and the icon, the input and the clear button as children                                                                     | `slotProps.inputGroup`                                                                                                    |
| `Autocomplete.Input`      | `<input role="combobox">`, with `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-controls` while open, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-labelledby` the label, `aria-activedescendant` the highlighted row, `autocomplete="off"`, `spellcheck="false"`, the field's `name`, and `data-popup-open` | `className` (`pn-SearchField-input`, then the caller's), `placeholder`, and `enterKeyHint="search"` (see Component rules)                                                                  | `slotProps.input`: `autoFocus`, `inputMode` and every other prop of an `<input>`                                          |
| `Autocomplete.Clear`      | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1">` through `render`: the `CloseButton`; mounted only while the input holds text, with `data-visible`                                                                                                                                                  | `className` (`pn-SearchField-clear`, then the caller's), and `render`, the `CloseButton` with the clear label                                                                              | `slotProps.clear`: every prop of a `<button>` but `disabled` (CR-7)                                                       |

Base UI already does: it filters `items` against the typed words, as the person types, with a collator in the runtime's locale that ignores case and accents (`contains`), matching each item's `label`; it opens the list when the person types words that aren't blank (reason `'input-change'`) or presses an arrow key (`'list-navigation'`), and closes it when the input is emptied (`'input-clear'`), on Esc (`'escape-key'`), on a press outside the field and the list (`'outside-press'`), when focus leaves (`'focus-out'`) and when an item is chosen (`'item-press'`); it moves a virtual highlight through the rows with the arrow keys, looping back to the input, keeping focus in the input with `aria-activedescendant`, and highlights a row under the pointer; on an item's press, or Enter on a highlighted row, it fills the input with the item's label, calls the item's `onClick` and closes the list; on Enter with no row highlighted it closes the list (`'none'`) and lets a form around it submit; on Esc with the list closed it empties the input; it shows the clear button only while the input holds text, keeps it out of the tab order and keeps focus in the input when it is pressed; it places the popup against the input group, below it, flipping above it when there is no room, and gives it `--anchor-width` and `--available-height`; it names the input by the label, puts the field's `name` on the input itself, so the typed words reach a form's `FormData`, and passes `disabled` from `Field.Root` to the input and the clear button; and it announces the empty message politely when it appears. While the list is open it also adds two screen-reader-only `Dismiss` controls and hides the rest of the page from the ear, the label and the clear button among them (see Keyboard and ARIA, Base UI's known exceptions).

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets its description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

SearchField is a composite control: its root is `Field.Root`'s `<div>`, and its value is the typed words, reported as `onChange(event, value, details)` adapted from `Autocomplete.Root`'s `onValueChange`, not React's own `onChange` on an `<input>` root. The contract's "Native text" rule fits a value only the `<input>` changes, but Base UI also changes this one from outside the input's own events (it fills the input with a chosen item's label, empties it on Esc and on the clear button, each with a `details.reason`), which React's `onChange(event)` never reports; the contract's Forms rule names a combobox among the composite controls; and the root must hold the label as well as the input. The field's `name` still reaches the `<input>`, so a native form submits the typed words, and form libraries connect through their controller.

From `Autocomplete.Root`, SearchField offers only `items`, `filter`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen` and `onClose`. It keeps Base UI's defaults for the rest (`mode` `'list'`, `autoHighlight` `false`, `openOnInputClick` `false`, `submitOnItemClick` `false`, `loopFocus` `true`, `limit` `-1`) and leaves out `readOnly`, `required`, `inline`, `grid`, `virtualized`, `modal`, `itemToStringValue`, `filteredItems`, `onItemHighlighted`, `actionsRef` and `inputRef`. These are what a search for a line or a stop needs; with `autoHighlight` off, Enter on the typed words submits a form around the field, as a search does, and a row is chosen by the arrow keys or the pointer; each prop left out can join later as an optional prop without a break.

`SearchFieldProps` extends `Field.Root.Props` without `children`, `ref`, `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `actionsRef`, `dirty` and `touched`, so `name`, `disabled`, `render`, `className` and `style` are inherited with Base UI's JSDoc, and SearchField has no invalid state. The registry gives SearchField no `Field.Error` or `Field.Description`, so an invalid field could only say so by its red edge, which [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) forbids as colour alone; a search is never wrong, only empty of matches; and without `required` (left out above), Base UI never marks the field invalid on its own, so `[data-invalid]` never appears and the Fields family's invalid edge is not drawn.

A suggestion is a `SearchFieldItem`, exported from `SearchField.tsx`, of the shape `{ value: string; label: string; description?: ReactNode; startIcon?: ReactNode }`, with `items` typed `ReadonlyArray<SearchFieldItem>` and `filter` typed `((item: SearchFieldItem, query: string) => boolean) | null`. `value` identifies the item and keys its row, so two stops with the same name stay apart; Base UI reads `label` from a `{ value, label }` object on its own, for filtering and to fill the input; `description` is the Rows family's second line; and `startIcon` follows the contract's name for a mark before a label, here a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) or a [LineBadge](line-badge.md). No `disabled` per item: a suggestion that can't be chosen is left out of `items`.

A chosen suggestion is reported by `onItemSelect(event, item)`, called from the item's `onClick` with the click event and the `SearchFieldItem` itself, on a press or on Enter with the row highlighted. `onChange` then carries only the words, with `details.reason` `'item-press'` when an item filled them, and a caller who moves the map to the stop needs the item, not its label, which two items can share. `onSelect` is not used because the root's `<div>` already takes React's `onSelect`, the text-selection event, and no row is ever "selected" in the Rows family's sense: Autocomplete keeps no chosen item.

SearchField takes a required `label` (`ReactNode`) and a `hiddenLabel` boolean, default `false`, that keeps the label for the ear only, rendering it through the `VisuallyHidden` shared part. Every input needs a name, and the label is the only one that never disappears as the placeholder does; Mylder's top bar search shows only the icon and the placeholder, so `hiddenLabel` is how it keeps the name; `hiddenLabel` is MUI's own name for a field without a visible label.

SearchField takes no `variant`, `size`, `color` or `fullWidth`: its root takes its container's width and its box is `size.input` tall. There is one search field look, `size.input` is the one height the layout tokens give a search field, and the contract has a component size to its container, so a caller sets the width on the container or through `className`.

The default filter keeps Base UI's own collator, in the runtime's locale, rather than PerronProvider's locale. PerronProvider exposes no locale to components, only their owned strings, and adding a hook is a change to every component's provider for one prop; the runtime's locale is the person's own; a caller who wants another collator passes it through `filter`.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The design states the deferred drawing shows are rest, hover, focus, open and disabled, for the field, and rest and highlighted, for a row. The Fields family keeps the box's rest look while the list is open, so open is the popup's look, not the box's; the Fields family's invalid edge is not drawn, since SearchField is never invalid (see Props).

The label takes `typography.label` in `color.text.primary`, `space.100` above the box, and the box holds, from its start, the search icon in `color.text.secondary` at `icon.size.400`, `space.300` in from its start edge, the input, `space.200` after the icon, and the clear button, `space.050` in from its end edge. `typography.label` is the contract's type for a name in a list or on a control, and `space.100` keeps the name with its box; `space.300` matches the inline padding of the rows below, so the icon and the rows' text start near one line; the icon is decoration beside the placeholder, so it takes the secondary ink the `CloseButton` takes at rest, and `space.050` sets the 34 px button inside the 36 px between the borders with a pixel above and below.

The list sits `space.100` below the box, as the positioner's `padding-block` rather than a `sideOffset` read in script, with the popup as wide as the box (`inline-size: var(--anchor-width)`) and at most as tall as the room left (`max-block-size: calc(var(--available-height) - 2 * var(--perron-space-100))`). Padding inside the box Base UI measures keeps the gap on whichever side the list flips to, with no script, so no prop needs the token as a value and the shared `tokenValue` helper is not called; a list as wide as its field reads as the field's own.

A row takes `space.150` above and below and `space.200` at its sides, with `space.200` between its start icon and its text, and the empty message takes `typography.body-sm` in `color.text.secondary`, with the same padding as a row while it holds the message and none while it is empty. Rows of `typography.label` at `space.150` stand about 29 px tall, above `size.target-min`, and a two-line row with its `typography.caption` description stays compact; the empty message is a sentence, not a row, so it takes body text in the secondary ink; and Base UI asks that `Autocomplete.Empty` stay mounted, never `display: none`, so its padding is drawn only on `:not(:empty)`, leaving no gap above the rows.
