# MapControls

The map's zoom in, zoom out and centre buttons, in one glass bar that is one tab stop, named and labelled in the reader's language.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the spec of [Toolbar](toolbar.md), the one entry it depends on, and of [IconButton](icon-button.md), which it does not use (see Anatomy). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/MapControls`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no bar of actions; the bar is Toolbar's, on the Popups' glass). Shared parts: none (each button is an icon-only `ToolbarButton`, named by its `aria-label` from an owned string, as Toolbar's icon-only buttons are).

MapControls renders Perron's `Toolbar`, vertical by default, holding three icon-only `ToolbarButton`s in the order zoom in, zoom out, a `ToolbarSeparator`, centre the map, with no `ToolbarGroup` and no IconButton, so its `dependsOn` in `packages/perron/components.json` names `Toolbar` alone. The Toolbar spec's Do and don't says an IconButton inside a Toolbar "falls out of the arrow-key order and adds a tab stop", and the IconButton spec says a `neutral` icon button floated over the map "disappears on the land and water", so the controls are Toolbar's buttons on Toolbar's glass; this is the column Toolbar's `Vertical` story draws ("zoom in, zoom out, a separator, locate"); and a group would only need a name of its own for two buttons the separator already sets apart.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                            | Base UI part                                                    | Class                      | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | Perron's `Toolbar`: the glass bar, a column (or a row when horizontal), named "Map controls"                                          | `Toolbar.Root`, through Perron's `Toolbar`                      | `pn-MapControls`           | none            |
| `zoomIn`            | A `ToolbarButton`, icon-only: the native `<button>` that zooms in, showing the `plus` icon                                            | `Toolbar.Button`, through Perron's `ToolbarButton`              | `pn-MapControls-zoomIn`    | none            |
| `zoomOut`           | A `ToolbarButton`, icon-only: the native `<button>` that zooms out, showing the `minus` icon                                          | `Toolbar.Button`, through Perron's `ToolbarButton`              | `pn-MapControls-zoomOut`   | none            |
| `separator`         | A `ToolbarSeparator`: the hairline across the bar between the zoom pair and the centre button                                         | `Toolbar.Separator`, through Perron's `ToolbarSeparator`        | `pn-MapControls-separator` | none            |
| `centerMap`         | A `ToolbarButton`, icon-only: the native `<button>` that centres the map on the network, showing the `locate` icon                    | `Toolbar.Button`, through Perron's `ToolbarButton`              | `pn-MapControls-centerMap` | none            |
| `icon`              | The inline SVG in each button: `plus`, `minus` or `locate` from `packages/perron/icons/`, inside `ToolbarButton`'s `aria-hidden` span | none: an `<svg>` inside the `startIcon` span of `ToolbarButton` | `perron-icon`              | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring on a button: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws on `button`, not an element                      | `Toolbar.Button`                                                | none                       | none            |

Each part also keeps the class of the Perron component it is: the root `pn-Toolbar`, each button `pn-ToolbarButton`, the separator `pn-ToolbarSeparator`, which carry every look (see Tokens).

## Base UI parts

None imported here: MapControls composes Perron's `Toolbar`, `ToolbarButton` and `ToolbarSeparator` from `packages/perron/src/components/Toolbar/Toolbar.tsx`, which render Base UI's parts from `@base-ui/react/toolbar` at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0), so the registry's `baseUiParts` is empty. The parts that reach the DOM:

| Base UI part        | Renders                                                                                                                            | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                            | Passed through                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Toolbar.Root`      | `<div role="toolbar" aria-orientation>`, with `data-orientation` and, when disabled, `data-disabled`                               | Through `Toolbar`: `className` (`pn-Toolbar`, then `pn-MapControls`, then the caller's), `ref`, `orientation` (default `'vertical'`), `disabled`, and `aria-label` from the `mapControls` owned string | `loopFocus`, `render`, `style`, `aria-labelledby` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}` |
| `Toolbar.Button`    | `<button type="button">`, three times, with `data-orientation`, `data-disabled` when disabled and `data-focusable` while focusable | Through `ToolbarButton`: `className` (`pn-ToolbarButton`, then `pn-MapControls-<part>`), `color` `'neutral'`, `startIcon` (the icon), `aria-label` from its owned string, `onClick`, `disabled`        | Nothing: the caller reaches each button only through its `on…`, `…Disabled` and `…Label` props           |
| `Toolbar.Separator` | `<div role="separator" aria-orientation>`, its orientation across the toolbar's, with `data-orientation`                           | Through `ToolbarSeparator`: `className` (`pn-ToolbarSeparator`, then `pn-MapControls-separator`)                                                                                                       | Nothing                                                                                                  |

Base UI already does: one tab stop for the whole bar with a roving `tabIndex`, so Tab enters at the button last focused (zoom in at first) and leaves in one step; the arrow keys of the bar's orientation move between the three buttons, skipping the separator, and wrap at the ends while `loopFocus` is on; a disabled `Toolbar.Root` disables every button; a disabled `Toolbar.Button` stays focusable by default (`focusableWhenDisabled` is `true`), with `aria-disabled` in place of `disabled` and its clicks stopped, so it stays in the arrow-key order; `Toolbar.Separator` takes the orientation across the bar's.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop MapControls declares gets this description as its JSDoc; the inherited rows keep Base UI's. Slots come last.

MapControls takes `orientation`, `'horizontal' | 'vertical'`, default `'vertical'`, passed to `Toolbar`, and redeclares it in `MapControlsProps` so its JSDoc gives that default. [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#page-shell) puts the controls at the bottom right, beside the scale, where the Toolbar spec gives `orientation` "for the map's vertical column of controls"; a screen that lays them along an edge, such as a phone's above the bottom sheet, sets `'horizontal'`.

MapControls takes one handler per button, `onZoomIn(event)`, `onZoomOut(event)` and `onCenterMap(event)`, each given to that `ToolbarButton`'s `onClick`, always renders all three buttons, and takes no `children`. The map, not the controls, holds the zoom level, so the screen does the zooming in a handler; three buttons always in one order keep every screen's controls alike, a button with no handler does nothing rather than vanish; and another map action, such as a layers switch, goes in a Toolbar of its own. Code names take the American spelling, as `color` does, and the English words the British, "Centre the map", as [Content design](../content-design.md) writes.

MapControls takes `zoomInDisabled` and `zoomOutDisabled`, booleans default `false`, that disable the one button at the map's zoom limits, leaving it focusable (`ToolbarButton`'s default `focusableWhenDisabled`). At the closest or farthest zoom a button that still looks pressable misleads; kept focusable, the button keeps the focus a keyboard user pressed it with, stays in the arrow-key order, and is announced as dimmed through `aria-disabled`.

MapControls takes no `slotProps`, and puts a `pn-MapControls-<part>` class on each button and the separator for a caller's CSS. The contract keys `slotProps` by Base UI part, and the three buttons share one, `Toolbar.Button`; every per-button need the sources name (handler, limit, words) is a prop above; and a `slotProps` key can join later as a new optional prop, which [Change](README.md#change) allows.

| Name                        | Type                                                   | Default      | Base UI prop                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation`               | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'`                           | `'vertical'` | `orientation`, through `Toolbar`    | Which way the bar runs, and so which arrow keys move through it: Up and Down for `vertical`, the map's column at the bottom right; Left and Right for `horizontal`.                       |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                                              | `false`      | `disabled`, through `Toolbar`       | Whether every button is disabled, such as while the map loads. The buttons stay focusable and in the arrow-key order.                                                                     |
| `zoomInDisabled`            | `boolean`                                              | `false`      | none                                | Whether the zoom in button is disabled, at the map's closest zoom. It stays focusable and announces that it is dimmed, and a click fires no `onZoomIn`.                                   |
| `zoomOutDisabled`           | `boolean`                                              | `false`      | none                                | Whether the zoom out button is disabled, at the map's farthest zoom. It stays focusable and announces that it is dimmed, and a click fires no `onZoomOut`.                                |
| `onZoomIn`                  | `(event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | none         | `onClick` of the `zoomIn` button    | Called when the zoom in button is pressed, by click, Enter or Space, with the click event. The screen zooms the map in by one step.                                                       |
| `onZoomOut`                 | `(event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | none         | `onClick` of the `zoomOut` button   | Called when the zoom out button is pressed, by click, Enter or Space, with the click event. The screen zooms the map out by one step.                                                     |
| `onCenterMap`               | `(event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | none         | `onClick` of the `centerMap` button | Called when the centre button is pressed, by click, Enter or Space, with the click event. The screen moves and zooms the map to show the whole network.                                   |
| `loopFocus`                 | `boolean`                                              | `true`       | inherited                           | If `true`, using keyboard navigation will wrap focus to the other end of the toolbar once the end is reached.                                                                             |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`                                     | none         | inherited                           | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `mapControlsLabel`          | `string`                                               | The locale's | none                                | Overrides "Map controls", the bar's name.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `zoomInLabel`               | `string`                                               | The locale's | none                                | Overrides "Zoom in", the zoom in button's name.                                                                                                                                           |
| `zoomOutLabel`              | `string`                                               | The locale's | none                                | Overrides "Zoom out", the zoom out button's name.                                                                                                                                         |
| `centerMapLabel`            | `string`                                               | The locale's | none                                | Overrides "Centre the map", the centre button's name.                                                                                                                                     |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                                                | none         | `className`, `style`                | Reach the root, the `role="toolbar"` element. `className` is merged after `pn-Toolbar` and `pn-MapControls`.                                                                              |

No `slotProps`, as answered above. No `children`: the three buttons are the component's own.

## Tokens

MapControls sets no token of its own: every value below is Toolbar's and ToolbarButton's, from the [Toolbar](toolbar.md) spec's Tokens, so the controls match every other toolbar. `MapControls.css` holds no declaration that sets one (CR-9). States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector, hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, pressed is `:active`, focus is `:focus-visible`, disabled is `[data-disabled]`. The three buttons are `neutral`; every `color` row sets the button's `color`, which the icon takes through `currentColor`.

| Part                             | State    | Property                    | Token                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                           | rest     | `background-color`          | `color.surface.overlay`                                                       |
| `root`                           | rest     | `backdrop-filter`           | `effect.glass-blur` (blur) and `effect.glass-saturate`                        |
| `root`                           | rest     | `box-shadow`                | `shadow.panel`                                                                |
| `root`                           | rest     | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                            |
| `root`                           | rest     | `border-color`              | `color.border.subtle`                                                         |
| `root`                           | rest     | `border-radius`             | `radius.lg`                                                                   |
| `root`                           | rest     | `padding`                   | `space.100`                                                                   |
| `root`                           | rest     | `gap`                       | `space.100`                                                                   |
| `separator`, in a vertical bar   | rest     | `border-block-start`        | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`                                   |
| `separator`, in a vertical bar   | rest     | `margin-inline`             | `space.100`                                                                   |
| `separator`, in a horizontal bar | rest     | `border-inline-start`       | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`                                   |
| `separator`, in a horizontal bar | rest     | `margin-block`              | `space.100`                                                                   |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `width`, `height`           | `size.control`                                                                |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `padding-inline`            | 0, as icon-only buttons                                                       |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `border-radius`             | `radius.md`                                                                   |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                            |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `border-color`              | `transparent`                                                                 |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `background-color`          | `transparent`                                                                 |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | rest     | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                                          |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | hover    | `background-color`          | `color.surface.hover`                                                         |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | pressed  | `background-color`          | `color.surface.hover`                                                         |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | focus    | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`) |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | disabled | `background-color`          | `transparent`                                                                 |
| `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`, `centerMap` | disabled | `color`                     | `color.text.tertiary`                                                         |
| `icon`                           | rest     | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400`, set by `ToolbarButton`'s icon span                           |

The bar's place on the map is not here: `z-index.map-controls` and `size.panel-gap` belong to the screen that places it (CR-10).

Highlighted, open, selected and invalid don't apply: a toolbar button takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, and the controls open nothing and hold no choice or value.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Toolbar.Root`, `Toolbar.Button` and `Toolbar.Separator`, as the [Toolbar](toolbar.md) spec gives them. "From" says who does it.

| Key                       | Does                                                                                                                                       | From        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`        | Moves focus into the bar, to the button that last had it (zoom in at first), and out again: the bar is one tab stop                        | Base UI     |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp`    | In the vertical bar, the default, move focus to the next and the previous button, skipping the separator, wrapping while `loopFocus` is on | Base UI     |
| `ArrowRight`, `ArrowLeft` | In a horizontal bar, move focus to the next and the previous button, wrapping while `loopFocus` is on                                      | Base UI     |
| `Enter`, `Space`          | Press the focused button: call its `onZoomIn`, `onZoomOut` or `onCenterMap`, unless it is disabled                                         | The browser |

`Home` and `End` do nothing, as on Toolbar. `+` and `−` zoom the map from the map canvas ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)), not from these controls.

MapControls listens to no keys of its own and sets no `aria-keyshortcuts`, leaving `+` and `−` to the map. Accessibility gives those keys to the screen ("+ and − zoom, arrow keys pan"), the map canvas has focus when they are pressed, and the controls can't know that the screen binds them, so announcing a shortcut could promise one that does nothing.

| Element     | Role                       | Accessible name from                                                            | States announced                                     |
| ----------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`      | `toolbar`, from Base UI    | `aria-label`, the `mapControls` owned string, or the caller's `aria-labelledby` | `aria-orientation`                                   |
| `zoomIn`    | `button`, native           | `aria-label`, the `zoomIn` owned string                                         | `aria-disabled` when `zoomInDisabled` or `disabled`  |
| `zoomOut`   | `button`, native           | `aria-label`, the `zoomOut` owned string                                        | `aria-disabled` when `zoomOutDisabled` or `disabled` |
| `centerMap` | `button`, native           | `aria-label`, the `centerMap` owned string                                      | `aria-disabled` when `disabled`                      |
| `separator` | `separator`, from Base UI  | none                                                                            | `aria-orientation`, across the bar's                 |
| `icon`      | none: inside `aria-hidden` | none                                                                            | none                                                 |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: each icon is `aria-hidden` inside its button, and the button's `aria-label` says the action it shows ("Zoom in", "Zoom out", "Centre the map"); a dimmed button is announced through `aria-disabled`; the separator is announced as one.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the bar is a `toolbar` named "Map controls" by its owned string, so it tells itself apart from the top bar's toolbars.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `mapControlsLabel`, `zoomInLabel`, `zoomOutLabel` and `centerMapLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: the props take no `ReactNode`; both orientations, every `…Disabled` combination and `disabled` render all three buttons, square, in the same order.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the controls keep no hidden copy and collapse nothing.
- [ ] Native semantics first: native `<button>`s from `Toolbar.Button`, Base UI's `toolbar` and `separator` roles, with ARIA only for the names an icon can't give.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the arrow keys move zoom in, zoom out, centre, in document order; the controls open nothing; a button that hits a zoom limit stays focusable, so focus never jumps away from the key a person pressed.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: each button is `size.control` (34 px) square.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the controls have no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

Every word MapControls announces is its own; it shows none. No key in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` says any of these, so all four are new, each with a JSDoc line like its neighbours, and agents write the Danish, Swedish and Norwegian.

The four new keys are `mapControls` "Map controls", `zoomIn` "Zoom in", `zoomOut` "Zoom out" and `centerMap` "Centre the map", overridden by `mapControlsLabel`, `zoomInLabel`, `zoomOutLabel` and `centerMapLabel`. They are the words the Toolbar spec's map stories and the IconButton spec's examples already use, `packages/perron/icons/icons.json` gives `locate` the use "Centre the map on the network", each names the action as a verb and what it acts on, in sentence case ([Content design](../content-design.md)), and the keys take the American spelling of code names.

| Key           | English          | Override           | Seen or heard where                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mapControls` | "Map controls"   | `mapControlsLabel` | `root`, heard as the toolbar's name through `aria-label`     |
| `zoomIn`      | "Zoom in"        | `zoomInLabel`      | `zoomIn`, heard as the button's name through `aria-label`    |
| `zoomOut`     | "Zoom out"       | `zoomOutLabel`     | `zoomOut`, heard as the button's name through `aria-label`   |
| `centerMap`   | "Centre the map" | `centerMapLabel`   | `centerMap`, heard as the button's name through `aria-label` |

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Perron's Toolbar already gives the one tab stop, the roving `tabIndex`, the arrow keys, the wrap, the disabled cascade and a disabled button that stays focusable, through Base UI, so MapControls rebuilds none of it, adds no key handler and sets no `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- **CR-2.** MapControls renders Perron's `Toolbar`, and in it, in this order, a `ToolbarButton` for zoom in, one for zoom out, a `ToolbarSeparator`, and one for centring the map, each button `color="neutral"` and icon-only (a `startIcon` and no `children`). It imports `Toolbar`, `ToolbarButton` and `ToolbarSeparator` from `packages/perron/src/components/Toolbar/Toolbar.tsx`, never `@base-ui/react/toolbar` or IconButton.
- **CR-3.** The root's `className` is `pn-MapControls` then the caller's, given to `Toolbar`, which puts `pn-Toolbar` first. Each button takes `pn-MapControls-zoomIn`, `pn-MapControls-zoomOut` or `pn-MapControls-centerMap`, and the separator `pn-MapControls-separator`, after the class of its own component.
- **CR-4.** `{...rest}` reaches `Toolbar` before MapControls' own attributes, and its own props are taken out of `rest` first (`orientation`, `zoomInDisabled`, `zoomOutDisabled`, `onZoomIn`, `onZoomOut`, `onCenterMap` and the four `…Label` props), so none reaches the DOM. `disabled`, `loopFocus`, `render`, `style`, `aria-labelledby` and `ref` pass through to `Toolbar`, and `ref` lands on the `role="toolbar"` element. The root's `aria-label` is set after `rest` from the `mapControls` string, so a caller renames the bar with `mapControlsLabel`.
- **CR-5.** `orientation` defaults to `'vertical'` in MapControls' own destructuring and is passed to `Toolbar`; `MapControlsProps` redeclares it with `@default 'vertical'`. The root carries Base UI's `data-orientation`; MapControls has no `variant`, `color` or `size` prop, so it sets no `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size`.
- **CR-6.** The words come from `useOwnedStrings({ mapControls: mapControlsLabel, zoomIn: zoomInLabel, zoomOut: zoomOutLabel, centerMap: centerMapLabel })`. Each button's `aria-label` is its string; the component shows no text and sets no `title`.
- **CR-7.** Each icon is an inline `<svg>` with the `perron-icon` class, `viewBox="0 0 16 16"`, `fill="none"`, `stroke="currentColor"`, round caps and joins, and the stroke width and path data of its file in `packages/perron/icons/` (`plus.svg` and `minus.svg` at 1.8, `locate.svg` at 1.6), with no `width`, `height` or colour of its own: `ToolbarButton`'s icon span sets `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400` and hides it from screen readers.
- **CR-8.** `zoomInDisabled` and `zoomOutDisabled`, or `disabled`, set `disabled` on that `ToolbarButton`, which stays focusable (`focusableWhenDisabled` left at its `true` default), carries `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`, and stops the click, so its handler never fires. Neither limit disables the other button or the centre button.
- **CR-9.** `MapControls.css`, imported by the TSX as the contract asks, sets no colour, size, spacing or state: every look is Toolbar's, so the controls match every other toolbar, and a change to Toolbar's look reaches them.
- **CR-10.** MapControls sizes to its content, as Toolbar does, and places nothing: no `position`, `inset`, `margin` or `z-index`. The screen puts it at the bottom right, `size.panel-gap` from the edges, at `z-index.map-controls` ([Layout](../foundations/layout.md#stacking)), a token outside a component's [Token families](README.md#token-families).
- **CR-11.** Each handler is given as its button's `onClick` and called once per press, by click, Enter or Space, with the click event; no handler is called on focus, hover or an arrow key.
- **CR-12.** Changes of state are immediate, as on Toolbar: MapControls adds no transition.

## Stories

MapControls' deferred drawing has one variant property, `orientation` (`vertical`, `horizontal`), and no `State`, leaving the buttons' hover, focus, pressed and disabled looks to ToolbarButton's variants on the Toolbar page, with the zoom limits, `disabled` and the label overrides as stories beside the two variants. The buttons are ToolbarButtons, already drawn and storied in every state, so redrawing them here would only be a second copy to keep alike; the limits and the overrides are behaviour, which the `play` tests check.

The stories render the bar on its own, in a `PerronProvider` in English unless the story says otherwise, with `fn()` handlers for `onZoomIn`, `onZoomOut` and `onCenterMap`. The contract story takes the alphabetically first, `CustomLabels`, whose args hold every word the caller gives.

| Story             | Shows                                                                     | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`         | vertical bar, the default: zoom in, zoom out, a separator, centre the map | The toolbar is named "Map controls" and the buttons "Zoom in", "Zoom out", "Centre the map", each icon `aria-hidden`; Tab focuses zoom in; ArrowDown moves to zoom out, then centre, skipping the separator, and wraps; Enter fires `onZoomIn` once and Space `onCenterMap` once; Shift+Tab leaves |
| `Horizontal`      | horizontal bar, the same three buttons in a row                           | ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move between the buttons and ArrowDown doesn't; the separator's `aria-orientation` is `vertical`                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ZoomInDisabled`  | vertical bar with `zoomInDisabled`, at the closest zoom                   | Zoom in has `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`, the arrow keys still reach it, and a click and Enter fire no `onZoomIn`; zoom out and centre still fire                                                                                                                                           |
| `ZoomOutDisabled` | vertical bar with `zoomOutDisabled`, at the farthest zoom                 | Zoom out has `aria-disabled`, and a click fires no `onZoomOut`; zoom in still fires                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Disabled`        | vertical bar with `disabled`                                              | Every button has `data-disabled`, the arrow keys still move between them, and no click fires a handler                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `CustomLabels`    | vertical bar with all four `…Label` props set                             | The toolbar and the buttons are named by the overrides; rendered in `da` with no overrides, they are named by the Danish dictionary                                                                                                                                                                |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                        | Don't                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Use MapControls for the map's zoom and centre buttons, once per map                                       | Build the same bar from IconButtons or from your own Toolbar: an IconButton in a toolbar adds a tab stop, and a second copy drifts from this one |
| Place it from the screen, at the bottom right, `size.panel-gap` from the edges, at `z-index.map-controls` | Expect MapControls to position itself, or give it a `z-index` through the component: it sizes to its content and the screen places it            |
| Set `zoomInDisabled` or `zoomOutDisabled` when the map reaches a zoom limit                               | Hide or unmount a button at a limit: focus on it is lost and the bar changes shape under the pointer                                             |
| Centre the map on the whole network in `onCenterMap`, as its words promise                                | Wire it to the reader's own location: its words, "Centre the map", and the `locate` icon's use promise the network                               |
| Rename the bar or a button with its `…Label` prop, such as `zoomInLabel`                                  | Pass `aria-label` to the root: the bar's own name is set after it and replaces it                                                                |
| Bind `+` and `−` on the map canvas, where Accessibility puts them                                         | Expect MapControls to listen for keys: it adds none beyond the toolbar's arrows                                                                  |
| Put another map action, such as a layers switch, in a Toolbar of its own beside it                        | Wrap MapControls to add buttons inside it: it takes no `children`, so its three buttons stay the same on every screen                            |

# Tabs

A row of tabs that switches between views of one thing, one panel showing at a time, such as a stop's departures, its lines and its disruptions in the detail panel.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the ROADMAP line that names it (`ROADMAP.md`, "Wave 3, interactive, on Base UI"). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Tabs`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no row of tabs; a tab is ink on whatever surface holds it, marked by an underline). Shared parts: none (every word is the caller's, and the count is text the tab is named by).

The `Tabs` folder holds four components, `Tabs`, `TabsList`, `Tab` and `TabsPanel`, each exported with its props type from `Tabs.tsx`, as an exception to the contract's "one component per folder", and the indicator is drawn by `TabsList`, not offered as a component. Base UI's `Tabs.List`, `Tabs.Tab`, `Tabs.Indicator` and `Tabs.Panel` read `Tabs.Root`'s context, so they can't be built or shown apart, as Toolbar's parts can't; the caller writes many tabs and panels, so each is a component of its own; and an underline that every tab list draws the same way belongs to the list, reached through `slotProps.indicator`, not to the caller. The `props` check reads all four props types, and the `api-compatibility` check only `TabsProps`, so the review holds the other three to the contract's Change rules.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                          | Base UI part                   | Class                   | `slotProps` key             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `root`              | `Tabs`: a flex column that holds the caller's `TabsList` and `TabsPanel`s and owns which tab is selected                                                            | `Tabs.Root`                    | `pn-Tabs`               | none                        |
| `list`              | `TabsList`: the row of tabs, a flex row on a hairline that runs its full width, and the positioning box of the indicator                                            | `Tabs.List`                    | `pn-TabsList`           | none                        |
| `indicator`         | A `<span>` inside `TabsList`, after the caller's tabs: the underline under the selected tab, placed by Base UI's `--active-tab-*` variables                         | `Tabs.Indicator`               | `pn-TabsList-indicator` | `indicator` (on `TabsList`) |
| `tab`               | `Tab`: the native `<button>` of one tab, a flex row, centred, that holds the label and the count                                                                    | `Tabs.Tab`                     | `pn-Tab`                | none                        |
| `label`             | A `<span>` in `Tab` that holds the caller's `children`                                                                                                              | none: a span inside `Tabs.Tab` | `pn-Tab-label`          | none                        |
| `count`             | A `<span>` in `Tab`, after the label, that shows the `count` prop as a pill, with `data-disabled` while the tab is disabled; only rendered when `count` is a number | none: a span inside `Tabs.Tab` | `pn-Tab-count`          | none                        |
| `panel`             | `TabsPanel`: the `<div>` of one view, shown while its tab is selected                                                                                               | `Tabs.Panel`                   | `pn-TabsPanel`          | none                        |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring on a tab or the open panel: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws, not an element                                                 | `Tabs.Tab`, `Tabs.Panel`       | none                    | none                        |

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/tabs`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part     | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Perron sets                                                                                                             | Passed through                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tabs.Root`      | `<div>`, with `data-orientation` and `data-activation-direction`                                                                                                                                                                                | `className` (`pn-Tabs`, then the caller's), `ref`, `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange` adapted from `onChange` | `render`, `style` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                                                                  |

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

A tab's value is a `string`, with `null` for no tab selected, rather than Base UI's untyped `Tabs.Tab.Value`. Mylder's tabs name views (`'departures'`, `'lines'`), a name survives the tabs being reordered where an index doesn't, and a string union narrows in the caller's `onChange`. Base UI's own `defaultValue` default, `0`, then never matches a tab, so leaving `defaultValue` out selects the first enabled tab, which is what the Default column says.

Tabs leaves out Base UI's `orientation`, so tabs only run horizontally. Mylder's tabs sit across the top of a 364 px detail panel or a sheet, where a vertical list leaves no room for the panel; the API only grows, so a later `orientation` costs nothing now, and leaving it out keeps the CSS to one direction.

`onChange` also fires for Base UI's automatic changes, with `details.reason` `'initial'`, `'disabled'` or `'missing'`, as well as for the user's (`'none'`). The contract passes Base UI's details through unchanged, and a caller that keeps the value elsewhere, such as in the URL, needs to hear the fallback; one that only wants the user's choices checks `details.reason`.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector, hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, pressed is `:active`, focus is `:focus-visible`, disabled is `[data-disabled]`, and selected is Base UI's `[data-active]` on the tab (Tabs sets no `data-selected`). Every `color` row on `tab` sets the tab's `color`, which the label takes.

A tab is `size.button` tall, as its least height, with no new `size.tab` token. `size.button` (36 px) is the height of a button of label text, which a tab is, and it clears `size.target-min`; `size.control` (34 px) is for icon buttons and chips, and `size.segment` (32 px) is the segmented control's, which a tab should not be mistaken for.

The tabs are underline tabs: no fill in any state, the label `color.text.secondary` at rest and `color.text.primary` on hover, pressed and selected, the selected tab marked by a `border.width.050` underline in `color.text.primary`, on a `border.width.025` hairline in `color.border.subtle` under the whole list. [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#border-widths) gives `border.width.050` to "the selected state of a control"; `color.text.primary` is the neutral intent's mark and reaches 17:1, past the 3:1 a state mark needs, where the hairline only decorates; a fill would read as the segmented control's selected segment; and the selected tab is told by its underline, not by its colour alone.

From the Base UI reference for `Tabs` and the installed `TabsRoot`, `TabsList`, `TabsTab`, `TabsPanel`, `TabsIndicator` and the composite root they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key              | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | From                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`            | Moves focus into the tab list, to the selected tab; from a tab, on to the open panel, which is focusable (`tabIndex` 0); the tab list is one tab stop                                                                     | Base UI                                                |
| `Shift+Tab`      | Moves focus back: from the panel to the selected tab, and from the list out of it                                                                                                                                         | Base UI                                                |
| `ArrowRight`     | Moves focus to the next tab, wrapping from the last to the first while `loopFocus` is on, without selecting it unless `activateOnFocus`; the previous tab under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up | Base UI                                                |
| `ArrowLeft`      | Moves focus to the previous tab, wrapping from the first to the last while `loopFocus` is on, without selecting it unless `activateOnFocus`; the next tab under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`                              | Base UI                                                |
| `Home`, `End`    | Move focus to the first and the last tab                                                                                                                                                                                  | Base UI                                                |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Select the focused tab and show its panel; nothing on a disabled tab                                                                                                                                                      | The browser's click; Base UI for a non-button `render` |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: which tab is selected, which the underline shows, is `aria-selected`; a disabled tab's tertiary colour is `aria-disabled`; the count is text in the tab's name, heard after the label; the underline itself is `presentation`.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: each panel is named by its tab through Base UI's `aria-labelledby`, and the tab list by the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which every story sets.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Tabs owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: a tab's `children` and a panel's render a string, an element and a list alike; `count` renders `0` and larger numbers alike.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: a hidden panel is unmounted, or with `keepMounted` kept `hidden` and `inert` by Base UI; Tabs keeps no copy for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: native `<button>`s from `Tabs.Tab`, and Base UI's `tablist`, `tab` and `tabpanel` roles with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby`, with ARIA from the caller only for the list's name.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Tab goes from the selected tab to its panel, and the arrow keys move through the tabs in document order; Tabs opens and closes nothing, and focus stays on the tab it selects.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is a tab with a one-word label, `size.button` (36 px) tall and its label plus `space.300` on each side wide.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Tabs has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as a tab's `children`, a panel's content, or the list's `aria-label`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's tabs already give the one tab stop, the roving `tabIndex`, the arrow, Home and End keys, the wrap, manual activation, the first-enabled fallback and the tab and panel ARIA, so the components rebuild none of it and add no key handlers.
- **CR-2.** `TabsList`, `Tab` and `TabsPanel` only render inside a `Tabs`: Base UI's parts read its context. Every story renders them in one, and the `Default` story's args hold a whole set, a list of tabs and a panel for each, so the contract story renders it alone.
- **CR-3.** Each of the four takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `disabled`, `count`, `slotProps`; an inherited Base UI prop such as `activateOnFocus` or `keepMounted` stays in `rest`, keeping Base UI's default), and merges `className` after its own `pn-` class; `ref` reaches its one element.
- **CR-4.** `Tabs` adapts Base UI's `onValueChange(value, details)` into `onChange(details.event, value, details)` inside itself and exposes neither `onValueChange` nor `orientation`. It passes `defaultValue` on only when the caller gives one, so Base UI's first-enabled fallback runs when it is left out, and with no destructuring default its JSDoc says `@default The first enabled tab`, as the Props table gives it.
- **CR-5.** `TabsList` renders one `Tabs.Indicator` after its `children`, with `slotProps.indicator` merged by `mergeProps`, the component's own props last. The list is `position: relative` and the indicator `position: absolute` at the block end of the selected tab's row, so it covers the list's hairline only when that tab is on the last row (CR-11), its `left` and `width` read from Base UI's `--active-tab-left` and `--active-tab-width`, its underline drawn as a `border-block-end`, never a background, so Windows' forced colours keep it.
- **CR-6.** No rule sets `display` on the indicator or on a panel: Base UI hides both with the `hidden` attribute (the indicator until the selected tab is measured, a panel while its tab isn't selected), and a `display` would show them. The panel being left is the one exception to `hidden`: Base UI keeps it mounted, without `hidden` and with `data-ending-style`, until its exit animations end, a frame at least with none, so `.pn-TabsPanel[data-ending-style]` sets `position: absolute` and `visibility: hidden`, taking it out of the flow and out of sight meanwhile, and the new panel never paints below it.
- **CR-7.** The states keep the tab's geometry: hover, pressed, focus, selected and disabled change colours only, never the height, padding, gap, typography or weight, so selecting a tab never moves its neighbours or the underline.
- **CR-8.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the hover colour in a rule outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a disabled tab: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]`, since a disabled tab has `aria-disabled`, not the native `disabled`, and still matches `:hover` and `:active`. Selected is `.pn-Tab[data-active]`, one class then attributes.
- **CR-9.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`, on the tab and on the open panel; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline.
- **CR-10.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a tab's state change or the underline's move, so the CSS has no transition, and the underline jumps to the selected tab.
- **CR-11.** When the tabs outrun the list's width, they wrap onto another row (`flex-wrap: wrap` on the list, each tab's label kept on one line with `white-space: nowrap`), rather than the list scrolling sideways. [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) lets only the map scroll sideways at 320 px, Mylder's tab sets are two to four short words, and Base UI's indicator follows the selected tab onto any row.
- **CR-12.** The count is rendered only when `count` is a number, `0` included, and its text joins the tab's accessible name after the label with a space between, "Disruptions 2", which a `play` test checks; the space is in the markup, not only a CSS gap, which the name leaves out.
- **CR-13.** In `@media (forced-colors: active)`, a disabled tab and its count take `GrayText`, and the underline and the hairline keep their borders in the system colours, so the selected and disabled states still show.
- **CR-14.** Tabs sizes to its container: the root and the list are as wide as the box that holds them, and the tabs sit at the list's inline start. The panel's padding and its place in the detail panel belong to the pattern that uses it.

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                  | Don't                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use Tabs to switch between views of one thing, such as a stop's departures, lines and disruptions                                                   | Use Tabs to filter or sort one view, such as departures by mode: a segmented control or filter chips change a view, tabs change which one   |
| Name the tab list with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as the stop's name, so a screen reader tells it from the next one                    | Leave the list unnamed beside another set of tabs                                                                                           |
| Keep each label to a word or two, in sentence case: "Departures", "Planned works"                                                                   | Write a sentence on a tab, or put a count in the label's text: give it as `count`, so every count has one shape                             |
| Give every `Tab` a `TabsPanel` with the same `value`                                                                                                | Leave a tab without a panel: its `aria-controls` points at nothing, and selecting it shows nothing                                          |
| Show a tab whose view is empty, and say so in its panel with an [EmptyState](empty-state.md) or a [DataStatePanel](../patterns/data-state-panel.md) | Disable a tab because its view has no data: a disabled tab can't say why, and the empty view is what Mylder should tell                     |
| Use `keepMounted` on a panel that holds state the caller would lose, such as a scrolled list                                                        | Keep every panel mounted by default: hidden panels still render, and update with the live data                                              |
| Link to another screen with a [LinkButton](link-button.md)                                                                                          | Use tabs as navigation between pages: a tab selects a panel on this screen, and a link is what goes elsewhere                               |
| Let the tabs size to their labels and wrap on a narrow screen                                                                                       | Set the list to scroll sideways or give the tabs fixed widths: only the map scrolls sideways, and a translated label outgrows a fixed width |
