title: MapTooltip
markdown:
# MapTooltip

The map's hover card: a small inverse card of the caller's words, placed against a point on the map or an element, shown while the pointer rests on a vehicle or a stop.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens and the Base UI reference. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/MapTooltip`. Family: Tooltips. Shared parts: none (the card holds the caller's words and draws no mark of its own).

MapTooltip is a controlled card with no trigger: it is placed against its `anchorEl` (a virtual element at a point the map projects, or an element) and opened and closed by the caller through `open`, so it composes `Tooltip.Root`, `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Positioner` and `Tooltip.Popup` and not `Tooltip.Provider` or `Tooltip.Trigger`, which the build takes out of the entry's `baseUiParts`. The vehicles and stops are drawn on the map canvas, not as elements a `Tooltip.Trigger` could wrap, so only the map knows what is under the pointer; and without triggers there is no hover delay for a `Tooltip.Provider` to share.

The popup is the component's root, taking `ref`, `className`, `style`, `render` and the rest props. `Tooltip.Root`'s props other than `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` (as `onClose`) are not offered, and `slotProps` has keys for the portal and the positioner only. The popup is the element the eye sees and the one a caller restyles, and `Tooltip.Root` renders no element; its other props (`actionsRef`, `handle`, `triggerId`, `trackCursorAxis`, `disabled`, `disableHoverablePopup`, `onOpenChangeComplete`) serve triggers, cursor tracking and exit animations this card doesn't have.

The card leaves out Base UI's `Tooltip.Arrow` and `Tooltip.Viewport`. The Tooltips family draws no arrow, and the content swaps at once, with no transition for a viewport to run (see Component rules).

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                             | Base UI part         | Class                      | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The card: an inverse box that holds the caller's `children`, a block that wraps its text                               | `Tooltip.Popup`      | `pn-MapTooltip`            | none            |
| `positioner`        | Not drawn: the box Base UI places against the anchor, above it by default, and that carries the stacking               | `Tooltip.Positioner` | `pn-MapTooltip-positioner` | `positioner`    |
| `portal`            | Not drawn: the `<div>` Base UI appends to `<body>` while the card is open, so no panel's overflow or stacking clips it | `Tooltip.Portal`     | `pn-MapTooltip-portal`     | `portal`        |

`Tooltip.Root` groups the parts and holds the open state; it renders no element, so it has no layer, class or `slotProps` key.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/tooltip`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part         | Renders                                                                                                                                                                     | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Passed through                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tooltip.Root`       | No element                                                                                                                                                                  | `open` and `defaultOpen` from MapTooltip's props, and `onOpenChange`, turned into `onClose(event, reason, details)` when it reports `false`                                                                 | none                                                                                                                                               |
| `Tooltip.Portal`     | A `<div>` appended to `<body>`, rendered only while the card is open                                                                                                        | `className` (`pn-MapTooltip-portal`, then the caller's)                                                                                                                                                     | `slotProps.portal`: `container`, `keepMounted` and the rest of its props                                                                           |
| `Tooltip.Positioner` | A `<div role="presentation">`, placed by Base UI, with `data-side`, `data-align`, `data-open` or `data-closed`, `data-anchor-hidden`, and the `--available-width` variables | `className` (`pn-MapTooltip-positioner`, then the caller's), `anchor` from MapTooltip's `anchorEl`, and the defaults `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` (see Props), which `slotProps.positioner` replaces | `slotProps.positioner`: `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and the rest of its props |
| `Tooltip.Popup`      | A `<div tabindex="-1">` with no role, with `data-side`, `data-align`, `data-open` or `data-closed`, `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and `data-instant`           | `className` (`pn-MapTooltip`, then the caller's), `ref`, and the caller's `children`                                                                                                                        | `render`, `style`, `id`, `onPointerEnter`, `onPointerLeave` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                                 |

Base UI already does: it renders the card only while it is open; it places the card against the anchor, on the side asked for, flipping to the opposite side when that one has no room and shifting it along the edge so it stays inside the viewport; it re-reads the anchor when an ancestor scrolls, the anchor or the card resizes or the layout shifts, though not on every frame; it marks the positioner `data-anchor-hidden` when the anchor is out of view or a virtual one measures nothing (a 0 by 0 rect at 0, 0); it reports Esc, from anywhere in the document while the card is open, as `onOpenChange(false)` with the reason `'escape-key'`, and a press outside the card as `'outside-press'`; it leaves the card readable but out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) and makes the positioner `inert` while the card is closed; and it sets the variables `--available-width` and `--available-height`, the room between the anchor and the viewport's edge.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

The prop that places the card is named `anchorEl`, MUI Popper's name for what a popper sits against, and it is required. MUI's `anchorEl` takes an element or a virtual element, an object whose `getBoundingClientRect()` gives a point with no element behind it, as this one does. Its type is Base UI's for `Tooltip.Positioner`'s `anchor` without `undefined`, since the prop is required, onto which it maps one to one, so it also takes a ref and a function. It is not named `anchor`, because Sheet, MapTooltip's sibling in Overlays, already ships `anchor` as the edge it slides from (Sheet CR-3), and one name has one type and default across the library. With no trigger, a card without an anchor has nothing to sit against.

MapTooltip leaves out `onOpen`. Nothing inside the component opens the card: Base UI reports an opening only from a trigger's hover or focus, and MapTooltip has no trigger, so an `onOpen` would never fire. It can join later as an optional prop without a break.

MapTooltip leaves the side and alignment to `slotProps.positioner`, keeping Base UI's `side` of `'top'` and `align` of `'center'`, and sets two defaults read in script, since Base UI takes numbers: a `sideOffset` of `space.200` and a `collisionPadding` of `size.panel-gap`. Their pixel lengths are read at run time from the tokens' custom properties, `--perron-space-200` and `--perron-size-panel-gap`, in the document's computed style, because the tokens' `numeric` values in `@mylder/perron/tokens.ts` sit outside the package build's `rootDir`, so a component under `src/` cannot import them. A card above the point leaves the vehicle under the pointer in view, `space.200` keeps it clear of the largest dot, and `size.panel-gap` keeps it as far from the screen edge as the panels are; a caller who needs another side gives it through `slotProps.positioner`, which the contract makes the way inside.

| Name                   | Type                                                                                                                 | Default | Base UI prop                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `children`             | `ReactNode`                                                                                                          | none    | none                             | The card's content: a few words on what is under the pointer, in sentence case, such as "Bus 5C to Husum". It takes the card's inverse text colour.                                                                      |
| `anchorEl`             | `Element \| VirtualElement \| React.RefObject<Element \| null> \| (() => Element \| VirtualElement \| null) \| null` | none    | `anchor` on `Tooltip.Positioner` | Required. What the card sits against: a virtual element whose `getBoundingClientRect()` gives the point the map projects for a vehicle or stop, or an element. Pass a new one when the point moves, so the card follows. |
| `open`                 | `boolean`                                                                                                            | none    | `open`                           | Whether the card is shown. Set it while the pointer rests on what the card describes, and clear it in `onClose`.                                                                                                         |
| `defaultOpen`          | `boolean`                                                                                                            | `false` | `defaultOpen`                    | Whether the card is shown at first, when `open` is not set.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `onClose`              | `(event, reason, details) => void`                                                                                   | none    | `onOpenChange`                   | Called when the card asks to close: `reason` is `'escape-key'` on Esc or `'outside-press'` on a press outside it, and `details.cancel()` keeps it open.                                                                  |
| `render`               | Base UI's `render`                                                                                                   | none    | inherited                        | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                |
| `className`            | `string \| ((state: Tooltip.Popup.State) => string \| undefined)`                                                    | none    | inherited                        | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.                                                                                                                     |
| `style`                | `CSSProperties \| ((state: Tooltip.Popup.State) => CSSProperties \| undefined)`                                      | none    | inherited                        | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.                                                                                                                  |
| `ref`                  | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                                                                                | none    | none                             | Reaches the root, the card.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.portal`     | `Tooltip.Portal.Props`                                                                                               | none    | `Tooltip.Portal`                 | Props for the `portal` part, such as `container` to render the card inside the map's own element.                                                                                                                        |
| `slotProps.positioner` | `Tooltip.Positioner.Props`                                                                                           | none    | `Tooltip.Positioner`             | Props for the `positioner` part, such as `side`, `align` or `sideOffset`. Its `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` replace MapTooltip's defaults.                                                                         |

`MapTooltipProps` extends `Tooltip.Popup.Props` without its `children` and `ref`, so `render`, `className` and `style` are inherited with Base UI's JSDoc, and declares `children`, `anchorEl`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onClose`, `ref` and `slotProps`. No `variant`, `size` or `color`: the card has one look, the Tooltips family's. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop. None of the names is one the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table bans; `onOpenChange` stays inside the component.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The card has one design state, open: it renders only while open, and takes no hover, focus, press, selection or disabled look, since it holds no control. Rest below is the open card.

The card takes the Tooltips family's treatment: `color.surface.inverse` with `color.text.inverse`, no shadow, no border, `radius.md`, text in `typography.label-sm`. The positioner takes `z-index.dialog`, as the contract's CSS section asks of everything that renders in a portal, so a dialog opened after the card paints over it; the screen's `z-index.tooltip` is a pattern's token, outside a component's [families](README.md#token-families).

The card is padded `space.150` on the block axis and `space.200` on the inline axis. The family sets no padding; `space.150` above and below keeps a line of `typography.label-sm` and a `size.badge` line badge comfortable, and `space.200` at the sides matches the offset from the point.

The card's width follows its content, capped at `--available-width`, Base UI's room between the anchor and the viewport's edge, with no token for a largest width. The card holds a few words, and the cap keeps it on screen at 320 px wide; a fixed largest width would need a new token through the `design-tokens` skill for no use yet.

In forced colours, the card draws a `border.width.025` outline in `CanvasText`, so its edge still shows on the map. Forced colours replace the inverse fill with `Canvas`, the map's own colour there, and an outline, unlike a border, keeps the card's size.

When Base UI marks the positioner `data-anchor-hidden`, the card is hidden with `visibility: hidden` until its anchor is back in view. The card speaks of a point the reader can no longer see, such as a vehicle panned off the map.

| Part         | State          | Property                 | Token                                                                          |
| ------------ | -------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `positioner` | rest           | `z-index`                | `z-index.dialog`                                                               |
| `positioner` | anchor hidden  | `visibility`             | `hidden`, on `[data-anchor-hidden]`                                            |
| `root`       | rest           | `background-color`       | `color.surface.inverse`                                                        |
| `root`       | rest           | `color`                  | `color.text.inverse`                                                           |
| `root`       | rest           | `font`, `letter-spacing` | `typography.label-sm`, with its tracking twin                                  |
| `root`       | rest           | `border-radius`          | `radius.md`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `padding-block`          | `space.150`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `padding-inline`         | `space.200`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `max-inline-size`        | `var(--available-width)`, Base UI's variable                                   |
| `root`       | rest           | `box-shadow`             | `none`                                                                         |
| `root`       | forced colours | `outline`                | `border.width.025` solid `CanvasText`, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)` |

The defaults MapTooltip gives the positioner in script, read from the tokens' custom properties at run time:

| Part         | State | Property           | Token            |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------ | ---------------- |
| `positioner` | rest  | `sideOffset`       | `space.200`      |
| `positioner` | rest  | `collisionPadding` | `size.panel-gap` |

Hover, highlighted, focus, pressed, disabled, selected and invalid don't apply: the card is not a control. Base UI's `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` take no look, as the card has no transition.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Tooltip` and the installed `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipPositioner`, `TooltipPopup` and the dismiss hook they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key      | Does                                                                                                                                                                                     | From    |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `Escape` | While the card is open, from anywhere in the document: calls `onClose(event, 'escape-key', details)`; an uncontrolled card closes, a controlled one closes when the caller clears `open` | Base UI |

No other key: the card is out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) and holds no control, so Tab passes it by. Opening it from the keyboard is the map's, which moves focus between vehicles in the vehicle list rather than on the canvas.

The card keeps no role and stays in the accessibility tree, with neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-hidden`. Base UI sets no role on `Tooltip.Popup`, and `role="tooltip"` describes a trigger through `aria-describedby`, which the card has none of; left readable, a screen reader's reading cursor still finds its words, while the map's text alternative, the vehicle list, carries the same facts.

| Element      | Role                                   | Accessible name from                  | States announced |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `positioner` | `presentation`, from Base UI           | none                                  | none             |
| `root`       | none: a `<div>` that reads as its text | none: its `children` are read as text | none             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the card shows only the caller's `children`, read as text in the accessibility tree; it draws no mark, and the facts it shows are also in the vehicle list and the detail panel, the map's text alternative.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the card is not a landmark or a region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the card owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders a string, an element and a list alike, as the `Content` story shows.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the card leaves the document when it closes, and Base UI makes the positioner `inert` while it is closed.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a plain `<div>` for words, with no role, since the card is neither a control nor a description tied to one.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the card never takes focus, so opening and closing it leaves focus where it was.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: none here; the card takes no press.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the card has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word on the card comes from the caller, as `children`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** MapTooltip renders `Tooltip.Root`, then `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Positioner` and `Tooltip.Popup`, and no `Tooltip.Provider`, `Tooltip.Trigger`, `Tooltip.Arrow` or `Tooltip.Viewport`. The caller opens and closes it; the component adds no pointer or key handlers of its own.
- **CR-2.** Base UI already places the card, flips and shifts it inside the viewport, re-reads the anchor on scroll, resize and layout shift, reports Esc and a press outside, and marks the hidden anchor, so the component rebuilds none of it.
- **CR-3.** The popup is the root: `{...rest}` comes before its own attributes, `ref` reaches it, and `className` is merged after `pn-MapTooltip`. `children`, `anchorEl`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onClose` and `slotProps` are taken out of `rest` first, so none reaches the `<div>`.
- **CR-4.** `onOpenChange(open, details)` is adapted once, inside the component: when `open` is `false` it calls `onClose(details.event, details.reason, details)`; MapTooltip exposes no `onOpenChange`, and `onClose` is never called for an opening.
- **CR-5.** `slotProps.portal` and `slotProps.positioner` are spread through `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), the component's own props last, so the positioner's `anchor` is MapTooltip's `anchorEl`; the portal has no props of the component's own to merge, so its `mergeProps` call, kept in the form Dialog uses, passes the caller's props as they are. Each part's class is set after the merge, by `withClass`, because `mergeProps` joins class strings rightmost first and joins only strings, not a function of state: `pn-MapTooltip-portal` and `pn-MapTooltip-positioner` come first, then the caller's `className`, a string or a function of the part's state. The positioner's `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` are defaults: the component passes `space.200` and `size.panel-gap` only when `slotProps.positioner` gives none, reading their pixel lengths in script from the tokens' custom properties, `--perron-space-200` and `--perron-size-panel-gap`, in the document's computed style, never a literal. With no document, as on a server, or before a token stylesheet has given both properties in pixels, it passes neither, so Base UI's own defaults apply, and it keeps the first reading that gives both for the life of the page.
- **CR-6.** The positioner takes `z-index.dialog`, and hides the card with `visibility: hidden` while it carries `[data-anchor-hidden]`.
- **CR-7.** The card's look is the Tooltips family's and nothing more: `color.surface.inverse`, `color.text.inverse`, `radius.md`, `typography.label-sm` with its tracking twin, no shadow and no border. The family sets no padding, so the card's is its own: `space.150` on the block axis and `space.200` on the inline axis. Its text wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`) inside `max-inline-size: var(--available-width)`, with `box-sizing: border-box` so the padding stays inside that cap, and its width otherwise follows its content.
- **CR-8.** The card is a block: `children` flow as the caller writes them, and the component sets no flex or grid on them. Content takes the card's colour through `currentColor`.
- **CR-9.** Opening and closing are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a hover card, so the CSS has no transition or animation, and `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` take no look.
- **CR-10.** In forced colours the card draws a `border.width.025` solid `CanvasText` outline, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, so its geometry doesn't change.
- **CR-11.** The popup keeps no role and no `aria-hidden`, and the component adds none.

## Stories

The deferred drawing has no variant property and no `State`: the card has one look and one design state, open, so its one variant is `Default` (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). The other stories are behaviour, which the `play` tests check.

The meta sets `parameters: { docs: { story: { inline: false, height: '480px' } } }`, since the card portals to `<body>`, and each story renders in its own frame. A virtual anchor in a story is a point inside the frame, such as `{ getBoundingClientRect: () => DOMRect.fromRect({ x: 240, y: 240, width: 0, height: 0 }) }`, never one at 0, 0, which Base UI reads as hidden, except in the two stories that test the hidden anchor: `AnchorHidden`, at 0, 0, and `MovingPoint`, whose point leaves the frame. Each `play` finds the card through `screen`, outside `canvasElement`, and ends with it closed.

| Story          | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`      | The subject story: the card open (`defaultOpen`) against a virtual point, with one line of text, "Bus 5C to Husum"; its args pass every rule alone                                                            | The card has `pn-MapTooltip`, no role, and the text; its positioner has `data-side="top"`, and the card's bottom edge sits above the point; Esc with `details.cancel()` in `onClose` leaves the card open; Esc again calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and the card leaves the document                                                                                              |
| `Controlled`   | The card with `open` held in the story's state, against an element (a small dot standing in for a stop), beside a button "Show the card" that opens it again                                                  | Esc calls `onClose` once with `'escape-key'` and the story clears `open`; the button opens it again; a press outside the card calls `onClose` with `'outside-press'`; focus stays on the button throughout; ends closed                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Content`      | The card open against a virtual point, with an element and a list as `children`: a bold line, "Bus 5C to Husum", and a second line, "Live, on time"                                                           | Both lines render inside the card in `color.text.inverse`, and the card stays inside the viewport                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `NearTopEdge`  | The card open against a virtual point near the top of the frame, where there is no room above it                                                                                                              | The positioner flips to `data-side="bottom"`, and the card's top edge stays at least `size.panel-gap` from the top of the viewport                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `MovingPoint`  | The card with `open` held in the story's state, against a virtual point the story holds, beside a button "Move the bus" that moves the point to another place in the frame, then off its left edge, then back | The card sits centred `space.200` above the point; Enter on the button passes a new `anchorEl`, and the same card, still open, sits centred `space.200` above the new point; Enter again moves the point off the frame, the positioner takes `data-anchor-hidden` and the card has `visibility: hidden`; Enter again brings the point back, and the card shows above it; Esc closes it |
| `AnchorHidden` | The card open (`defaultOpen`) against a virtual point that measures nothing, 0 by 0 at 0, 0, as a map gives before it has projected the vehicle                                                               | The positioner has `data-anchor-hidden`, and the card has `visibility: hidden` and is not visible (CR-6); Esc calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and the card leaves the document                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                 | Don't                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open the card while a mouse pointer rests on a vehicle or a stop, and select it on a tap or a click, opening its detail panel      | Open the card on touch: a tap has no hover, and Accessibility asks that anything shown on hover is also reached by selecting the item             |
| Keep the card open while the pointer is over it, using the card's `onPointerEnter` and `onPointerLeave`, and close it in `onClose` | Close it the moment the pointer leaves the dot: Accessibility asks that a hover card stays while the pointer is over it                           |
| Give a few words: the line and its destination, the data state                                                                     | Put a link, a button or a field in the card: it is out of the tab order, so the keys can't reach them; use a panel or a popover                   |
| Pass a new `anchorEl` when the vehicle moves, so the card moves with it                                                            | Expect the card to follow a moving point on its own: Base UI re-reads the anchor on scroll, resize and layout shift, not on every frame           |
| Let the card's words take its inverse colour, and use components that draw their own colours on a fill, such as a line badge       | Put text that sets its own secondary or tertiary colour in the card: those colours are measured on light surfaces, not on `color.surface.inverse` |
| Give the same facts in the vehicle list or the detail panel                                                                        | Put anything only in the card: screen reader, keyboard and touch users never see it                                                               |
| Change the side through `slotProps.positioner`, such as `side: 'bottom'`                                                           | Move the card with a margin or a `transform`: Base UI's placement and flipping no longer match what is drawn                                      |
| Show one card at a time                                                                                                            | Open a card for each vehicle at once: the cards cover the map they describe                                                                       |

# Sheet

A panel that slides in from the edge of the screen and floats over the map: the overview sheet and the detail panel on a wide screen, and the bottom sheet they become on a phone ([Layout](../foundations/layout.md#page-shell)).

The design is deferred (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides the variant property, the parts and the token of every part, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens and the Base UI reference. A later design run can change them.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Sheet`. Family: `Panels`. Shared parts: `CloseButton`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                          | Base UI part                                                    | Class               | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The panel itself: the dialog, holding the header and the content                                    | `Drawer.Popup`                                                  | `pn-Sheet`          | none            |
| `trigger`           | The caller's button that opens the sheet, when the caller gives one                                 | `Drawer.Trigger`                                                | none: the caller's  | `trigger`       |
| `portal`            | Moves the sheet to the end of `<body>`, or to the caller's container; draws nothing                 | `Drawer.Portal`                                                 | none                | `portal`        |
| `backdrop`          | The scrim behind a modal sheet; not rendered when the sheet is not modal                            | `Drawer.Backdrop`                                               | `pn-Sheet-backdrop` | `backdrop`      |
| `viewport`          | The fixed layer that places the panel against its edge, `size.panel-gap` in from the screen's edges | `Drawer.Viewport`                                               | `pn-Sheet-viewport` | `viewport`      |
| `header`            | The row along the top of the panel: the title, then the close button                                | none: a `div` that only lays out the title and the close button | `pn-Sheet-header`   | none            |
| `title`             | The sheet's name, the heading that labels the dialog                                                | `Drawer.Title`                                                  | `pn-Sheet-title`    | `title`         |
| `close`             | The icon button that closes the sheet, the `CloseButton` shared part                                | `Drawer.Close`                                                  | `pn-Sheet-close`    | `close`         |
| `content`           | The caller's children, below the header; it scrolls on its own, so the header stays in place        | `Drawer.Content`                                                | `pn-Sheet-content`  | `content`       |

`Drawer.Description` is not one of the sheet's parts: `packages/perron/components.json` leaves it out, and a sheet's body is the caller's own content.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/drawer`, at the version pinned in `package.json`.

| Base UI part      | Renders                      | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Passed through                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Drawer.Root`     | Nothing                      | `open`, `defaultOpen`; `onOpenChange`, adapted into `onOpen` and `onClose`; `modal`; `disablePointerDismissal`, true while `modal` is false; `swipeDirection` from `anchor`; the snap point props with `anchor` `'bottom'`                                                                                                        | The sheet's own props in the Props table; `handle`, `actionsRef`, `triggerId`, `defaultTriggerId`, `onOpenChangeComplete` and `snapToSequentialPoints` are not exposed |
| `Drawer.Trigger`  | `<button>`                   | `render` from `trigger`; rendered only when `trigger` is given                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `slotProps.trigger`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Drawer.Portal`   | `<div>`                      | Nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `slotProps.portal`: `container`, `keepMounted`                                                                                                                         |
| `Drawer.Backdrop` | `<div>`                      | `className` `pn-Sheet-backdrop`; rendered only while `modal` is true                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `slotProps.backdrop`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Drawer.Viewport` | `<div>`                      | `className` `pn-Sheet-viewport`, `data-anchor`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `slotProps.viewport`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Drawer.Popup`    | `<div>`, role `dialog`       | `ref`, `className` `pn-Sheet` then the caller's, `data-anchor`, the rest props first                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The rest props: `initialFocus`, `finalFocus`, `render`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*` and the HTML attributes                                                      |
| `Drawer.Content`  | `<div>`                      | `className` `pn-Sheet-content`, `children`; `tabIndex` 0 while the content overflows, its `scrollHeight` greater than its `clientHeight`, watched with a `ResizeObserver` on the body and each block in it, which a `MutationObserver` watches again when the body's children change, and merged after `slotProps.content` (CR-2) | `slotProps.content`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Drawer.Title`    | `<h2>`                       | `className` `pn-Sheet-title`, `title` as its children                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `slotProps.title`                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Drawer.Close`    | `<button>`, as `CloseButton` | `className` `pn-Sheet-close`, rendered through the `CloseButton` part with the owned `close` string as its label                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `slotProps.close`                                                                                                                                                      |

Base UI already does: the `dialog` role and its name from the title through `aria-labelledby`; `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on the trigger; moving focus to the popup on open (Drawer's `initialFocus` defaults to the popup, unlike Dialog's) and back to the trigger or the element focused before on close; trapping focus, locking the page's scroll and hiding everything outside from assistive technology with `aria-hidden` while modal; closing the topmost sheet on Esc; closing a modal sheet on a press outside it; swipe to dismiss in `swipeDirection`, with `data-swiping`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`, `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` and `--drawer-swipe-strength`; snapping a bottom sheet to its snap points, with `--drawer-snap-point-offset`; `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` for the open and close transitions; letting a mouse select text inside `Drawer.Content` without starting a swipe; and the `hidden` attribute on a closed popup kept mounted.

- The root's glass, border, radius and shadow are the Panels family's row in the contract, and `typography.heading-md` is the role [Typography](../foundations/typography.md) gives panel titles. A bottom sheet is opaque because [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts panels full of text on `color.surface.default` on phones, where bottom sheets are.
- The `close` rows belong to the `CloseButton` part: the sheet places it, and the part draws it (CR-11).
- The sheet's geometry: a side sheet is `size.sheet-width` wide and the viewport's full height, `size.panel-gap` from the screen's edges; a bottom sheet is the viewport's full width, flush with the bottom and side edges, and `size.panel-gap` short of the top at full height; the header is padded `space.400` at the top and sides with `space.300` between the title and the close button; the content sits `space.300` below the header and is padded `space.400` at the sides and bottom, as the rows above give them.
- Side sheets slide in and out on `duration.sheet` and `easing.sheet` too, though the tokens' descriptions name only the bottom sheet, so every sheet moves alike ([Motion](../foundations/motion.md): "The sheet slides").
- The `CloseButton` part has no folder yet, so Sheet, the first component that composes it, decides its look: an icon button `size.control` square with `radius.md`, the `close` icon at `icon.size.400` (its size in `packages/perron/icons/icons.json`) in `color.text.secondary`, turning `color.text.primary` on `color.surface.hover` on hover and `color.surface.selected` when pressed, as the `close` rows above give it.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for each part. "From" says who does it: Base UI, or Perron.

| Key                | Does                                                                                                                               | From                                                  |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`   | On the trigger, opens the sheet and moves focus to the popup; Tab then reaches the close button                                    | Base UI                                               |
| `Enter`, `Space`   | On the close button, closes the sheet with reason `close-press`, and focus returns to the trigger or to the element focused before | Base UI                                               |
| `Esc`              | Closes the topmost open sheet with reason `escape-key`, and focus returns as above                                                 | Base UI                                               |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | In a modal sheet, moves through the sheet's tabbable elements and wraps inside it                                                  | Base UI                                               |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | In a sheet that is not modal, moves on into the page; the sheet stays open                                                         | Base UI, with `disablePointerDismissal` set by Perron |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | Stops on the body while it scrolls, and the arrow keys, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home` and `End` scroll it                           | Perron, with `tabIndex` 0 while the body overflows    |

| Element    | Role                 | Accessible name from                      | States announced                                                                 |
| ---------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`  | `button`             | The caller's element                      | `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, with `aria-controls` naming the popup |
| `root`     | `dialog`             | `title`, through `aria-labelledby`        | While modal, everything outside it is `aria-hidden`                              |
| `title`    | `heading`, level 2   | `title`                                   | None                                                                             |
| `close`    | `button`             | The owned `close` string, or `closeLabel` | None                                                                             |
| `backdrop` | None: presentational | None                                      | None                                                                             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the close button's icon is `aria-hidden` and the `CloseButton` part gives it the owned label; the body scrolls at every snap point and takes focus while it does, so everything in it can be reached by keys and screen readers without the grab; the close button and Esc dismiss it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the dialog is named by its required `title`, through Base UI's `aria-labelledby`.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `closeLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike, in each `anchor`: the `Left`, `Right` and `Bottom` stories' `play` tests open a sheet with an element title and a string body, a list title and an element body, and a string title and a list body, each named by its title.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; a closed sheet is unmounted, or `hidden` when `slotProps.portal.keepMounted` keeps it.
- [ ] Native semantics first: `<button>` for the trigger and the close button, `<h2>` for the title, and Base UI's `dialog` role on the root.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: title, close button, then the content; Base UI returns focus to the trigger or to the element focused before.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the close button, `size.control`.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the slide reads `duration.sheet`, which the tokens shorten to 0.01 ms.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's Drawer already handles focus moving in and back, the focus trap and scroll lock of a modal sheet, Esc, outside presses, swipes and snap points, so the component rebuilds none of them.
- **CR-2.** The root is `Drawer.Popup`: `ref`, `className` (`pn-Sheet` first, then the caller's) and the rest props reach it, the rest spread before the component's own attributes. The other parts are reached only through `slotProps`, merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last.
- **CR-3.** `anchor`, MUI Drawer's name for the edge, maps to `swipeDirection`, with no `top` until a screen needs one: `left` to `'left'`, `right` to `'right'`, `bottom` to `'down'`. The root and the viewport carry `data-anchor` with its value, the default included, and the CSS places and slides the sheet from it: `.pn-Sheet[data-anchor='bottom']`.
- **CR-4.** While `modal` is false, the component passes `disablePointerDismissal`, renders no `Drawer.Backdrop`, and the viewport takes `pointer-events: none` with the root back on `auto`, so the map under and beside the sheet stays usable. While `modal` is true, the backdrop renders with `color.scrim`, and a press on it closes the sheet with reason `outside-press`.
- **CR-5.** The viewport and the backdrop take `z-index.dialog`, as everything in a portal does. A pattern that lays a sheet among the map screen's panels sets its own `z-index.*` through `slotProps.viewport`'s `className`.
- **CR-6.** The component holds no media query for the phone: it sizes to its viewport, and the screen picks `anchor` `bottom` under `breakpoint.phone`.
- **CR-7.** The root is a flex column: the header keeps its height, and the content takes the rest, with `overflow-y: auto` and `overscroll-behavior: contain`, so a long body scrolls under a header that stays.
- **CR-8.** A side sheet moves with `transform: translateX(var(--drawer-swipe-movement-x))`, and a bottom sheet with `transform: translateY(calc(var(--drawer-snap-point-offset) + var(--drawer-swipe-movement-y)))`. Under `[data-starting-style]` and `[data-ending-style]` it sits off its edge: a side sheet by its own width and the `size.panel-gap` it keeps from the edge, `translateX(calc(-100% - size.panel-gap))` from the left and `translateX(calc(100% + size.panel-gap))` from the right, and a bottom sheet by its own height, `translateY(100%)`, with its `padding-block-end` at 0. At rest, a bottom sheet's `padding-block-end` takes the same `calc()` as its `translateY`, so the scrolling body ends on screen, and keeps on screen, at every snap point. Base UI's `--drawer-*` properties are read, never set, by the component's CSS.
- **CR-9.** The snap point props reach `Drawer.Root` only with `anchor` `bottom`. With no `snapPoints`, a bottom sheet snaps to `size.sheet-peek` and to `1`, and opens at the peek. The peek is read at runtime from the token's custom property, `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--perron-size-sheet-peek')`, a `px` string Base UI takes as a snap point, once, when a bottom sheet first renders.
- **CR-10.** `onOpen(event, details)` and `onClose(event, reason, details)` are adapted from `onOpenChange` inside the component, with `event` as `details.event` and `reason` as `details.reason`; `onSnapPointChange(event, snapPoint, details)` is adapted the same way. Neither of Base UI's callbacks is exposed.
- **CR-11.** The close button is the `CloseButton` shared part, rendered through `Drawer.Close`, after the title in the header. Its label is `useOwnedStrings({ close: closeLabel }).close`. When the part's folder does not exist yet, the build adds it, as the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) say, drawn by the `close` rows of [Tokens](#tokens), with the `close` icon from `packages/perron/icons/close.svg`.
- **CR-12.** The portal renders nothing in static markup, so the contract's `OwnedStrings` story sees only the trigger. A `play` test runs `expectOwnedStrings` over the open sheet's markup in `da`, with the story's `title` and `children` as the caller's words.
- **CR-13.** The `Left` story's args hold `defaultOpen: true`, so the contract story finds its root, the popup, with the `ref` and the `data-testid` on it.

## Stories

One per variant and state the spec decides, named by the `anchor` values. The design is deferred, so there is no Penpot export to pair them with yet.

| Story            | Shows                                                                                                | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Left`           | `anchor` `left`, with a trigger, open by `defaultOpen`, with a title and a few lines of body         | The open sheet's markup holds only owned and caller words in `da` (CR-12); Esc closes it with reason `escape-key` and focus returns to the trigger; `title` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Right`          | `anchor` `right`, with a trigger, open by `defaultOpen`                                              | Esc closes it; Enter on the trigger opens it again and focus moves to the popup, and Tab then reaches the close button; a short body takes no Tab stop, so Tab from the close button leaves the sheet, which stays open; Shift+Tab comes back; Enter on the close button closes it and focus returns to the trigger; `title` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike |
| `Bottom`         | `anchor` `bottom`, with a trigger, open at the `size.sheet-peek` snap point                          | The body at the peek ends on screen, takes focus and scrolls; `onClose` is called with reason `escape-key` on Esc, the sheet closes and focus returns to the trigger; `title` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike                                                                                                                                                |
| `BottomExpanded` | `anchor` `bottom`, with a trigger, open at `defaultSnapPoint` `1`, with a body long enough to scroll | The content scrolls and the header stays in place; Esc closes it with reason `escape-key` and focus returns to the trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Modal`          | `anchor` `left`, `modal`, with a trigger, open by `defaultOpen` over the scrim                       | A click on the backdrop closes it with reason `outside-press`; clicking the trigger opens it again; Tab wraps inside the sheet; Esc closes it and focus returns to the trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                    | Don't                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use a sheet for a panel beside the map, left open while the rider pans and picks vehicles: it is not modal by default                                 | Use a modal sheet to ask for a decision; that is a Dialog, which needs no swipe or snap points (Base UI's own advice)                              |
| Pick `anchor` `bottom` on a phone, under `breakpoint.phone`, in the screen's code                                                                     | Expect the sheet to turn into a bottom sheet on its own; it sizes to its viewport and holds no media query                                         |
| Name the sheet with `title`: the stop, line or destination it shows                                                                                   | Leave the title out, or draw a heading of your own in `children`: the dialog takes its name from `title`                                           |
| Handle `onClose` and let Esc close the topmost sheet, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) orders: a dialog, then a detail panel | Cancel every close of a sheet the rider can't otherwise leave; cancel only the reasons a screen must refuse, such as `swipe` on the overview sheet |
| Mark a horizontal carousel or slider inside a bottom sheet with `data-base-ui-swipe-ignore`, so its drags don't swipe the sheet                       | Let a control that drags sideways fight the sheet's swipe                                                                                          |
| Keep one primary action per sheet                                                                                                                     | Put two brand buttons in one sheet; a screen has one brand action at most                                                                          |

title: Delay
markdown:
# Delay

How late or early a vehicle or departure runs, as a short figure in the delay's colour, such as "+3 min", with the same thing said in words to a screen reader.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Delay`. Family: none. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so the layers below are the ones the drawing will name. Delay has no Base UI part: it is display text with no behaviour, so its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop, and its inner parts are plain elements.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                          | Base UI part                                   | Class                               | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The whole delay, one inline run of text: a `<span>` in the delay's colour                                                           | none: a `<span>` rendered by `useRender`       | `pn-Delay`                          | none            |
| `value`             | The visible figure: the signed whole minutes ("+3", "−1"), "On time", or "—" when unknown                                           | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Delay-value`                    | none            |
| `unit`              | "min", after a space, shown only after a signed figure                                                                              | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Delay-unit`                     | none            |
| `label`             | The words a screen reader hears in place of the figure: "3 min late", "1 min early", "Delay unknown". Not drawn, so no Penpot layer | none: the VisuallyHidden shared part           | `pn-VisuallyHidden`, the part's own | none            |

Delay shows a signed figure with its unit, "+3 min" late and "−1 min" early (the true minus sign), "On time" in words when on time, and "—" with no unit when unknown, as content design writes numbers: a space before units, the true minus sign for early and "—" for unknown.

Delay's one Penpot variant property is `delay`, with the values `on-time`, `slight`, `late`, `early` and `unknown`. The code map maps it to the CSS state `[data-delay]` with the same value rather than to a prop, since the component works it out from `minutes`. The variants are `OnTime`, `Slight`, `Late`, `Early` and `Unknown`, and the stories carry those names.

## Base UI parts

Delay imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props over its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                          | Passed through                                        |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`, `className` (`pn-Delay` first, then the caller's), `data-delay`, the children (CR-3, CR-4) | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style`, the rest props |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class, data attribute and children; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Delay takes no `children`: it writes its own figure and words. It has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and Delay has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root.

The delay is given as `minutes: number | null`, required, in minutes (positive late, negative early, `0` on time, `null` unknown) and rounded to the nearest whole minute, not as `value` or in seconds: the contract's `value` belongs to controls with `defaultValue` and `onChange`, and the tokens, the words and the visible figure all count whole minutes.

| Name                 | Type                   | Default      | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minutes`            | `number \| null`       | (required)   | none                 | The delay in minutes: positive when late, negative when early, `0` on time, `null` when no real-time data says (timetable only, no signal). Rounded to the nearest whole minute.          |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`     |              | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `minutesUnitLabel`   | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min", the unit after the figure                                                                                                                                                |
| `minutesLateLabel`   | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min late", heard after the number when late                                                                                                                                    |
| `minutesEarlyLabel`  | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min early", heard after the number when early                                                                                                                                  |
| `onTimeLabel`        | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "On time"                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `delayUnknownLabel`  | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "Delay unknown", heard in place of "—"                                                                                                                                          |
| `className`, `style` | React's                |              | through `mergeProps` | Reach the root; `className` is merged after `pn-Delay`                                                                                                                                    |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>` |              | `useRender`'s `ref`  | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Tokens

Delay is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row's state names the `data-delay` value it applies to. Delay is not one of the contract's families, so it draws no fill, border or radius.

Delay comes in one size, set in `typography.data`, with no `size` prop; a caller who needs it larger (beside a `typography.data-lg` countdown) sets the font through `className`. `typography.data` is the role for "times, delays, counts and percentages in lists and tables", where Delay sits, and a second size can join later as a `size` prop without a break.

| Part    | State                          | Property               | Token                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `font`                 | `typography.data`                                      |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.data-tracking`                             |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `font-variant-numeric` | none: the keyword `tabular-nums`, so figures line up   |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `white-space`          | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "+3 min" never breaks   |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='on-time'`   | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.on-time`                          |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='slight'`    | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.slight`                           |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='late'`      | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.late`                             |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='early'`     | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.early`                            |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='unknown'`   | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.unknown`                          |
| `value` | rest, every `data-delay`       | `color`                | none: inherits the root's                              |
| `unit`  | rest, `data-delay` with a unit | `color`                | none: inherits the root's                              |
| `label` | rest                           | none                   | none: the VisuallyHidden part's own styles, never seen |

The space between `value` and `unit` is a text space, as content design writes "4 min", not a gap token, so a copied delay reads "+3 min".

## Keyboard and ARIA

Delay is text: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys.

| Key  | Does                               | From   |
| ---- | ---------------------------------- | ------ |
| none | Delay is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element            | Role                         | Accessible name from                                                            | States announced |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`             | none: a generic `<span>`     | Not named; its text is read in place, as part of the row or sentence it sits in | none             |
| `value` and `unit` | hidden, `aria-hidden="true"` | Not read, except "On time", which is read as shown (CR-3)                       | none             |
| `label`            | text                         | The owned strings: "3 min late", "1 min early", "Delay unknown"                 | none             |

The visible figure is `aria-hidden`, with a VisuallyHidden label saying the delay in words: the number without its sign and then "min late" or "min early" ("3 min late", "1 min early"), and "Delay unknown" in place of "—", while "On time" is read from the visible text. A screen reader reads "+3 min" as "plus 3 min" and skips or spells "—", so the ear would get less than the eye, and an `aria-label` on a role-less `<span>` is not allowed.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the colour and sign say late, slight, early or on time; the label says "N min late" or "N min early", "On time" is read as shown, and `null` says "Delay unknown". In forced colours the colour goes, and the sign and words still carry it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; Delay is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `minutesUnitLabel`, `minutesLateLabel`, `minutesEarlyLabel`, `onTimeLabel` and `delayUnknownLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `minutes` is a number or `null`; positive, negative, zero, fractional (rounded), `NaN` and infinite (both unknown, CR-1) all render, and a story's `play` test covers each kind.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; Delay does not animate. The visible figure is `aria-hidden` because the label speaks for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<span>`, with no role and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` on the figure the label replaces.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Delay takes no focus.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Delay is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Delay has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word Delay shows or announces is its own; the caller gives only `minutes`. The number is never part of a string: it renders as its own text run beside the word, so the dictionaries stay plain strings (CR-3).

| Key            | English         | Override            | Seen or heard where                                         |
| -------------- | --------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minutesUnit`  | "min"           | `minutesUnitLabel`  | `unit`, seen after a signed figure, "+3 min"; `aria-hidden` |
| `minutesLate`  | "min late"      | `minutesLateLabel`  | `label`, heard after the number when late: "3 min late"     |
| `minutesEarly` | "min early"     | `minutesEarlyLabel` | `label`, heard after the number when early: "1 min early"   |
| `onTime`       | "On time"       | `onTimeLabel`       | `value`, seen and heard when `minutes` rounds to `0`        |
| `delayUnknown` | "Delay unknown" | `delayUnknownLabel` | `label`, heard in place of "—" when `minutes` is `null`     |

No key in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` says any of these, so all five are new, each with a JSDoc line like its neighbours.

"On time" and "Delay unknown" join the data-state and delay words table in `docs/content-design.md`, with their Danish, Swedish and Norwegian, so every screen says a delay the same way; content design says delays always use the words in that table, and its test then holds the locale files to them. "min", "min late" and "min early" stay out of it, as parts of a number's phrase rather than words a screen shows on their own.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** Delay works out its kind from `minutes` after rounding it with `Math.round`: `null`, `NaN` or an infinite number is `unknown`; `0` (and `-0`) is `on-time`; `1` or `2` is `slight`; `3` or more is `late`; `-1` or less is `early`. Early has no slight step. These are the bounds the `color.transit.delay.*` tokens describe.
- **CR-2.** The visible figure is "+N" when late and "−N" when early, with U+2212, never a hyphen-minus, then a text space and the `minutesUnit` word in `unit`. On time, `value` is the `onTime` word and there is no `unit`. Unknown, `value` is "—" (U+2014) and there is no `unit`.
- **CR-3.** When late, early or unknown, `value` and `unit` are `aria-hidden="true"` and the VisuallyHidden `label` holds the words: the number without its sign, a space and `minutesLate` or `minutesEarly`, or `delayUnknown` alone. The number and each word are separate text runs, so `expectOwnedStrings` reads the words as dictionary values. On time, `value` is read as shown and there is no `label`.
- **CR-4.** The root always carries `data-delay` with the kind from CR-1, `on-time`, `slight`, `late`, `early` or `unknown`, and the CSS reads the colour from it, as [Tokens](#tokens) gives.
- **CR-5.** Delay takes no data state. A caller showing a timetable-only or no-signal vehicle passes `minutes={null}`, as [Data states](../foundations/data-states.md#delays) says those always show an unknown delay.
- **CR-6.** Delay is not a live region. A screen that updates delays announces changes of state in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) asks.
- **CR-7.** Delay composes the VisuallyHidden shared part from its folder in `packages/perron/src/`, and never draws its own hiding styles. If no earlier component has added the part yet, Delay's build adds it, as the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) table already describes it.
- **CR-8.** The root renders through `useRender` with `mergeProps`: Delay's own props (`className` starting with `pn-Delay`, `data-delay`, the children) win over the caller's rest props, and `minutes` and every `*Label` prop are taken out of the rest before the merge, so none reaches the DOM.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named as CR-1's kinds in PascalCase. Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree, not the pixels.
