| `style`     | `CSSProperties`                                                                                 |              | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ref`       | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>`                                                                          |              | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

`line` is named and typed exactly as LineBadge's `line` prop: whichever of the two is built second takes the other's name and type. No `slotProps`: the root is the only part. No label props: the component owns no strings (see [Owned strings](#owned-strings)). No `children`: the marker holds nothing, so the props type leaves `children` out.

## Tokens

One row per part, variant, line and property. StationIcon is not interactive, so its only design state is rest. The CSS sets `color` to the line's token and draws the ring, and the `filled` dot, in `currentColor`.

| Part                         | State | Property                    | Token                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`, `size='small'`       | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.325`                                                                                                 |
| `root`, `size='medium'`      | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400`                                                                                                 |
| `root`, `size='large'`       | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.450`                                                                                                 |
| `root`                       | rest  | `inline-size`, `block-size` | `--perron-icon-size`, the size's `icon.size.*`                                                                  |
| `root`                       | rest  | `border-width`              | `border.width.050`                                                                                              |
| `root`                       | rest  | `border-radius`             | `radius.full`                                                                                                   |
| `root`                       | rest  | `border-color`              | `currentColor`, the line's colour below                                                                         |
| `root`, `variant='outlined'` | rest  | `background`                | `color.surface.raised`, so it hides a stop timeline's rail running behind it, as the map fills a station's ring |
| `root`, `variant='filled'`   | rest  | `background`                | `currentColor`, the line's colour below                                                                         |
| `root`, no `line`            | rest  | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                                                                            |
| `root`, `line='m1'`          | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.m1`                                                                                         |
| `root`, `line='m2'`          | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.m2`                                                                                         |
| `root`, `line='m3'`          | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.m3`                                                                                         |
| `root`, `line='m4'`          | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.m4`                                                                                         |
| `root`, `line='a'`           | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.a`                                                                                          |
| `root`, `line='b'`           | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.b`                                                                                          |
| `root`, `line='c'`           | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.c`                                                                                          |
| `root`, `line='e'`           | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.e`                                                                                          |
| `root`, `line='f'`           | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.f`                                                                                          |
| `root`, `line='h'`           | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.line.h`                                                                                          |
| `root`, `line='bus'`         | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.mode.bus`                                                                                        |
| `root`, `line='regional'`    | rest  | `color`                     | `color.transit.mode.regional`                                                                                   |

The light line colours, F (`#F5C200`), M2 (`#F0B400`) and bus (`#D99A00`), fall short of 3:1 on the light surfaces, and no token outlines them outside the map (`color.data-state.outline` is "Map only"). The marker keeps the exact line colour with no outline, as line badges keep their official pairs: it is decorative, the line and the stop are always named in words beside it, so 1.4.1 and 1.4.11 hold through the text.

## Keyboard and ARIA

No Base UI part, so nothing from Base UI here: the marker is decorative, never focusable, and hidden from assistive technology.

| Key  | Does                                                    | From   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | The marker takes no focus and no keys; Tab passes it by | Perron |

| Element | Role                               | Accessible name from                                                   | States announced |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | None: `aria-hidden="true"`, hidden | None: the stop's name, and the line's, are the caller's text beside it | None             |

StationIcon is always decorative: Perron sets `aria-hidden="true"` after the rest props so it wins over them (a `render` element's own props merge last, as [CR-3](#component-rules) says), with no accessible name and no label prop, as an icon next to text is ([Icons](../foundations/icons.md#style)). It always sits beside the stop's name, and the line is named in words nearby, so it adds nothing for the ear.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the marker tells the eye the line's colour and, filled, which stop matters; the caller's text beside it names the stop and the line, and a filled stop's meaning (such as "Next stop"), as [Do and don't](#do-and-dont) says
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here, the marker is not a region
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here, the marker owns no label
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: every `line` value, and none, in both variants and all three sizes, shown by the `Lines` story and the six variant stories
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here, nothing animates or collapses
- [ ] Native semantics first: a plain `<span>` with `aria-hidden="true"`, no role
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the marker is never focused, so focus passes it in reading order
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: none here, the marker is not a target; a caller that makes a stop pressable makes its whole row the target
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here, nothing moves

## Owned strings

No owned strings: the marker shows and announces no words, and the stop's and line's names come from the caller beside it.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root renders through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'span'`, so `render`, `className`, `style` and `ref` behave as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) and [Customising](README.md#customising) say, with no Base UI component underneath.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant` and `data-size`, defaults included, and `data-line` with the `line` value when one is given; with no `line`, `data-line` is absent and the neutral colour applies. CSS selects on these: `.pn-StationIcon[data-line='m1']`.
- **CR-3.** `aria-hidden="true"` is set after the rest props, so they cannot unhide the marker. A `render` element's own props are the caller's: `useRender` merges them last, as Base UI does, so a caller that swaps the element leaves `aria-hidden` and `data-*` off it. The marker never takes `tabIndex`, a role or an accessible name.
- **CR-4.** The marker's diameter is `--perron-icon-size`, which the root sets from `size` to its `icon.size.*` token, and the ring is `border.width.050` at every size, so it reads as the same mark beside caption, label and title text.
- **CR-5.** The ring and the filled dot are both drawn in `currentColor`, and the root sets `color` to the line's token, so one rule per line colours both variants.
- **CR-6.** Line colours stay exact: the marker never adjusts, tints or outlines them, as [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#line-colours) says.
- **CR-7.** In `(forced-colors: active)`, the ring is `CanvasText` and the filled dot's background is `CanvasText`, so filled and outlined stay apart when the system replaces colours ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks), "Forced colors").
- **CR-8.** The marker does not shrink in a flex row (`flex: none`), as an icon doesn't, so a long stop name wraps rather than squeezing it.

## Stories

No Penpot design yet, so the stories are named by the variant names the design will have: `variant`, then `size`, each in PascalCase (the Conventions of `penpot/README.md`). `line` is a colour, not a Penpot variant property, and the `Lines` story shows every value.

| Story            | Shows                                                                                                               | `play` test                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OutlinedSmall`  | `variant='outlined'`, `size='small'`, no line, beside a caption-sized stop name                                     | none                                                                                               |
| `OutlinedMedium` | `variant='outlined'`, `size='medium'`, no line, beside a label-sized stop name                                      | The root is `aria-hidden`, has no role or name, and Tab passes it by to the next focusable element |
| `OutlinedLarge`  | `variant='outlined'`, `size='large'`, no line, beside a panel-title stop name                                       | none                                                                                               |
| `FilledSmall`    | `variant='filled'`, `size='small'`, no line                                                                         | none                                                                                               |
| `FilledMedium`   | `variant='filled'`, `size='medium'`, no line                                                                        | none                                                                                               |
| `FilledLarge`    | `variant='filled'`, `size='large'`, no line                                                                         | none                                                                                               |
| `Lines`          | Every `line` value, and none, in both variants at `size='medium'`, each beside a stop's name with its line after it | Each marker carries its `data-line`, and none without a `line`                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                           | Don't                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Put the marker beside the stop's name, with the line named in words nearby, because the marker is hidden from screen readers | Use it alone, or as the only sign of which line serves a stop: colour is never alone ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)) |
| Leave `line` out for a station several lines serve, so the marker is neutral                                                 | Pick one of several lines' colours for a shared station, which tells the eye only one line stops there                                        |
| Use `filled` for the one stop that matters most in a list, such as the next stop, and say why in words beside it             | Fill several stops in one list, or use `filled` to mean a state the words don't say                                                           |
| Use a `LineBadge` to name a line                                                                                             | Use a StationIcon as a line's badge or swatch in a row of badges, where it reads as a stop                                                    |
| Pick the `size` that matches the text beside it: `small` for captions, `medium` for labels, `large` for panel titles         | Resize it with `className` or a raw width, which breaks the ring's weight against its icon-sized neighbours                                   |
| Make the whole row pressable when a stop opens something, at least `size.target-min` tall                                    | Make the marker itself a button or link: it is too small a target and has no name                                                             |

title: DataStatePanel
markdown:
# DataStatePanel

Holds a data view, such as a vehicle table or a day's chart, and shows the caller's content once its data is in, or in its place a calm message while the data loads, when there is none, or when it could not be loaded.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](../components/README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the spec of [EmptyState](../components/empty-state.md), the one entry in its `dependsOn`. The ROADMAP names it among the patterns (7.2) and the registry files it under Data, beside ReportStrip, VehicleTable and DayProfileChart, the views it is for. As a pattern it imports only Perron's components and parts, never `@base-ui/react`.

DataStatePanel is the wrapper that shows a data view's loading, empty and error messages in place of its content, built on EmptyState. The words "data state" elsewhere name the five Prik states, which PrikLegend explains, and its docs say once that its `status` is not a Prik data state.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Patterns/DataStatePanel`. Family: none, since it draws no surface and sits on the panel, sheet or card that holds it. Shared parts: none.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Base UI part                | Class                          | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` holding the `message` part and, once `status` is `'ready'`, the caller's `children`                                                                                                                | None: a `div`               | `pn-DataStatePanel`            | none            |
| `message`           | A `div` with `role="status"`, always rendered, so a change of status is announced: it holds the `emptyState` part while `status` is `'loading'`, `'empty'` or `'error'`, and nothing while it is `'ready'` | None: a `div`               | `pn-DataStatePanel-message`    | `message`       |
| `emptyState`        | Perron's [EmptyState](../components/empty-state.md), its title the status's owned string, with the caller's `description` and `action` under it in the empty and error statuses                            | None: Perron's `EmptyState` | `pn-DataStatePanel-emptyState` | `emptyState`    |

No part has a Base UI part: a pattern builds on Perron's components, never on `@base-ui/react` (the contract's [Patterns](../components/README.md#patterns)), and none of these parts has behaviour of its own for Base UI to give. The root and the message part are plain `div`s, and the `emptyState` part is the EmptyState component, which renders its own parts through `useRender`.

The message part stays mounted, `role="status"`, in every status, empty while `status` is `'ready'`, so screen readers announce each change, and the caller's `children` render beside it, not inside it. A live region added to the page with its text already in it is often not announced, and the caller's table or chart stays outside the live region, or every refresh of it would be read out.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI part: a pattern imports only Perron's components and parts, React and its own files (the contract's [Patterns](../components/README.md#patterns)), so it has no `render` prop and nothing inherited from Base UI. What it composes instead:

| Base UI part                | Renders                                      | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                        | Passed through                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| None: a `div` for root      | `div`                                        | `ref`, the class `pn-DataStatePanel`, `data-status` with `status`, the message part and then `children` when `status` is `'ready'`                                                 | `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props                              |
| None: a `div` for message   | `div`                                        | The class `pn-DataStatePanel-message`, `role="status"`, `tabIndex={-1}` (CR-6), the `emptyState` part as children unless `status` is `'ready'`                                     | `slotProps.message`                                                                      |
| None: Perron's `EmptyState` | EmptyState's `div`, with its own inner parts | The class `pn-DataStatePanel-emptyState`, `title` from the status's owned string, and in the empty and error statuses `description` as its `children` and `action` as its `action` | `slotProps.emptyState`: EmptyState's own props, such as `icon` and its `slotProps.title` |

Base UI already does: nothing here directly. EmptyState, through `useRender`, swaps its parts' elements on `render` and joins `className` strings, as its spec says.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                   | Type                                                       | Default      | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`               | `'ready' \| 'loading' \| 'empty' \| 'error'`               | `'ready'`    | none         | Where the data view's data stands: `ready` shows `children`; `loading` says "Loading" while there is no data yet; `empty` says the data came back with nothing in it; `error` says it could not be loaded. Not a Prik data state |
| `children`             | `ReactNode`                                                |              | none         | The data view itself, such as a table or a chart, shown only while `status` is `'ready'`                                                                                                                                         |
| `description`          | `ReactNode`                                                |              | none         | The sentence under the message in the empty and error statuses: why, and what to try. "Try again in a minute." Not shown while loading or ready                                                                                  |
| `action`               | `ReactNode`                                                |              | none         | What the person can do about it in the empty and error statuses, such as a button that loads the data again, below the sentence. Not shown while loading or ready                                                                |
| `loadingLabel`         | `string`                                                   | The locale's | none         | Overrides "Loading", the message while `status` is `'loading'`                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `noDataLabel`          | `string`                                                   | The locale's | none         | Overrides "No data to show", the message while `status` is `'empty'`. Give it what is missing when the caller knows: "No vehicles on line 5C right now"                                                                          |
| `loadFailedLabel`      | `string`                                                   | The locale's | none         | Overrides "Could not load the data", the message while `status` is `'error'`                                                                                                                                                     |
| `className`            | `string`                                                   |              | none         | Joined after `pn-DataStatePanel` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `style`                | `CSSProperties`                                            |              | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ref`                  | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                      |              | none         | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `slotProps.message`    | `ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>`                             |              | none         | Props for the `message` part                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `slotProps.emptyState` | `Omit<EmptyStateProps, 'title' \| 'children' \| 'action'>` |              | none         | Props for the `emptyState` part, the EmptyState: its `icon`, its `slotProps`, a `className`                                                                                                                                      |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, as the contract's Root section says. The root has no Base UI part, so there is no `render` and no prop inherited from Base UI.

`status` is optional, with the default `'ready'`, the first value, as the contract makes a variant's, so `<DataStatePanel>{table}</DataStatePanel>` renders the table and a caller adds `status` only while the data is not in. `status` is free in the contract's [Names from other libraries](../components/README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table, where `state` is not.
The caller gives the sentence and the action as `description` and `action`, shown in the empty and error statuses only, and anything else EmptyState takes, such as its `icon`, through `slotProps.emptyState`. `children` is the data view, so the sentence cannot be `children` as it is on EmptyState; `description` is the name of EmptyState's part for it, and `action` is EmptyState's own prop. Loading shows no sentence or action, since there is nothing yet to explain or act on.
DataStatePanel draws no icon of its own; the caller gives one through `slotProps.emptyState.icon`, such as `signal-off` in the error status. Perron's icons are inlined in the component that owns them, a pattern cannot borrow another's, and the icon is decorative, hidden from screen readers, with the title saying what it shows.

## Tokens

DataStatePanel sets no token of its own: the root and the message part have no fill, border, radius, padding or gap, so the panel takes the surface it sits on, and every message wears EmptyState's look, its tokens on [EmptyState](../components/empty-state.md#tokens). The root is a block that sizes to its container; the message part, empty while `status` is `'ready'`, takes no space.

All three messages, loading included, wear EmptyState's look unchanged, with no spinner, skeleton or animation, and the panel keeps no minimum height between statuses. The brand is calm and a loop needs a `duration.*` token no foundation gives a spinner; a skeleton would draw rows the data may not have, claiming more than it knows; and no `size.*` token gives a panel's height, so one goes through the `design-tokens` skill when a design asks for it.

## Keyboard and ARIA

DataStatePanel has no keys of its own. The action in the empty and error statuses, and the caller's content once ready, are reached in reading order.

| Key         | Does                                                                            | From        |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable element in the action, or in `children` once ready | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back out, to whatever came before the DataStatePanel                      | The browser |

| Element      | Role                                                                 | Accessible name from                                                | States announced                                                                                        |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`       | None (generic `div`)                                                 | None                                                                | None                                                                                                    |
| `message`    | `status`, a polite live region                                       | None: a status region needs none, and its text is what it announces | Its text whenever it changes: "Loading", the empty or error title with the sentence, nothing when ready |
| `emptyState` | EmptyState's: a paragraph title, the sentence, the caller's controls | Its title's text, from the status's owned string                    | None of its own                                                                                         |

The root takes no `aria-busy` while loading. Screen readers may hold back a busy element's live regions until it is no longer busy, which would silence "Loading", and nothing inside the root is half-built while it loads: the content is not rendered at all.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the message is the visible title, sentence and action, read in place and announced through the message part's `role="status"`; a caller's `icon` is `aria-hidden` inside EmptyState and the title says what it shows.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is not a landmark, and a `status` region takes no name.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `loadingLabel`, `noDataLabel` and `loadFailedLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children`, `description` and `action` each render a string, an element and an array; `description` and `action` land in EmptyState's `div` parts, so block content is valid in them.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; a status not shown is not rendered at all, so nothing hidden stays in the tree.
- [ ] Native semantics first: plain `div`s and EmptyState's `p` title; `role="status"` only on the message part, where no element says it; the action holds the caller's own `button` or `a href`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the message comes before the content in the DOM, the action after the sentence; when a change of status removes the element that had focus inside the message, focus moves to the message part (CR-6), never to the page's top.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: DataStatePanel has no target of its own; the action's targets are the caller's components, which keep their own sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

Each status but ready shows one string of its own as the EmptyState's title. `loading` is in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` already; `noData` and `loadFailed` are new keys, and agents write their Danish, Swedish and Norwegian.

| Key          | English                 | Override          | Seen or heard where                                                                        |
| ------------ | ----------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `loading`    | Loading                 | `loadingLabel`    | The `emptyState` part's title while `status` is `'loading'`, announced by the message part |
| `noData`     | No data to show         | `noDataLabel`     | The `emptyState` part's title while `status` is `'empty'`, announced by the message part   |
| `loadFailed` | Could not load the data | `loadFailedLabel` | The `emptyState` part's title while `status` is `'error'`, announced by the message part   |

The empty status's owned string is `noData`, "No data to show", with `noDataLabel` for the caller to name what is missing. It says only what the panel knows, that the data came back with nothing in it, without claiming why; a caller that knows says more through `noDataLabel` or `description`.
The error status's owned string is a new key, `loadFailed`, "Could not load the data", not "Data feed problems". "Data feed problems" is the fixed name of a kind of disruption on a line, which content design keeps for that alone; a panel whose request failed may have lost the network, not the feed, and "Could not load the data" says only what happened.

## Component rules

Rules for this pattern alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Exactly one of two things shows: the caller's `children` while `status` is `'ready'`, or the `emptyState` part in every other status. `children` is not rendered, not hidden, while loading, empty or in error, so a stale table is never read out beside a message.
- **CR-2.** The message part is always rendered, with `role="status"`, as the root's first child, and the caller's `children` come after it, outside it. While `status` is `'ready'` it holds nothing.
- **CR-3.** The `emptyState` part's `title` is the status's owned string, read with `useOwnedStrings({ loading: loadingLabel, noData: noDataLabel, loadFailed: loadFailedLabel })`. `description` becomes its `children` and `action` its `action` in the empty and error statuses only; while loading, it shows the title alone.
- **CR-4.** The root carries `data-status` with `status`, the default included, so CSS and tests can read it; the root sets no role, no `aria-busy` and no `tabindex`.
- **CR-5.** Each part's props are its `slotProps` value with the pattern's own laid over them, its own last: `className` strings joined, the part's class first, and `role`, `title`, `children` and `action` the pattern's. A pattern cannot import Base UI's `mergeProps`, so the merge is written in its own folder. `status`, `description`, `action`, the `*Label` props and `slotProps` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root.
- **CR-6.** The message part takes `tabIndex={-1}`. When `status` changes while focus is inside the message part, such as on a "Try again" button that sets `status` to `'loading'`, and the focused element is no longer in the document after the change, DataStatePanel moves focus to the message part. It moves focus only when focus has fallen to the page's body, so it never takes focus from an element that took it in the same change. It never moves focus otherwise: not on mount, and not into `children` when the data arrives.
- **CR-7.** It sizes to its container, with no width, height or minimum of its own; EmptyState wraps long words, so a long Danish stop name in `noDataLabel` fits a 320 px screen.
- **CR-8.** A `status` is not a Prik data state: DataStatePanel never shows the data-state words ("Live", "No signal"), and a view whose vehicles have gone silent is `'ready'`, its rows showing each vehicle's own state.

When a change of status removes the element that had focus inside the message, such as the "Try again" button once loading starts, focus moves to the message part, made focusable with `tabIndex={-1}` (CR-6). Otherwise focus falls to the page's top, and the contract asks that focus never be lost; the message part is where the person was, and it says what is happening now.

## Stories

One per variant the design would show, named by the `status` value in PascalCase, as `penpot/README.md` names variants, and `ErrorRetry`, which drives the error status's action from the caller's state. Each variant's story stays in its status, so the visual check pairs it with its export; the change of status, and focus with it, is `ErrorRetry`'s alone. Each story's data view is a short list of three departures as plain text; the empty and error stories give a sentence and an `outline` `neutral` Button.

| Story        | Shows                                                                                                                      | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Ready`      | `status` `'ready'`: the list of departures, and an empty message part                                                      | The list renders; the `status` region is empty and no `pn-EmptyState` element renders                                                                                                                |
| `Loading`    | `status` `'loading'`: the EmptyState with "Loading" alone, no sentence or action, and no list                              | The `status` region reads "Loading"; the list, the sentence and the action do not render                                                                                                             |
| `Empty`      | `status` `'empty'`: "No data to show", the sentence "Try another line, such as 5C." and the action "Clear filters"         | The `status` region holds the title and the sentence; Tab reaches "Clear filters" and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started                                                            |
| `Error`      | `status` `'error'`: "Could not load the data", the sentence "Try again in a minute." and the action "Try again"            | The `status` region holds the title and the sentence; Tab reaches "Try again" and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started                                                                |
| `ErrorRetry` | The error status, its "Try again" setting `status` to `'loading'` through the caller's state, as a data view's retry would | Tab to "Try again" and press Enter: the `status` region reads "Loading" and focus is on the message part (CR-6), not on the page's body; the message part is blurred, so focus ends where it started |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the pattern, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                | Don't                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Keep `status` `'ready'` while fresh data replaces data already shown, and use `'loading'` only while there is nothing to show yet | Flip to `'loading'` on every refresh: the table blinks out every few seconds and the status region reads "Loading" each time                                |
| Name what is missing through `noDataLabel` when the view knows: "No vehicles on line 5C right now"                                | Write "No data" when the view knows what kind: content design asks to say what is happening, plainly                                                        |
| Give the error status one neutral action that loads the data again, such as "Try again"                                           | Add a `brand` action when the panel already has one: a screen has one brand action at most                                                                  |
| Show a vehicle that has gone silent as `'ready'` content, with its Prik state and the words "No signal"                           | Use `'error'` or `'empty'` for a vehicle's data state: `status` is about the view's data request, and the data-state words have their own components        |
| Use plain EmptyState for a list that is empty for a reason the screen already knows, such as a search with no matches             | Wrap a list in DataStatePanel only to show an empty message: it is for views whose data loads, and its status region would announce a state nothing changed |
| Let the message part announce the change, and put the view's own live updates, if any, in the view                                | Add `role="status"` or `aria-live` to `children` or the root: the table's every refresh would be read out, on top of the message                            |

title: DetailHeader
markdown:
# DetailHeader

The top of the detail panel: it names what the panel shows, a line's vehicle by its line badge and destination or a stop by its marker and name, with a line under it and room for the panel's own controls.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](../components/README.md) and its Patterns section, the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the specs of the two components in `dependsOn`, [LineBadge](../components/line-badge.md) and [StationIcon](../components/station-icon.md). The extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it. DetailHeader is the first pattern, so it also sets how a pattern takes a line.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Patterns/DetailHeader`. Family: none, since it is content that sits on the detail panel's surface and draws no surface of its own. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`.

The drawing will have a `root` board holding four layers: `mark`, `title`, `subheader` and `action`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                              | Base UI part                                         | Class                       | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` laying the parts out in a three-column grid: mark, then title over subheader, then action                                                                                       | None: a pattern never imports Base UI; a plain `div` | `pn-DetailHeader`           | none            |
| `mark`              | A `div` holding a `large` LineBadge (variant `line`) or a `large` outlined StationIcon (variant `stop`), hidden from screen readers; rendered only when it has something to show (CR-3) | None: a plain `div` around a Perron component        | `pn-DetailHeader-mark`      | `mark`          |
| `title`             | An `h2` holding the caller's `title`: the destination, or the stop's name. In the `line` variant it starts with the line's name in a `VisuallyHidden` span (CR-4)                       | None: a plain `h2`                                   | `pn-DetailHeader-title`     | `title`         |
| `subheader`         | A `div` holding the caller's `subheader`: one supporting line, such as the next stop or the lines a stop has; rendered only when given                                                  | None: a plain `div`                                  | `pn-DetailHeader-subheader` | `subheader`     |
| `action`            | A `div` holding the caller's `action`, the panel's own controls such as "Show on map", at the end of the row; rendered only when given                                                  | None: a plain `div`                                  | `pn-DetailHeader-action`    | `action`        |

- DetailHeader has two variants, the Penpot `variant` property: `line` (a LineBadge and a destination, for a vehicle or a line), first and so the default, and `stop` (a StationIcon and a stop's name), so the drawing has one variant per kind of panel and the stories pair with them.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI part: `baseUiParts` is empty in `packages/perron/components.json`, and the contract's Patterns section forbids a pattern to import `@base-ui/react`, so every part is a plain element and the marks come from Perron's own components, `LineBadge` and `StationIcon`, and the `VisuallyHidden` shared part.

| Base UI part          | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                        | Passed through                                              |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| None, for `root`      | `div`   | The class `pn-DetailHeader` then the caller's, `data-variant` from `variant`, and the parts below as children                                                      | `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props |
| None, for `mark`      | `div`   | The class `pn-DetailHeader-mark`, `aria-hidden="true"`, and a `LineBadge` or `StationIcon` from `variant`, `line` and `lineName`                                   | `slotProps.mark`                                            |
| None, for `title`     | `h2`    | The class `pn-DetailHeader-title`, an `id` (the caller's from `slotProps.title`, or one from React's `useId`), and `title` as children, after the hidden line name | `slotProps.title`                                           |
| None, for `subheader` | `div`   | The class `pn-DetailHeader-subheader`, `subheader` as children                                                                                                     | `slotProps.subheader`                                       |
| None, for `action`    | `div`   | The class `pn-DetailHeader-action`, `action` as children                                                                                                           | `slotProps.action`                                          |

Base UI already does: nothing here. The behaviour the parts need comes from the browser (a heading, reading order) and from the composed components, which bring their own: LineBadge sets its line's fill and label colours, and StationIcon hides itself and sets its line's colour.

- DetailHeader has no `render`, on the root or in `slotProps`: a pattern can't import `useRender`, so the root is a `div` that never swaps and each `slotProps` value takes its part's HTML props only. ROADMAP 7.1's pattern contract is to say so for every pattern.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                  | Type                                                                                            | Default  | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`             | `'line' \| 'stop'`                                                                              | `'line'` | none         | What the panel shows: `line` heads a vehicle or a line with its line badge and destination; `stop` heads a stop or station with its marker and name. Set on the root as `data-variant`.                                |
| `line`                | `'m1' \| 'm2' \| 'm3' \| 'm4' \| 'a' \| 'b' \| 'c' \| 'e' \| 'f' \| 'h' \| 'bus' \| 'regional'` |          | none         | The line whose colours the mark takes, typed as LineBadge's and StationIcon's `line`. In `line`, the badge's colours, needed with `lineName`; in `stop`, the marker's colour, left out for a stop several lines serve. |
| `lineName`            | `ReactNode`                                                                                     |          | none         | The line's short name as riders know it, "5C", "M2" or "A": the badge's label in `line`, also read first in the title. Not used in `stop`.                                                                             |
| `title`               | `ReactNode`                                                                                     |          | none         | The panel's title: the destination in `line` ("Husum Torv"), the stop's name in `stop` ("Nørreport St."). Required. Replaces the HTML `title` attribute.                                                               |
| `subheader`           | `ReactNode`                                                                                     |          | none         | One supporting line under the title, such as "Next stop: Nørreport St." or the lines a stop has.                                                                                                                       |
| `action`              | `ReactNode`                                                                                     |          | none         | The panel's own controls at the end of the row, such as a "Show on map" button. The panel's close button is DetailPanel's, from the Sheet, and needs no place here.                                                    |
| `className`           | `string`                                                                                        |          | none         | Joined after `pn-DetailHeader` on the root                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `style`               | `CSSProperties`                                                                                 |          | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ref`                 | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                                                           |          | none         | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `slotProps.mark`      | `ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>`                                                                  |          | none         | Props for the `mark` part                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.title`     | `ComponentPropsWithRef<'h2'>`                                                                   |          | none         | Props for the `title` part. Its `id` is the one the panel's `aria-labelledby` points at.                                                                                                                               |
| `slotProps.subheader` | `ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>`                                                                  |          | none         | Props for the `subheader` part                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `slotProps.action`    | `ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>`                                                                  |          | none         | Props for the `action` part                                                                                                                                                                                            |

`className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, as the contract's [Root](../components/README.md#root) says. `title`, `children`, `variant`, `line`, `lineName`, `subheader`, `action` and `slotProps` are taken out of the rest props first, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element. The props type leaves out `children`: the header's words come through the named props. No `render` (see [Base UI parts](#base-ui-parts)), and no `*Label` prop, since DetailHeader owns no string.

- A pattern takes a line as two flat props: `line`, the id, typed exactly as LineBadge's and StationIcon's `line`, and `lineName`, the short name, the badge's children; not one `line` object such as `{ id, name }`. The id passes straight to LineBadge and StationIcon, and the patterns after this one (DepartureRow, DisruptionCard, VehicleTable) take the same two.
- The text props take MUI `CardHeader`'s names, `title`, `subheader` and `action`, as EmptyState took `title` and `action`, with no `children`.
- The panel's close button is not DetailHeader's and never comes in through `action`: DetailPanel puts DetailHeader in the Sheet's `title` slot, and the Sheet's own close button, `Drawer.Close`, follows it at the end of the header row (DetailPanel's CR-2), since a pattern can't import Base UI to render `Drawer.Close` into `action`. DetailHeader has no `onClose` prop and no "Close" owned string, so it needs no IconButton or CloseButton, owns no string, and Esc and focus return stay with the Sheet that owns the panel.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. DetailHeader has no interactive state of its own, so every row is rest; the controls in `action` keep their own states, and the marks their own tokens through their props.

| Part        | State                | Property              | Token                                                                                |
| ----------- | -------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mark`      | rest, `variant` line | `height`              | `size.badge-lg`, through LineBadge's `size='large'`, "the badge in a panel's header" |
| `mark`      | rest, `variant` stop | `--perron-icon-size`  | `icon.size.450`, through StationIcon's `size='large'`, "beside a panel title"        |
| `mark`      | rest                 | `margin-inline-end`   | `space.300`, the 12 px between parts of a detail panel                               |
| `title`     | rest                 | `font`                | `typography.heading-md`, the role for panel titles: a stop or a destination          |
| `title`     | rest                 | `letter-spacing`      | `typography.heading-md-tracking`, the role's twin                                    |
| `title`     | rest                 | `color`               | `color.text.primary`                                                                 |
| `subheader` | rest                 | `font`                | `typography.body-sm`, the role for the line under a title                            |
| `subheader` | rest                 | `letter-spacing`      | `typography.body-sm-tracking`, the role's twin                                       |
| `subheader` | rest                 | `color`               | `color.text.secondary`                                                               |
| `subheader` | rest                 | `margin-block-start`  | `space.100`                                                                          |
| `action`    | rest                 | `margin-inline-start` | `space.300`, the 12 px between parts of a detail panel                               |
| `action`    | rest                 | `column-gap`          | `space.200`, between two controls                                                    |

The root is a grid of three columns, `auto`, `minmax(0, 1fr)` and `auto`, with no gap between them: the mark in the first and the action in the last, and the title over the subheader in the middle. The mark's `margin-inline-end` and the action's `margin-inline-start` hold the `space.300` beside the text, so with no mark or no action its column is zero wide and the middle column takes their room. Its rows are `1fr`, `auto`, `auto` and `1fr`: the title and the subheader in the two `auto` rows, and the mark and the action spanning all four and centred in them, so the title and the subheader sit together in the middle of the mark's and the action's height, and with no subheader its row is zero high. The title resets the margins an `h2` brings; the mark, the subheader and the action keep only the margins above.

- DetailHeader draws no fill, border, padding or shadow of its own, taking the detail panel's surface and padding from DetailPanel: it is the top of a panel, not a card. `space.300` between mark, text and action is what Semantic spacing gives between parts of a detail panel, `space.100` from title to subheader matches EmptyState's title-to-sentence gap, and `space.200` sits between controls in the action.
- In the `stop` variant the marker is StationIcon's `outlined` variant, since the header names one stop and has no list to single it out from; `filled` is kept for the one stop that matters most in a list.

## Keyboard and ARIA

DetailHeader has no keys of its own and is never focusable. The controls in `action` follow the title in the DOM and on screen, so Tab reaches them in reading order.

| Key         | Does                                                              | From        |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable element in `action`, after the title | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back out of `action`, to whatever came before the header    | The browser |

| Element     | Role                                                              | Accessible name from                                                                            | States announced |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`      | None (generic `div`)                                              | None                                                                                            | None             |
| `mark`      | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"`                                      | None: the title says the line in words                                                          | None             |
| `title`     | Heading, level 2                                                  | Its text: in `line`, the hidden `lineName` then `title`, as "5C Husum Torv"; in `stop`, `title` | None             |
| `subheader` | None (generic `div`)                                              | None                                                                                            | None             |
| `action`    | None (generic `div`); the caller's controls carry their own roles | The caller's controls' own names                                                                | Theirs           |

- The title is always an `h2`, with an `id` the caller can set through `slotProps.title` (React's `useId` otherwise), so DetailPanel can name its Sheet with `aria-labelledby` pointing at it: the header heads one panel over a page whose own heading is the `h1`, and with no `render` a pattern can't swap the level.
- In the `line` variant the mark is `aria-hidden` and the title starts with `lineName` in a `VisuallyHidden` span and a space, so the heading, and the panel name taken from it, reads "5C Husum Torv" rather than "Husum Torv" with the badge read apart before it: a screen reader moving by headings, and the panel's name, then carry the line, and the badge is read once.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the badge's line name is read in the title (CR-4), and the StationIcon is decorative beside the stop's name, which the title says; the line's colour is never the only sign of the line.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here, the root is not a landmark; the title's `id` lets DetailPanel name its panel from the heading (CR-5).
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; DetailHeader owns no string.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title`, `lineName`, `subheader` and `action` each render a string, an element and a list alike; `subheader` and `action` are `div`s, so block content is valid there, and the title takes phrasing content as an `h2` does.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses. The `mark` is `aria-hidden` because the title repeats it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: an `h2` for the title, plain `div`s for the rest, and the caller's own `button` or `a href` in the action; no ARIA but `aria-hidden` on the mark.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the action follows the title and subheader in the DOM and on screen; DetailHeader never moves focus, and the Sheet around it returns focus on close.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: DetailHeader has no target of its own; the action's controls keep their own sizes, `size.control` for an icon button.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word DetailHeader shows or announces comes from the caller, through `lineName`, `title`, `subheader` and `action`, and the panel's close label belongs to the Sheet's close button, which DetailPanel sets after the header, not in `action`.

## Component rules

Rules for this pattern alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The pattern imports only `LineBadge`, `StationIcon`, the `VisuallyHidden` part, `PerronProvider` if it needs it, and React, as the contract's Patterns section says; never `@base-ui/react`. A type-only import is fine.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant`, the default `line` included.
- **CR-3.** The `mark` part renders only when it has a mark to hold: in `line`, when both `line` and `lineName` are given, holding `<LineBadge line={line} size="large">{lineName}</LineBadge>`; in `stop`, always, holding `<StationIcon variant="outlined" size="large" line={line} />`, neutral when `line` is left out. `subheader` renders only when `subheader` is given and `action` only when `action` is; a value that renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) counts as not given, so no empty cell takes up a gap.
- **CR-4.** In `line`, when the mark renders, the title starts with `lineName` and a space inside a `VisuallyHidden` span, and the mark carries `aria-hidden="true"` after the caller's `slotProps.mark` props, so the line is read once, in the heading. In `stop`, the mark is `aria-hidden` too, and StationIcon hides itself as well.
- **CR-5.** The title is always an `h2`. Its `id` is `slotProps.title.id` when given, else one from React's `useId`, so DetailPanel can point its Sheet's `aria-labelledby` at it.
- **CR-6.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value with the pattern's own laid over it: the class joins the part's own, such as `pn-DetailHeader-mark`, first, then the caller's, and `aria-hidden` on the mark and the children of every part are the pattern's.
- **CR-7.** DetailHeader sizes to its container, with no width of its own; the middle column is `minmax(0, 1fr)`, and the title and subheader wrap long words (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a long Danish name fits the panel at 320 px with the action beside it. The mark and the action never shrink.
- **CR-8.** No fill, border, radius, padding or shadow on any part: the header takes the detail panel's surface and padding. Colour sits on the title and subheader only.

## Stories

Stories are titled `Patterns/DetailHeader`. No Penpot design yet, so the variant stories are named by the variant names the design will have, the `variant` values in PascalCase (the Conventions of `penpot/README.md`). `Line` comes first and gives the contract story its args: every word in them is a string arg, and bus 5C is a line pair that meets 4.5:1, so axe's `color-contrast` rule stays on. Two more stories prove the action and the wrapping.

| Story        | Shows                                                                                                                                                         | `play` test                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Line`       | `variant` line, `line` bus, `lineName` "5C", `title` "Husum Torv", `subheader` "Next stop: Nørreport St.", no action                                          | The heading level 2 is named "5C Husum Torv"; the mark is `aria-hidden`; nothing in the header takes focus                                                 |
| `Stop`       | `variant` stop, no `line`, `title` "Nørreport St.", `subheader` "Metro, S-tog and buses", no action                                                           | The heading level 2 is named "Nørreport St."; the marker is neutral, with no `data-line`                                                                   |
| `WithAction` | `Line`'s args, with an outlined neutral Button "Show on map" in `action`                                                                                      | Tab reaches the button after the title, and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started                                                            |
| `LongTitle`  | `variant` stop, `line` m3, `title` "Københavns Hovedbanegård (Tietgensgade)", a `subheader` that wraps, and `WithAction`'s button, in a 320 px wide container | The title and the subheader each wrap onto more than one line inside the middle column and the button stays whole: the root is no wider than its container |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the pattern, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                   | Don't                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Give the destination as `title` and the line's short name as `lineName`: "Husum Torv" with "5C"      | Put the line in the title as well, "5C Husum Torv": the header already reads the line first, so it would be said twice                                            |
| Leave `line` off in `stop` for a station several lines serve, and name its lines in `subheader`      | Pick one line's colour for a shared station, which tells the eye only one line stops there                                                                        |
| Keep `subheader` to one plain line that says no more than the data knows: "Next stop: Nørreport St." | Put a list of departures or delays in `subheader`; they belong in the panel's body                                                                                |
| Put at most one of the panel's own controls in `action`, such as "Show on map"                       | Put a close button in `action`, which DetailPanel draws from the Sheet after the header; or add a `brand` action there when the panel already has its main action |
| Use one DetailHeader at the top of a detail panel, and name the panel from its title's `id`          | Use it to head a section inside a panel: its title is always an `h2`                                                                                              |
| Let the panel set the surface and padding around it                                                  | Give it a fill or a border with `className`; it would draw a card inside the panel                                                                                |

title: DetailPanel
markdown:
# DetailPanel

The panel that opens on the right of the map when a rider picks a vehicle or a stop: a Sheet headed by a DetailHeader, which names the line's vehicle or the stop, with the close button at the end of its header row and the caller's details below, and the bottom sheet it becomes on a phone.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](../components/README.md) and its Patterns section, the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the specs of the two entries in `dependsOn`, [Sheet](../components/sheet.md) and [DetailHeader](detail-header.md). The extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it. What the foundations already say of the detail panel is that it sits on the right ([Layout](../foundations/layout.md#page-shell)), is `size.detail-width` wide on a wide screen, stacks at `z-index.detail` ([Layout](../foundations/layout.md#stacking)), becomes a bottom sheet under `breakpoint.phone`, sets its parts `space.300` apart ([Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#space)), and closes on Esc after a dialog and before a highlight ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)).

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Patterns/DetailPanel`. Family: Panels, through [Sheet](../components/sheet.md), whose popup draws the Panels row's glass, border, `radius.xl` and `shadow.panel`; the pattern draws no surface of its own. Shared parts: `CloseButton`, through the Sheet's close button; the `VisuallyHidden` span DetailHeader composes stays inside it.

The drawing will have a `root` board, an instance of Sheet at `anchor` `right`, holding three layers: `header`, an instance of DetailHeader, with its `action` in a row of its own under the title and the subheader; `close`, the Sheet's close button after it in the same row; and `content`, the caller's body below.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Base UI part                                                                   | Class                     | `slotProps` key                           |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `root`              | The panel: Perron's Sheet, its popup the dialog that holds the header row and the content                                                                                                                     | None: a pattern never imports Base UI; Perron's Sheet, whose root is its popup | `pn-DetailPanel`          | none                                      |
| `trigger`           | The caller's button that opens the panel, when the caller gives one: the Sheet's `trigger`                                                                                                                    | None: the Sheet's `trigger` part                                               | none: the caller's        | `trigger`                                 |
| `portal`            | Moves the panel to the end of `<body>`, or to the caller's container; draws nothing: the Sheet's `portal`                                                                                                     | None: the Sheet's `portal` part                                                | none                      | `portal`                                  |
| `viewport`          | The fixed layer that places the panel against its edge, `size.panel-gap` in from the screen's edges, stacked at `z-index.detail`: the Sheet's `viewport`                                                      | None: the Sheet's `viewport` part                                              | `pn-DetailPanel-viewport` | `viewport`                                |
| `header`            | Perron's DetailHeader, the start of the header row: the line badge or stop marker, the `h2` title and the subheader, with the caller's `action` under them, in the Sheet's `title` slot rendered as a `div`   | None: Perron's DetailHeader, inside the Sheet's `title` part                   | `pn-DetailPanel-header`   | `header`                                  |
| `action`            | DetailHeader's `action` part, the caller's controls, in a row of its own under the mark, the title and the subheader, from the header's start edge, so the title keeps the row beside the close button (CR-2) | None: DetailHeader's `action` part                                             | `pn-DetailPanel-action`   | none: `slotProps.header.slotProps.action` |
| `close`             | The icon button that closes the panel, at the end of the header row, after the DetailHeader: the Sheet's `close`, the `CloseButton` part                                                                      | None: the Sheet's `close` part                                                 | `pn-DetailPanel-close`    | `close`                                   |
| `content`           | The caller's `children`, below the header row, laid out in a column; it scrolls on its own, so the header row stays in place: the Sheet's `content`                                                           | None: the Sheet's `content` part                                               | `pn-DetailPanel-content`  | `content`                                 |

- The DetailHeader goes in the Sheet's `title` slot, rendered as a `div` through the Sheet's `slotProps.title.render`, with the panel's `aria-labelledby` pointing at the DetailHeader's `h2`, and the Sheet's own close button stays at the end of the header row after it, not in DetailHeader's `action`. The Sheet always draws its header with `title` and its close button, and a pattern can't import Base UI to render `Drawer.Close` into DetailHeader's `action`, which DetailHeader's spec assumed; the `title` slot keeps the header in place while the body scrolls, where a DetailHeader at the top of `children` would scroll away and repeat the Sheet's heading. `Drawer.Title` is an `h2`, which can't hold DetailHeader's `div`s and `h2`, so it renders as a `div`, and Base UI's `aria-labelledby` would then name the dialog from the whole header, subheader and action included, so the panel passes its own, which Base UI merges last. DetailHeader's `action` keeps the caller's other controls, in a row of their own under the title and the subheader (CR-2). The build then rewrites what still says otherwise to say this: the Sheet's `title` description in Sheet's code and in its spec, "passes its name as `title` and the rest of its header in `children`"; and DetailHeader's spec, whose `action` part, `action` prop, close-button note, Owned strings and Do and don't (`docs/patterns/detail-header.md`, lines 19, 50, 63, 123 and 158) put the panel's close button in `action`, with the `action` JSDoc in `packages/perron/src/patterns/DetailHeader/DetailHeader.tsx` and a changeset line for it.
- The Sheet's `backdrop` is not one of the panel's parts: the panel is never modal (CR-4), so the Sheet renders none. The Sheet's `header` row and `title` part are the pattern's own, set by CR-2, and get no `slotProps` key.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI part: `baseUiParts` is empty in `packages/perron/components.json`, and the contract's Patterns section forbids a pattern to import `@base-ui/react`, so every part comes from Perron's Sheet, which brings Base UI's Drawer, and Perron's DetailHeader.

| Base UI part         | Renders                                          | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Passed through                                                                             |
