| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| None, for `root`     | Sheet's popup, a `<div>` with role `dialog`      | `anchor`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `trigger`, the snap point props and `closeLabel` given on to the Sheet; no `modal`, so the Sheet keeps its default, false (CR-4); `title` the DetailHeader; `children` the caller's; the class `pn-DetailPanel` then the caller's, joined after the Sheet's `pn-Sheet`; `data-variant` from `variant`; `aria-labelledby` the DetailHeader title's `id`; `ref`; the rest props first                                                                                   | `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props                                |
| None, for `trigger`  | The caller's element, as the Sheet's trigger     | Nothing: the Sheet sets its ARIA                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `slotProps.trigger`, given on as the Sheet's `slotProps.trigger`                           |
| None, for `portal`   | The Sheet's portal `<div>`                       | Nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `slotProps.portal`, given on as the Sheet's `slotProps.portal`: `container`, `keepMounted` |
| None, for `viewport` | The Sheet's viewport `<div>`                     | The class `pn-DetailPanel-viewport` then the caller's, joined after the Sheet's `pn-Sheet-viewport`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `slotProps.viewport`, given on as the Sheet's `slotProps.viewport`                         |
| None, for `header`   | DetailHeader's `div`, in the Sheet's title `div` | `variant`, `line`, `lineName`, `title`, `subheader` and `action`; the class `pn-DetailPanel-header` then the caller's, after DetailHeader's `pn-DetailHeader`; the class `pn-DetailPanel-action` then the caller's from `slotProps.header.slotProps.action`, after DetailHeader's `pn-DetailHeader-action`, and `data-anchor` from `anchor` on it (CR-5); its title's `id`, the caller's from `slotProps.header.slotProps.title.id` or one from React's `useId`; the Sheet's `slotProps.title` set to `{ render: <div /> }` | `slotProps.header`: DetailHeader's own props less the six the panel sets                   |
| None, for `close`    | The Sheet's close `<button>`, as `CloseButton`   | The class `pn-DetailPanel-close` then the caller's, joined after the Sheet's `pn-Sheet-close`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `slotProps.close`, given on as the Sheet's `slotProps.close`                               |
| None, for `content`  | The Sheet's content `<div>`                      | The class `pn-DetailPanel-content` then the caller's, joined after the Sheet's `pn-Sheet-content`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `slotProps.content`, given on as the Sheet's `slotProps.content`                           |

Base UI already does, through the Sheet: the `dialog` role, named here by the panel's own `aria-labelledby`, which Base UI's Drawer merges after its own (`DrawerPopup` takes the element props last), so it wins over the title `div`'s `id`; moving focus to the popup on open and back to the trigger or the element focused before on close; closing the topmost open sheet on Esc, so an open dialog closes before the panel; swipe to dismiss towards its edge; a bottom sheet's snap points; and the open and close slide. The Sheet adds, on top: the body's Tab stop while it scrolls, the non-modal panel that leaves the map usable, and the close button's owned label.

- DetailPanel has no `render`, on the root or in `slotProps`, as DetailHeader and KioskBar have none: the contract's `render` is Base UI's, inherited from a Base UI props type, which a pattern can't import, so `slotProps.header` leaves out the `render` DetailHeader doesn't have either, and the Sheet's parts' props are given on as they are.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

Set on the root as `data-variant`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

A controlled panel sets `open` to false here, and the screen clears its selection.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

`DetailPanelProps` extends the `div`'s props, `ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>`, less `title` and `children`, which it declares as its own, as DetailHeader's does: `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, the Sheet's popup, as the contract's [Root](../components/README.md#root) says. Every member above is taken out of the rest props first, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element. The types of the Sheet's props come from `SheetProps` and `DetailHeaderProps` by type-only imports, which the contract's Patterns section allows. No `variant` beyond DetailHeader's, no `color` or `size`: the panel has one look per anchor.

- The panel leaves out the Sheet's `modal`, so it is never modal: the detail panel sits beside the map while the rider pans and picks other vehicles, the Sheet's own Do and don't keeps a modal sheet for what is a Dialog, and the Sheet's default, false, is what the panel always passes.
- The panel leaves out the Sheet's `initialFocus`, `finalFocus` and `render`, which the Sheet inherits from `Drawer.Popup`, by extending the `div`'s props rather than `SheetProps`: Base UI's defaults are what the panel needs, focus to the popup on open and back to the trigger or the element focused before, such as the vehicle list's row, on close; a pattern takes no `render`; and a member can join later without a break, where taking one out is one.
- The panel takes a `slotProps` key for each of its parts but the root, `header`, `trigger`, `portal`, `viewport`, `close` and `content`, each given on to DetailHeader or to the Sheet's key of the same name, and none for the Sheet's `title` and `backdrop`, as KioskBar and DetailHeader give one per part, `slotProps.portal.container` is how a screen puts the panel in its own shell, and the Sheet's `title` is the panel's own (CR-2), and its `backdrop` never renders (CR-4).

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property the pattern sets itself. Everything else is drawn by the two entries it composes, and their rows hold: the root's glass, border, radius, shadow, slide and focus ring, the viewport's padding, the header row's padding and gap, the content's padding and font, and the close button's every state are [Sheet](../components/sheet.md#tokens)'s; the mark, title, subheader and action are [DetailHeader](detail-header.md#tokens)'s, all but the action's place, which the rows below move to a row of its own. The panel has no interactive state of its own, so every row is rest.

| Part       | State                 | Property              | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`     | rest, `anchor` right  | `inline-size`         | `size.detail-width`, at most `100%` of the viewport's box, as the Sheet keeps it. The pattern sets its own width on its root's class, leaving the Sheet's right sheet at `size.sheet-width`: the token is the detail panel's by its description and by Layout, and the Sheet's review (`components/sheet/review.md`, P3-2) left the choice open between the Sheet and this pattern; the pattern's class keeps the Sheet one width for every sheet that isn't a detail panel. |
| `root`     | rest, `anchor` bottom | `inline-size`         | The Sheet's `100%`, unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `viewport` | rest                  | `z-index`             | `z-index.detail`, over the Sheet's `z-index.dialog`, so the panel stacks above the overview sheet and the highlight chip and below the top bar, the tooltip and a dialog ([Layout](../foundations/layout.md#stacking)), as the Sheet's CR-5 asks of a pattern that lays a sheet among the map's panels                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `content`  | rest                  | `row-gap`             | `space.300`, between the caller's blocks, the gap Semantic spacing gives the parts of a detail panel, not none or `space.600`, the blocks of a pane: a vehicle's StopTimeline and FactList are parts of one panel, the Sheet sets its body the same `space.300` below the header row, and a caller who wants more between Sections sets it with `slotProps.content.className`.                                                                                               |
| `action`   | rest                  | `margin-block-start`  | `space.300`, the 12 px between parts of a detail panel, under the subheader, or under the title without one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `action`   | rest                  | `margin-inline-start` | `0`, no token: DetailHeader's `space.300` beside the text goes, since the row starts at the header's start edge, under the mark                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `action`   | rest                  | `row-gap`             | `space.200`, between two controls that wrap onto a second line, as DetailHeader's `column-gap` between them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

- The content is a grid of one column, `minmax(0, 1fr)`, its rows packed at the start with `row-gap` as above, so no child shrinks or stretches in the scrolling body and a long word never widens it; the Sheet's rules that take the outer margins off its first and last child still hold.
- With `anchor` `bottom`, the root is the Sheet's opaque bottom sheet, `color.surface.default` with no blur, since [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) keeps panels full of text off the moving map on phones; the pattern adds nothing to it.
- The header row is the Sheet's: `space.400` at the top and sides and `space.300` between the DetailHeader and the close button, the same 12 px DetailHeader keeps between its own parts, with the close button at the row's top, where the Sheet sets it for every sheet, its top level with the title's, so a title that wraps or an action row under it leaves it in the corner.
- The action is in DetailHeader's grid, in a fifth row of its own under the four that hold the mark, the title and the subheader, spanning all three columns, so the mark stays centred on the title and the subheader and the title's column runs to the close button. With the action in the row beside the title, the title's column was 108 px wide in a `size.detail-width` panel, and "Hovedbanegård" broke inside the word; under it, the title has the row's width less the mark, and a Danish name breaks between words at 320 px. The controls in it lay out in a row that wraps, so two that don't fit side by side never widen the panel.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Sheet and its Base UI Drawer. "From" says who does it: Base UI, the Sheet, or the pattern.

| Key                                         | Does                                                                                                                               | From                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`                            | On the trigger, opens the panel and moves focus to the popup                                                                       | Base UI                                               |
| `Tab`                                       | From the popup, moves to the controls in `action`, then to the close button, then to the body while it scrolls, in reading order   | The browser, in the DOM order the pattern sets (CR-2) |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`                          | Moves on out of the panel into the page; the panel stays open, since it is not modal                                               | Base UI, with the Sheet's `disablePointerDismissal`   |
| `Enter`, `Space`                            | On the close button, closes the panel with reason `close-press`, and focus returns to the trigger or to the element focused before | Base UI                                               |
| `Esc`                                       | Closes the panel with reason `escape-key` when it is the topmost open sheet, after any dialog above it, and focus returns as above | Base UI                                               |
| Arrows, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `Home`, `End` | Scroll the body while it has focus                                                                                                 | The Sheet, with `tabIndex` 0 while the body overflows |

| Element   | Role                                             | Accessible name from                                                                                                 | States announced                                                                 |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `trigger` | `button`                                         | The caller's element                                                                                                 | `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, with `aria-controls` naming the popup |
| `root`    | `dialog`                                         | The DetailHeader's `h2`, through the panel's `aria-labelledby`: "5C Husum Torv" in `line`, "Nørreport St." in `stop` | None: it is not modal, so the page stays in the accessibility tree               |
| `header`  | None (generic `div`, in the Sheet's title `div`) | None                                                                                                                 | None                                                                             |
| title     | `heading`, level 2, DetailHeader's               | Its text: in `line` the hidden `lineName` then `title`, in `stop` `title`                                            | None                                                                             |
| `close`   | `button`                                         | The owned `close` string, or `closeLabel`                                                                            | None                                                                             |
| `content` | None (generic `div`)                             | None                                                                                                                 | None                                                                             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the header's badge or marker is `aria-hidden` and its line is read in the title, which names the panel; the close button's icon is `aria-hidden` and the `CloseButton` part gives it the owned label; the body scrolls by keys and screen reader at every snap point, as the Sheet makes it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the dialog is named by DetailHeader's `h2` through `aria-labelledby` (CR-3), never by the whole header row, so the subheader and the action's names stay out of it.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `closeLabel`, given to the Sheet.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title`, `lineName`, `subheader`, `action` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike, in `line` and `stop`; the `Line` and `Stop` stories' `play` tests open the panel with each but `action`, and the `WithAction` story's with `action`.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; a closed panel is unmounted, or `hidden` when `slotProps.portal.keepMounted` keeps it, as the Sheet does.
- [ ] Native semantics first: the `h2` from DetailHeader, `<button>` for the close button and the trigger, and Base UI's `dialog` role on the root; the panel adds only `aria-labelledby`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the popup, then the header's action, under the title it acts on, then the close button, the last control of the header as the Sheet places it in every sheet, then the body; Base UI returns focus to the trigger or to the element focused before.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the close button, `size.control`; the action's controls keep their own sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the slide reads `duration.sheet`, which the tokens shorten to 0.01 ms.

## Owned strings

Every word the component shows or announces on its own. Reuse a key `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` already has; a new key gets its English here, and agents write the Danish, Swedish and Norwegian in the locale files.

| Key     | English | Override     | Seen or heard where                                                          |
| ------- | ------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close` | Close   | `closeLabel` | The Sheet's close button at the end of the header row, announced as its name |

Every other word comes from the caller, through `lineName`, `title`, `subheader`, `action` and `children`; the panel adds no key.

## Component rules

Rules for this pattern alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The pattern imports only `Sheet`, `DetailHeader`, their props types, the `classes` and `withClass` helpers from `packages/perron/src/internal/nodes.ts`, `PerronProvider` if it needs it, and React, as the contract's Patterns section and Shared helpers say; never `@base-ui/react`, its `mergeProps` included, so every class is joined with `classes`, or with `withClass` for a part of the Sheet's: the part's own first, then the caller's, whether the caller's `className` is a string or Base UI's function of the part's state, which `withClass` calls first.
- **CR-2.** The DetailHeader is the Sheet's `title`, and the Sheet's `slotProps.title` is `{ render: <div /> }`, so the header row is the DetailHeader, then the close button, in the DOM and on screen. The DetailHeader takes `variant`, `line`, `lineName`, `title`, `subheader` and `action`, over `slotProps.header`, and its `action` part takes the class `pn-DetailPanel-action`, which puts the action in a row of its own under the title and the subheader, so the title keeps the row beside the close button. The action stays DetailHeader's part, in the Sheet's title slot, so it stays in place while the body scrolls and comes before the close button in the DOM: Tab reaches the panel's own controls, then the close button last, as the Sheet places it.
- **CR-3.** The panel names its dialog from the DetailHeader's title: it passes the Sheet `aria-labelledby` set to the title's `id`, which it gives the DetailHeader through `slotProps.title.id`: the caller's `slotProps.header.slotProps.title.id` when given, else one from React's `useId`. Base UI's Drawer merges the popup's element props after its own, so this wins over the title `div`'s `id`.
- **CR-4.** The panel is never modal: it passes the Sheet no `modal`, so the Sheet keeps its default, false, with `disablePointerDismissal` and no backdrop, and the map stays usable beside it.
- **CR-5.** The root always carries `data-variant`, the default `line` included, and the Sheet's `data-anchor`. The root's class, `pn-DetailPanel`, sets its width with `anchor` `right`; the viewport's, `pn-DetailPanel-viewport`, sets `z-index.detail`; the action's, `pn-DetailPanel-action`, gives it its row; and the content's, `pn-DetailPanel-content`, lays out the body, by the rows of [Tokens](#tokens). The close button's, `pn-DetailPanel-close`, sets nothing, so the close button keeps the Sheet's place. The width, the `z-index` and the action's place each have a rule of the Sheet's or DetailHeader's for the same property to beat, `.pn-Sheet[data-anchor='right']`, `.pn-Sheet-viewport` and `.pn-DetailHeader-action`, so the pattern's selector is one class, then attributes, as the contract's Styling says, with one more attribute of the element than theirs: `.pn-DetailPanel[data-anchor='right'][data-variant]`, with the `data-variant` the root always carries; `.pn-DetailPanel-viewport[data-anchor]`, with the Sheet's `data-anchor` on its viewport; and `.pn-DetailPanel-action[data-anchor]`, with the `data-anchor` the panel gives the action through DetailHeader's `slotProps.action`, after the caller's props, set to `anchor` as the Sheet sets its viewport's. A `play` test proves the computed value or the box (see [Stories](#stories)). The content's grid has no Sheet rule for its property: the Sheet leaves the content's `display` as it is.
- **CR-6.** The pattern holds no media query for the phone, as the Sheet holds none: the screen picks `anchor` `bottom` under `breakpoint.phone`, and the snap point props reach the Sheet as given.
- **CR-7.** `onOpen`, `onClose` and `onSnapPointChange` are the Sheet's, given on unchanged, so the panel adapts no Base UI callback of its own.
- **CR-8.** The Sheet's portal renders nothing in static markup, so the contract's `OwnedStrings` story sees only the trigger. A `play` test runs `expectOwnedStrings` over the open panel's markup in `da`, with the story's `lineName`, `title`, `subheader` and body as the caller's words.
- **CR-9.** The `Line` story's args hold `defaultOpen: true`, so the contract story finds the root, the popup, with the `ref` and the `data-testid` on it.

## Stories

Stories are titled `Patterns/DetailPanel`. No Penpot design yet, so the variant stories are named by the variant names the design will have, the `variant` values in PascalCase (the Conventions of `penpot/README.md`), drawn at `anchor` `right`. `Line` is first alphabetically and gives the contract story its args: bus 5C to Husum Torv, the line pair DetailHeader's subject story uses, which meets 4.5:1, so axe's `color-contrast` rule stays on. Three more stories prove the action, the wrapping and the phone.

- The drawing has one variant property, `variant`, with `line` and `stop`, drawn at `anchor` `right`, and leaves the bottom sheet's look to Sheet's drawing, with the phone shown by the `OnPhone` story: the bottom sheet adds nothing of the panel's own, every story name after `Line` sorts after it, so `Line` stays the subject story, and a `Bottom` story would sort first and make the subject a bottom sheet.

| Story        | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Line`       | The subject story: `variant` line, `line` bus, `lineName` "5C", `title` "Husum Torv", `subheader` "Next stop: Nørreport St.", two paragraphs of body, a trigger button "Show bus 5C", open by `defaultOpen` | The dialog is named "5C Husum Torv" and holds one heading, level 2; the root carries `data-variant="line"` and is `size.detail-width` wide, and its viewport's `z-index` is `z-index.detail`'s; the open panel's markup holds only owned and caller words in `da` (CR-8); Esc closes it with reason `escape-key` and focus returns to the trigger; `title`, `lineName`, `subheader` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike |
| `Stop`       | `variant` stop, no `line`, `title` "Nørreport St.", `subheader` "Metro, S-tog and buses", a short body, a trigger button "Show Nørreport St.", open by `defaultOpen`                                        | The dialog is named "Nørreport St."; Tab from the popup reaches the close button, and Enter on it closes the panel with reason `close-press` and focus returns to the trigger; `title`, `subheader` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithAction` | `Line`'s args, with an outlined neutral Button "Show on map" in `action` and a subheader                                                                                                                    | Tab from the popup reaches "Show on map", then "Close", in that order, and Shift+Tab comes back; the action sits under the subheader from the header's start edge, the title's column runs to the header's end, beside the close button, and the close button's top is the header's; `action` shows a string, an element and a list alike                                                                                                     |
| `LongTitle`  | `variant` stop, `line` m3, `title` "Københavns Hovedbanegård (Tietgensgade)", a `subheader` that wraps, and `WithAction`'s button under them                                                                | The title and the subheader each wrap onto more than one line, the close button and the action stay whole inside the panel, the action under the subheader, and the root is no wider than `size.detail-width`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `OnPhone`    | `Line`'s args with `anchor` `bottom` and a body long enough to scroll, open at the `size.sheet-peek` snap point                                                                                             | The root carries `data-anchor="bottom"` and its viewport's `z-index` is `z-index.detail`'s; the header row stays in place while the body scrolls; Esc closes it with reason `escape-key` and focus returns to the trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the pattern, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open one detail panel at a time, controlled by `open`, for the vehicle or stop the rider picked, and clear the selection in `onClose`    | Stack a second detail panel over the first; pick the new vehicle into the open panel, so Esc still closes the topmost thing first |
| Give the destination as `title` and the line's short name as `lineName`: "Husum Torv" with "5C"                                          | Put the line in the title as well, "5C Husum Torv": the panel already reads the line first, so its name would say it twice        |
| Put at most one control of your own in `action`, such as "Show on map", and let the panel draw its close button                          | Put a close button of your own in `action`: the panel has one, at the end of the header row, which Esc and focus return go with   |
| Pick `anchor` `bottom` under `breakpoint.phone`, in the screen's code                                                                    | Expect the panel to turn into a bottom sheet on its own; it holds no media query                                                  |
| Compose the body from Perron's patterns and components, StopTimeline, FactList, Section and DisruptionCard, with their own `h3` headings | Put a heading of level 2 in the body: the panel's title is its `h2`, and a section inside it is an `h3`                           |
| Keep one primary action per panel                                                                                                        | Put a `brand` button in `action` and another in the body; a screen has one brand action at most                                   |

title: StopTimeline
markdown:
# StopTimeline

The stops of one vehicle's trip, in order, on a rail in its line's colour: each stop's name, its time and how late the vehicle runs there, with the stops already passed set back and the next stop marked, as in a vehicle's detail panel.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Patterns/StopTimeline`, not drawn yet: the design is deferred (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing. Family: none. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden.

StopTimeline is a pattern ([Patterns](../components/README.md#patterns)): it composes Perron's [StationIcon](../components/station-icon.md) for each stop's marker and [Delay](../components/delay.md) for each stop's delay, and takes a trip's stops as Mylder's domain data. It has no variant property: which stops are passed and which is next comes from the data, and `line` is a colour, not a variant. So the drawing has one variant, `Default`, a trip partway through. Its layers, top to bottom, are the parts below; `stop` repeats once per stop, holding that stop's `rail`, `marker`, `name`, `next` (the next stop only), `time` and `delay`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                           | Base UI part                                          | Class                               | `slotProps` key |

| `root`              | The whole timeline: an ordered list of the trip's stops, a grid whose columns the stops share                                                        | None: a pattern never imports Base UI; a plain `<ol>` | `pn-StopTimeline`                   | none            |

| `rail`              | The piece of the rail from this stop's marker to the next stop's, in the line's colour, or set back once passed; absent on the last stop. Decorative | None: a plain `<span>`, `aria-hidden="true"`          | `pn-StopTimeline-rail`              | none            |

## Base UI parts

No Base UI part: the registry gives StopTimeline no `baseUiParts`, and a pattern's code imports only Perron's components and parts, `PerronProvider`, React and its own files, never `@base-ui/react`, not even a type ([Patterns](../components/README.md#patterns); the `patterns` check). The root is a plain `<ol>` and the inner parts plain elements, StationIcon and Delay.

| Base UI part | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                                | Passed through                                                |
| ------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| None         | `<ol>`  | `className` (`pn-StopTimeline` first, then the caller's), `data-line`, `ref`, and the stops as its children (CR-1 to CR-4) | `className`, `style`, `ref` and the `<ol>`'s other attributes |

Base UI already does: nothing here. StationIcon and Delay bring their own Base UI underneath; StopTimeline adds layout, the rail and the words of a stop's place in the trip.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. StopTimeline takes no `children`: it writes its own stops from `stops`, so the props type leaves `children` out of the `<ol>`'s attributes. It has no `render`: the contract's `render` is Base UI's and inherited from a Base UI props type, which a pattern cannot import, and declaring it fails the `props` check. It has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and StopTimeline has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root. The `<ol>`'s other attributes, such as `aria-labelledby`, reach the root and get no row, as in MUI's tables.

Left out, the vehicle's place is unknown and no stop is passed or next. |

`stops` is an array of `StopTimelineStop`, a type the pattern exports beside `StopTimelineProps`:

| Field   | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`  | `string`         | The stop's name, as the operator writes it.                                                                                                                                 |
| `time`  | `string`         | Optional. The timetabled time at the stop, 24-hour `HH:MM`, such as `'08:14'`. Left out, the stop shows no time.                                                            |

A stop is a plain object with `name`, an optional `time` (`HH:MM`) and an optional `delay` in minutes (`number | null`, given to Delay's `minutes`), keyed in the list by its index, not a ReactNode name, a `Date` or an `id`: a trip's stops are data the pattern lays out, `HH:MM` is how content design writes a time, `delay` keeps Delay's minutes and its `null` for unknown, and a trip's stops never reorder, so the index is a stable key.

`line` is typed as StationIcon's `line`, through a type-only import of `StationIconProps['line']`, so the two never drift.

The vehicle's place is one number, `nextStopIndex`: the stops before it are passed, an index past the last stop means the trip is over, and none means the place is unknown. No stop carries a `passed` flag or a kind of its own, since one number can't describe two next stops or a passed stop after an upcoming one, and the name says which stop it points at without `value`, which the contract keeps for controls.

StopTimeline takes Delay's five label props, `minutesUnitLabel`, `minutesLateLabel`, `minutesEarlyLabel`, `onTimeLabel` and `delayUnknownLabel`, and gives them to every Delay it renders: the contract's checklist asks that every default label the pattern shows can be overridden on one instance, and the names stay Delay's, so a caller learns them once.

The stops the vehicle has passed are set back: their names and times in `color.text.secondary` and the rail behind them in `color.border.strong`, while the rail from the next stop on keeps the line's colour, and every marker keeps it too. It shows at a glance how far the trip has come without hiding what was passed (`color.text.secondary` still reaches 4.5:1 on every surface); the rail is decoration, so `color.border.strong` fits it; and StationIcon keeps line colours exact ([Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#line-colours)), so the markers are not recoloured.

## Keyboard and ARIA

No Base UI part, so nothing from Base UI here: the timeline is read, not operated. It takes no focus, and no key does anything.

| Key  | Does                                                        | From   |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | The timeline is not focusable or operable; Tab passes it by | Perron |

| Element             | Role                               | Accessible name from                                                                                   | States announced                       |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `root`              | `list`, from the native `<ol>`     | None of its own; the caller's `aria-labelledby`, such as the detail panel's heading, when it gives one | Its number of items, from the `<ol>`   |
| `stop`              | `listitem`, from the native `<li>` | Its text, read in order: the name, "Passed" or "Next stop", the time, the delay's words                | `aria-current="step"` on the next stop |
| `rail` and `marker` | hidden, `aria-hidden="true"`       | None: decorative; the words say what they show                                                         | None                                   |
| `next`              | text                               | The owned string "Next stop"                                                                           | None                                   |
| `passed`            | text, visually hidden              | The owned string "Passed"                                                                              | None                                   |
| `time`              | `time`, from the native `<time>`   | Its text, "08:14", with `dateTime` set to the same `HH:MM`                                             | None                                   |
| `delay`             | Delay's own: generic text          | Delay's own words: "3 min late", "On time", "Delay unknown"                                            | None                                   |

A next stop reads "Nørreport, Next stop, 08:14, 3 min late", and a passed one "Forum, Passed, 08:10, On time".

The next stop's list item carries `aria-current="step"` beside its "Next stop" words: it is the attribute ARIA gives for the current step in a sequence, so a screen reader names the stop as current when it lands on it from anywhere in the list, while the words say why.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the filled marker and the "Next stop" words say which stop is next, heard as "Next stop" and `aria-current="step"`; the set-back colour of a passed stop is heard as "Passed"; the rail and the line's colour are decoration, the line named in words by the panel around the timeline; each Delay says its delay in words; a stop with no `time` or `delay` shows and says nothing for it; with no `nextStopIndex`, nothing is set back or marked, and nothing is said
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is a list, not a region, and takes the caller's `aria-labelledby` when the panel names it
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `nextStopLabel` and `passedLabel`, and Delay's five, `minutesUnitLabel`, `minutesLateLabel`, `minutesEarlyLabel`, `onTimeLabel` and `delayUnknownLabel`
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: an empty `stops` renders an empty list; one stop renders with no rail; each stop with and without `time` and `delay`, and `delay` as a number and `null`; `nextStopIndex` left out, at the first stop, in the middle, at the last stop and past it, negative or not a whole number (CR-2); every `line` value and none; a long name wraps under itself
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses. The `rail` and `marker` are `aria-hidden` because they are decoration, not copies
- [ ] Native semantics first: `<ol>` and `<li>` for the ordered stops, `<time>` for each time, `aria-current` the one attribute ARIA adds
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the timeline takes no focus
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; the stops are not pressed (CR-8)
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves

## Owned strings

The stop names, times and delays are the caller's data; the words of a stop's place in the trip are the pattern's own, and Delay's words are Delay's, overridable here through the props above. Each word is a text run of its own, so `expectOwnedStrings` reads it as a dictionary value.

| Key            | English         | Override            | Seen or heard where                                                                           |
| -------------- | --------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nextStop`     | "Next stop"     | `nextStopLabel`     | `next`, seen under the next stop's name and read after it                                     |
| `passed`       | "Passed"        | `passedLabel`       | `passed`, heard after each passed stop's name; never seen                                     |
| `minutesUnit`  | "min"           | `minutesUnitLabel`  | Each `delay`, as Delay's spec gives it; an existing key in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` |
| `minutesLate`  | "min late"      | `minutesLateLabel`  | Each `delay`, as Delay's spec gives it; an existing key                                       |
| `minutesEarly` | "min early"     | `minutesEarlyLabel` | Each `delay`, as Delay's spec gives it; an existing key                                       |
| `onTime`       | "On time"       | `onTimeLabel`       | Each `delay`, as Delay's spec gives it; an existing key                                       |
| `delayUnknown` | "Delay unknown" | `delayUnknownLabel` | Each `delay`, as Delay's spec gives it; an existing key                                       |

`nextStop` and `passed` are new, each with a JSDoc line like its neighbours in `en.ts`, and agents write their Danish, Swedish and Norwegian. Neither is a data-state, delay or disruption word, so neither joins content design's table.

The next stop shows "Next stop" in words under its name, as well as its filled marker, and a passed stop says "Passed" to the ear only: StationIcon's spec asks that a filled stop's meaning be said in words beside it, and a sighted rider learns the filled marker from the words; a passed stop's set-back colour is plain to the eye in its place in the list, so "Passed" in every passed row would only crowd it, while the ear, which can't see the colour, hears it.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root is an `<ol>` with `className` `pn-StopTimeline` first, then the caller's, and `data-line` with the `line` value when one is given; with no `line`, `data-line` is absent and the rail is neutral. Each `rail` piece carries the same `data-line`, which its colour reads. The rest props are spread first, so the pattern's own class and data attribute win, and `stops`, `line`, `nextStopIndex` and every `*Label` prop are taken out of them, so none reaches the DOM.
- **CR-2.** Each stop's place comes from `nextStopIndex` alone: a stop before it is `passed`, the stop at it `next`, a stop after it `upcoming`, carried as `data-stop` on its `<li>` and on its `rail`, `name` and `time`, whose colours read it. An index at or past `stops.length` makes every stop `passed` and none `next`, a trip that is over. Left out, negative, or not a whole number, every stop is `upcoming`, with no `passed` or `next`, since the vehicle's place is unknown; `Infinity` is not a whole number, so it is unknown too, not past the last stop.
- **CR-3.** At most one stop is `next`. Its marker is `variant='filled'`, its `<li>` carries `aria-current="step"`, and its `next` part says the `nextStop` word under its name. Every other marker is `variant='outlined'`.
- **CR-4.** A `passed` stop says the `passed` word in the VisuallyHidden part, straight after its name, so it is heard before the time.
- **CR-5.** Every marker is a StationIcon with `size='small'` and the timeline's `line`, so its colour and the rail's agree. The pattern never restyles the marker: StationIcon keeps the line's colour exact and its ring's weight, and its `color.surface.raised` fill hides the rail behind it.
- **CR-6.** The rail runs through the centres of the markers, from the first stop's to the last's: each stop but the last holds the `rail` piece from its own marker to the next stop's. A piece leaving a `passed` stop is `color.border.strong`, so the piece the vehicle is on now, from the last passed stop to the next stop, is set back too; every other piece is the line's colour. One stop alone has no rail.
- **CR-7.** The stops share the root's columns through `subgrid`, so the times and the delays line up down the list, and a long name wraps within its column rather than pushing them. The marker sits beside the name's first line.
- **CR-8.** The stops are text: no stop is a link or a button, and the pattern shows every stop it is given. A caller that wants fewer stops, such as the next few, passes those.
- **CR-9.** Each `time` renders as `<time dateTime={time}>{time}</time>`, the `HH:MM` given, as content design writes a time. A stop without `time` renders no `time` part; a stop without `delay` renders no Delay; `delay={null}` renders Delay's unknown "—".
- **CR-10.** Every Delay gets the five Delay label props as StopTimeline was given them, so an override reaches every stop.
- **CR-11.** StopTimeline is not a live region. A screen that moves the vehicle on announces the new next stop in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) asks.
- **CR-12.** In `(forced-colors: active)`, the rail is `CanvasText` and a passed piece `GrayText`, so the trip's progress still shows when the system replaces colours; StationIcon keeps its own forced-colours rule.
- **CR-13.** StopTimeline composes the VisuallyHidden shared part, StationIcon and Delay from their folders in `packages/perron/src/`, and imports nothing from Base UI.

StopTimeline stays a plain list: every stop it is given is shown and none is pressable, with no "Show earlier stops" button folding the passed stops and no stop a link. The first version reads a trip; folding and links bring a button, its owned strings and focus rules that no screen has asked for yet, and each can join later as an optional prop without a break.

| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name the line in words around the timeline, such as in the panel's header with a LineBadge, because the rail's colour is decoration | Rely on the rail's colour to say which line runs the trip: colour is never alone ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)) |
| Leave `nextStopIndex` out when no real-time data places the vehicle, so no stop claims to be next                                   | Guess a next stop from the timetable and pass it: it claims more certainty than the data has ([Content design](../content-design.md))     |
| Pass `delay: null` for a stop whose delay no real-time data says, and leave `delay` out where no delay belongs                      | Pass `0` for an unknown delay: "On time" claims a certainty the data doesn't have                                                         |
| Give the timetabled `time` and let Delay say how late the vehicle runs                                                              | Pass the expected time as `time` as well as a delay: the rider adds the delay twice                                                       |
| Point the root's `aria-labelledby` at the panel heading that names the trip                                                         | Wrap the timeline in a live region: every update rereads the whole trip                                                                   |
| Pass only the stops the screen needs, such as the next few, when the trip is long                                                   | Restyle the markers or the rail's width through `className`, which breaks the ring's and the rail's matching weight                       |

# DisruptionCard A card for one disruption on Copenhagen's network: its kind, the lines it touches, a short title and a plain sentence on what is happening, set as a raised card in a list of disruptions or in a line's detail panel. ## Anatomy Penpot page `Patterns/DisruptionCard`, not drawn yet: the design is deferred (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing. Its sources are the [contract](../components/README.md), the foundations, the tokens and the specs of the components it composes: [SeverityLabel](../components/severity-label.md), [LineBadge](../components/line-badge.md), [Surface](../components/surface.md) and [Text](../components/text.md), the four its `dependsOn` lists once the build adds Surface and Text to the registry (CR-1). Family: none. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, which says "Affected lines" before the line badges (CR-4). DisruptionCard is a [pattern](../components/README.md#patterns): it builds only on Perron's components, takes Mylder's domain props, and imports nothing from `@base-ui/react`, so none of its parts is a Base UI part.
